## Argo for Packets
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-smart-routing/argo-for-packets/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-smart-routing/argo- — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-smart-routing/argo-for-packets/#on-this-page
- [definition] Argo for Packets — Last updated May 5, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-smart-routing/argo-for-packets/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-smart-routing/argo-for-packets/#argo-for-packets
- [concept] Argo for Packets optimizes IP layer network routing for Cloudflare network services products. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-smart-routing/argo-for-packets/
- [concept] It uses existing Layer 4 traffic data and network analytics to select the fastest, most available path between every Cloudflare data center and your origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-smart-routing/argo-for-packets/
- [fact] Argo for Packets supports Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN (formerly Magic WAN), and Cloudflare for Offices. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-smart-routing/argo-for-packets/
- [idea] Organizations with multiple origin locations benefit most from Argo for Packets because it optimizes complex Internet paths that would otherwise route suboptimally. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-smart-routing/argo-for-packets/
- [actionable] To begin using Argo for Packets, contact your account manager. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-smart-routing/argo-for-packets/

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optim — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/auto` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/#on-this-page
- [definition] Troubleshooting — Last updated Apr 16, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/#troubleshooting
- [definition] WordPress plugin is undetected on Cloudflare dashboard — The WordPress plugin may go undetected on your Cloudflare dashboard for a few reasons. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/#wordpress-plugin-is-undetected-on-cloudflare-dashboard
- [definition] WordPress returns stale content — If WordPress is returning stale content, [purge the cache](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/purge-cache/) when APO is enabled. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/#wordpress-returns-stale-content
- [problem] Versions older than 3.8.2 of the WordPress plugin may cause it to be undetected on the Cloudflare dashboard. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/
- [actionable] Install version 4.4.0 of the WordPress plugin to resolve detection issues with older versions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/
- [problem] Version 3.8.2 of the plugin may return stale responses if existing cache plugins do not include the `cf-edge-cache` header. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/
- [actionable] Enable APO from the WordPress plugin and purge the cache in existing cache plugins to resolve stale content issues. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/
- [problem] If WordPress runs on a subdomain but the plugin checks against the apex domain, detection may fail. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/
- [idea] Refer to the Subdomains and subdirectories reference page for additional information on domain configuration issues. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/
- [problem] If the Cloudflare dashboard cannot detect the WordPress plugin after troubleshooting, verify all steps in the Activate the Cloudflare WordPress plugin guide were completed. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/
- [fact] The Cloudflare APO WordPress plugin does not support multisite WordPress installations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/
- [problem] WordPress may return stale content even when APO is enabled. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/
- [actionable] Purge the cache when APO is enabled to resolve issues with WordPress returning stale content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optim — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/auto` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#on-this-page
- [definition] FAQs — Last updated Apr 16, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#faqs
- [definition] Do I still need to create "Edge Cache TTL" page rules with "Cache Level: Cache Everything"? — No, you do not need create Edge Cache TTL page rules. When the WordPress plugin is installed, APO automatically caches content for 30 days and invalidates on change within 30 seconds. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#do-i-still-need-to-create-edge-cache-ttl-page-rules-with-cache-level-cache-everything
- [definition] Does Origin Cache Control override APO? — No. APO ignores Origin Cache Control for caching on the Edge, but APO serves original Origin Cache Control to the client. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#does-origin-cache-control-override-apo
- [definition] Why are my browser cache control headers missing with APO? — The browser cache control headers may be missing with APO if you set your **Browser Cache TTL** to **Respect Existing Headers**. For example: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#why-are-my-browser-cache-control-headers-missing-with-apo
- [definition] Is the stale-if-error directive still needed with APO? — No, the `stale-if-error` directive is not needed because the feature is built into APO. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#is-the-stale-if-error-directive-still-needed-with-apo
- [definition] When I check the posts and homepage cache status, the response header shows `cf-cache-status: BYPASS`. Is APO working? — When Chrome DevTools is open, Chrome sends `Cache-Control: no-cache` by default. You can uncheck the **Disable cache (while DevTools is open)** setting and see that `cf-cache-status: HIT` and `cf-apo-via: cache` headers will be returned. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#when-i-check-the-posts-and-homepage-cache-status-the-response-header-shows-cf-cache-status-bypass-is-apo-working
- [definition] When I check `cf-cache-status` via cURL, `MISS` and `DYNAMIC` are always returned. In my browser, I see `HIT` but other tools return `DYNAMIC`. Is this expected behavior? — Yes, this is expected behavior because the requests must contain `accept: "text/html"`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#when-i-check-cf-cache-status-via-curl-miss-and-dynamic-are-always-returned-in-my-browser-i-see-hit-but-other-tools-return-dynamic-is-this-expected-behavior
- [definition] Are Google Fonts optimized when APO is activated? — Yes, Google Fonts are also optimized when APO is activated. You can confirm the optimization by checking the font URLs. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#are-google-fonts-optimized-when-apo-is-activated
- [definition] Can I customize query string caching with APO? — For more information on query parameters, see [Query parameters and cached responses](https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#can-i-customize-query-string-caching-with-apo
- [definition] Why are my font URLs not being transformed? — APO will skip URL font transformation when the `content-security-policy` response header is present but missing the values described below. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#why-are-my-font-urls-not-being-transformed
- [definition] Why do I see Worker subrequests in my zone logs when using APO? — APO uses Cloudflare Workers internally to optimize content delivery, which results in Worker subrequests. These subrequests may appear in your zone logs (for example, via Logpush). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#why-do-i-see-worker-subrequests-in-my-zone-logs-when-using-apo
- [definition] For the APO plugin why do I see: This plugin hasn’t been tested with the latest 3 major releases of WordPress. It may no longer be maintained or supported and may have compatibility issues when used with more recent versions of WordPress. — It is not uncommon for mature plugins to see no updates for longer periods than it takes to trigger the WordPress not tested warning. The warning is for notification purposes and is not an indication that a plugin no longer works. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/#for-the-apo-plugin-why-do-i-see-this-plugin-hasnt-been-tested-with-the-latest-3-major-releases-of-wordpress-it-may-no-longer-be-maintained-or-supported-and-may-have-compatibility-issues-when-used-with-more-recent-versions-of-wordpress
- [fact] When the WordPress plugin is installed, APO automatically caches content for 30 days and invalidates on change within 30 seconds. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [problem] Existing Edge Cache TTL page rules with 'Cache Level: Cache Everything' are not needed and may affect resources served by APO. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [concept] APO ignores Origin Cache Control for caching on the Edge but serves the original Origin Cache Control to the client. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [problem] Browser cache control headers may be missing if Browser Cache TTL is set to Respect Existing Headers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [fact] The `stale-if-error` directive is not needed with APO because the feature is built into APO. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [problem] Chrome DevTools sends `Cache-Control: no-cache` by default, causing `cf-cache-status: BYPASS` in response headers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [actionable] Uncheck the 'Disable cache (while DevTools is open)' setting to see `cf-cache-status: HIT` and `cf-apo-via: cache` headers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [fact] Requests must contain `accept: "text/html"` for APO to return HIT status; otherwise, tools may see MISS or DYNAMIC. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [concept] Google Fonts are optimized when APO is activated, changing URLs from `https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/...` to `https://example.com/fonts.gstatic.com/s/...`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [fact] For proxied fonts, the `cf-apo-via:proxy` header is returned when APO optimizes Google Fonts. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [problem] APO skips URL font transformation if the `content-security-policy` response header is present but missing required values. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [actionable] To fix font transformation issues, allow `unsafe-inline` on either the `style-src` or `default-src` directive in the CSP header. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [actionable] To fix font transformation issues, allow `self` on either the `font-src` or `default-src` directive in the CSP header. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/
- [concept] APO uses Cloudflare Workers internally to optimize content delivery, which results in Worker subrequests appearing in zone logs. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/troubleshooting/faq/

- [fact] The `ref` parameter is included in the allowlist of query parameters that permit APO to serve cached content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] Query parameters such as `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, and `utm_campaign` are explicitly allowed for caching by APO. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] Facebook tracking parameters including `fbclid`, `fb_action_ids`, `fb_action_types`, and `fb_source` are supported in the APO allowlist. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] Google Ads parameters like `gclid` and `dclid` are permitted query parameters for APO caching. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] The `_ga` parameter is recognized by APO as an allowed query parameter for serving cached responses. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] Mailchimp parameters `mc_cid` and `mc_eid` are included in the list of query parameters that do not bypass the cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] The `_ke` parameter is an allowed query parameter for APO caching purposes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] Query parameters `cn-reloaded`, `age-verified`, and `ao_noptimize` are supported by APO without triggering a cache bypass. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] The `usqp` parameter is included in the list of query parameters that allow APO to serve cached content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] Parameters `mkt_tok`, `epik`, and `ck_subscriber_id` are recognized by APO as allowed query parameters. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [problem] Cookies with prefixes such as `wp-`, `wordpress`, and `comment_` always bypass the cache in APO. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] WooCommerce session cookies starting with `woocommerce_` are configured to always bypass the cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [problem] Cookies prefixed with `xf_`, `edd_`, or `jetpack` will always cause APO to bypass the cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] YITH plugin cookies `yith_wcwl_session_` and `yith_wrvp_` are listed as prefixes that always bypass the cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [problem] Cookies with the `wpsc_` prefix or the `ecwid` cookie always bypass the APO cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [fact] The `ec_` prefix is a known cookie pattern that triggers an immediate cache bypass in APO. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [problem] Bookly plugin cookies, including those prefixed with `bookly_` or named `bookly`, always bypass the cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [actionable] To add a custom query parameter to the allowlist, create a post in the Cloudflare community for consideration. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/
- [concept] Query parameters are often used for marketing attribution, such as UTMs, making quick loading times critical for users. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/query-parameters/

- [problem] If you choose to run APO on a subdomain, the apex domain is automatically disabled. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/subdomain-subdirectories/

- [problem] Using Cache Rules to bypass APO disables all caching, including static assets for the excluded paths. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/subdomain-subdirectories/
- [idea] It is recommended to disable APO via the response header rather than Cache Rules when running APO only on a subdirectory. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/automatic-platform-optimization/reference/subdomain-subdirectories/

## Enable cache in an R2 bucket
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudf — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cach` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/#on-this-page
- [definition] Enable cache in an R2 bucket — Last updated May 7, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/#enable-cache-in-an-r2-bucket
- [definition] Tiered Cache — By default, Cloudflare caches R2 content at edge data centers (the data centers closest to visitors) based on [cache rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/cache-rules/). Each edge data center that gets a cache miss fetches content directly from R2. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/#tiered-cache
- [concept] By default, R2 buckets are private and require a Custom Domain to serve objects through Cloudflare's cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [fact] The development URL (r2.dev) does not support caching, WAF, or bot management. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [concept] Tiered Cache organizes data centers into a hierarchy so that edge misses check an upper-tier data center before fetching from R2. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [idea] Enable Smart Tiered Cache to automatically select the upper-tier data center with the lowest latency to your R2 bucket. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [problem] Files exceeding cacheable size limits are not cached by Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [fact] Free, Pro, and Business plans have a cacheable file size limit of 512 MB per file. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [fact] Enterprise plans default to a cacheable file size limit of 5 GB per file. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [problem] Cloudflare does not cache HTML and JSON files by default unless a Cache Rule is created with appropriate settings. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [problem] Connecting a Custom Domain makes the R2 bucket publicly accessible, requiring manual access controls to restrict requests. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [actionable] Go to R2 and select your bucket to begin setting up a Custom Domain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [actionable] On the bucket page, select Settings, then under Public access > Custom Domains, select Connect Domain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/
- [actionable] Enter the desired domain name and review the new DNS record before selecting Connect Domain to finalize the setup. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/r2/

## Control cache access with WAF and Snippets
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudf — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cach` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/#on-this-page
- [definition] Control cache access with WAF and Snippets — Last updated May 7, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/#control-cache-access-with-waf-and-snippets
- [definition] Presigned URLs — A presigned URL is a regular URL with a cryptographic token appended to it. The token contains a hash-based message authentication code (HMAC) computed from the URL path, a timestamp, and a secret key shared between the signing service and the validator. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/#presigned-urls
- [concept] WAF custom rules run before cache rules in the request pipeline, allowing invalid requests to be blocked before consuming cache resources. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/
- [fact] Presigned URLs are regular URLs with a cryptographic token appended that contains an HMAC computed from the URL path, a timestamp, and a shared secret key. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/
- [concept] A presigned URL token cannot be reused for a different URL path but allows anyone with the URL to access content until the token expires. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/
- [idea] For optimal performance, separate the creation and validation processes by using Snippets for HMAC creation and WAF custom rules for HMAC validation. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/
- [fact] The Workers implementation of signing requests is compatible with the WAF's is_timed_hmac_valid_v0() validation function. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/
- [actionable] You can implement presigned URL logic using a combination of Snippets, Rules, or Cloudflare Workers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/
- [fact] Presigned URLs enable sharing direct access to content with an associated timeout similar to AWS S3. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/
- [problem] When an R2 bucket is publicly accessible via a Custom Domain, anyone who knows the URL can access the content without restrictions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/waf-snippets/

## Customize cache behavior with Workers
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudf — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cach` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/#on-this-page
- [definition] Customize cache behavior with Workers — Last updated Jul 6, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/#customize-cache-behavior-with-workers
- [definition] Cache features in Workers — Workers offer two ways to interact with the cache. Use `fetch()` when your Worker makes subrequests to an origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/#cache-features-in-workers
- [concept] Workers run as middleware in the request lifecycle, handling both the request and response phases before or after cache checks. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [fact] When a request arrives, it hits the Worker before the cache is checked. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [concept] Workers Cache is a separate cache that sits in front of the Worker itself, allowing Cloudflare to return cached responses without running the Worker. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [problem] When using cache rules with Workers, the rule must match properties of the URL in the fetch() request, not the original visitor URL/host. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [idea] Use Snippets for lightweight modifications like header changes or redirects without deploying a full Worker script. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [fact] Snippets have stricter resource limits of 5 ms execution time and a 32 KB package size. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [problem] When using Workers with O2O (traffic routing through two Cloudflare zones), some caveats and limitations may apply. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [concept] Workers offer two ways to interact with the cache: using fetch() for subrequests to an origin or the Cache API for responses without a backend origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [fact] When a Worker calls fetch(), the request passes through Cloudflare's cache and Tiered Cache if enabled. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [actionable] Control caching behavior in fetch() by setting properties on the request's cf object, including TTL values, custom cache keys, and cache headers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [concept] The Cache API allows programmatically storing, retrieving, and deleting responses using caches.default or caches.open(). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [problem] Unlike fetch(), the Cache API only operates on the cache in the data center handling the current request and does not interact with Tiered Cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/
- [idea] Use the Cache API when you need to cache responses that did not come from an origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers/

## How Workers interact with Cache Rules
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudf — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cach` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/#on-this-page
- [parameter] request\_cf\_overrides\_cache\_rules (Fetch API): Enabled by default=Compatibility dates on or after 2025-04-02; Prerequisite=None — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/#compatibility-date-behavior
- [parameter] cache\_api\_compat\_flags: Enabled by default=Compatibility dates on or after 2025-04-19; Prerequisite=None — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/#compatibility-date-behavior
- [parameter] cache\_api\_request\_cf\_overrides\_cache\_rules (Cache API): Enabled by default=Compatibility dates on or after 2025-05-19; Prerequisite=Requires cache\_api\_compat\_flags — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/#compatibility-date-behavior
- [definition] How Workers interact with Cache Rules — Last updated May 7, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/#how-workers-interact-with-cache-rules
- [definition] Precedence order — Cache behavior is determined by the following order of precedence: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/#precedence-order
- [definition] Compatibility flags — The override behavior is controlled by [compatibility flags](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/compatibility-flags/) — configuration settings that opt your Worker into specific runtime behaviors. There are two flags because Workers have two ways to interact with the cache: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/#compatibility-flags
- [definition] Compatibility date behavior — A Worker's [compatibility date](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/compatibility-dates/) determines which flags are active by default. When you set a compatibility date, all flags with an enable date on or before that date are automatically turned on. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/#compatibility-date-behavior
- [definition] Example (Older compatibility date) — A Cache Rule bypasses cache for `example.com/foo`. A Worker with a compatibility date before `2025-04-02` sets `cacheEverything: true` via `fetch()`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/#example-older-compatibility-date
- [concept] When both Cache Rules and Workers are used on the same request, the Worker's cache settings take priority if required compatibility flags are enabled. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [fact] A Worker script can override Cache Rules behavior for domains proxied through Cloudflare or those that are not. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [fact] If a Cache Rule is configured to bypass cache for `example.com/foo` but the Worker sets `cacheEverything: true` in the `cf` object of a `fetch()` request, the Worker's setting takes precedence. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [concept] Cache behavior follows a specific order of precedence: Workers script settings, then Cache rules, then Page rules. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [fact] When multiple rules at the same level match the same request, the last matching rule wins for any conflicting settings. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [concept] The override behavior is controlled by compatibility flags which opt a Worker into specific runtime behaviors. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [fact] For the Fetch API using `fetch()` with `cf` properties, the required flag is `request_cf_overrides_cache_rules`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [fact] For the Cache API using `caches.default.put()` or `caches.default.match()`, the required flag is `cache_api_request_cf_overrides_cache_rules`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [problem] If the correct flag is not enabled for the API being used, the Worker's cache settings are silently ignored and Cache Rules apply instead. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [concept] A Worker's compatibility date determines which flags are active by default; flags with an enable date on or before that date are automatically turned on. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [problem] The Cache API requires `cache_api_compat_flags` to be enabled for any compatibility flags to take effect; without it, the Cache API ignores all compatibility flags. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [fact] If a Worker uses a compatibility date before the dates listed for specific flags, you must manually add the flags to your configuration. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [problem] A Worker with a compatibility date before `2025-04-02` setting `cacheEverything: true` via `fetch()` will not override a Cache Rule bypassing cache for `example.com/foo`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/
- [problem] If using the Cache API with a compatibility date before `2025-04-19`, manually adding `cache_api_request_cf_overrides_cache_rules` has no effect because `cache_api_compat_flags` is not active. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/interaction-cloudflare-products/workers-cache-rules/

- [concept] Cache Reserve is a large, persistent data store implemented on top of R2 that serves as the ultimate upper-tier cache to shield origins from unneeded egress fees. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [fact] This functionality is now offered as part of Cloudflare's origin server safeguard, Smart Shield. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [concept] Content freshness in Cache Reserve is determined by the Edge Cache TTL setting or the origin's Cache-Control headers if Edge Cache TTL is not set. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [fact] The default retention period for assets in Cache Reserve is 30 days, after which unrequested assets are removed. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [problem] Assets larger than standard CDN limits will not be stored in the standard cache and will incur Cache Reserve operations costs more frequently. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [fact] Cache Reserve does not support Origin Range requests at this time. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [problem] Vary for images is currently not compatible with Cache Reserve. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [fact] Cache Reserve makes requests for uncompressed content directly from the origin and does not include the Accept-Encoding: gzip header. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [problem] Cache Reserve is bypassed when using the Cloudflare O2O (Cloudflare for Platforms) setup. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [fact] Requests to R2 public buckets linked to a zone's domain will not use Cache Reserve; it only applies to requests not destined for the bucket. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [actionable] To enable Cache Reserve, go to the Cloudflare dashboard Cache Reserve page and select Enable storage sync. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [fact] Purge Everything performs a soft purge on Cache Reserve and does not update metadata set by Cache Response Rules such as cache tags. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [idea] Cache Reserve is designed for use with Tiered Cache enabled to achieve maximum origin shielding and avoid higher storage operation costs. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [fact] Class A operations are writes triggered by cache misses, while Class B operations are reads triggered when data is fetched from Cache Reserve to respond to an edge miss. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [fact] Asset purges initiated by URL request are free, but other purge methods like purge by tag or prefix force revalidation and incur storage costs until retention TTL expires. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [fact] The billable quantity for Cache Reserve usage is rounded up to the nearest million. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [concept] Storage billing uses gigabyte-month (GB-month), calculated by recording total bytes stored for the duration of the month. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/
- [fact] Assets larger than 1 GB incur more operations proportional to their size. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/

- [fact] The deletion of Cache Reserve data may take up to 24 hours to complete. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/cache-reserve/

- [definition] Unexpected behavior with WordPress admin pages — When a site or an application requires exact query string ordering, enabling Query String Sort might cause unexpected behavior. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/#unexpected-behavior-with-wordpress-admin-pages
- [definition] Identify the problem — The screenshot below shows an example where resources in the Media Library are not rendered correctly and the browser debugging console reveals that the page is throwing an error: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/#identify-the-problem
- [definition] Respond to the issue — Start by analyzing your site or application behavior around the use of query strings. Do you have assets served with multiple possible arrangements of query strings? — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/#respond-to-the-issue
- [concept] Query String Sort increases cache-hit rates by sorting query strings into a consistent order before checking the Cloudflare cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [fact] By default, Cloudflare treats resources as distinct if their URL query strings are in a different order. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [fact] When enabled, URLs with the same parameter names are sorted by parameter value, so `/example/file?word=alpha&word=beta` and `/example/file?word=beta&word=alpha` become identical. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [actionable] To enable Query String Sort, log into the Cloudflare dashboard, select your account and zone, go to Caching > Configuration, and switch the Enable Query String Sort toggle to On. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [problem] Enabling Query String Sort can cause unexpected behavior for sites requiring exact query string ordering, such as WordPress admin pages. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [problem] Symptoms of this issue include media not appearing in the Media Library, inability to customize via Appearance > Customize, and issues with widgets or menus. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [fact] WordPress concatenates JavaScript files using multiple `load[]` parameters where the order is crucial for functionality. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [fact] A patch implemented in WordPress since 2019 (Changeset 45456) addresses this issue, so recent versions may not experience it. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [problem] When Query String Sort is enabled, `load[]` parameters are sorted alphabetically (e.g., `equest` before `hoverIntent`), which can swap dependencies and break script loading. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [problem] Errors in the browser console, such as `_____ is not defined at load-scripts.php?c=0&load[]=...`, indicate that Query String Sort is breaking WordPress admin functionality. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [idea] Consider disabling Query String Sort for the site if the feature does not add value to any part of your application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [actionable] Use Cache Rules to enable Query String Sort (set Cache key > Sort query string: On) only for URLs where preserving parameter order is not important. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [actionable] Use Cache Rules to disable Query String Sort (set Cache key > Sort query string: Off) for URLs requiring specific parameter order, such as `/wp-admin/load-scripts.php`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/
- [fact] Cloudflare disables the Query String Sort option by default in the Caching app. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/query-string-sort/

- [actionable] To serve content based on visitor location, create a URL Rewrite Rule that checks if the Country field equals a specific value and rewrites the query to include a dynamic parameter like loc=ca. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/serve-tailored-content/
- [fact] Requests from Canada to /products/item transformed to /products/item?loc=ca create a distinct cache entry before reaching the origin or cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/serve-tailored-content/
- [problem] Without distinct URLs or cache keys, serving different content versions from a single URL can result in incorrect content being served to users. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/serve-tailored-content/
- [concept] Vary for Images tells Cloudflare which variants your origin supports so it can cache each version separately and serve the correct one without contacting the origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/serve-tailored-content/

- [concept] Snippets are self-contained JavaScript fetch handlers that run at the edge to programmatically interact with the cache without changing the user-facing URL. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/serve-tailored-content/

- [concept] Custom Cache Keys is an Enterprise-only feature providing a no-code interface to define which request properties are included in the cache key. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/serve-tailored-content/
- [actionable] To cache different content types at the same URL, create a rule that uses a custom cache key to include the Accept header value. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/advanced-configuration/serve-tailored-content/

- [definition] Only cache files that are truly static — Review the caching configuration for your origin web server and ensure you are caching files that are static and do not depend on user input in any way. - [definition] Do not trust data in HTTP headers — Attackers can exploit HTTP headers to inject malicious content into cached responses. For example, if your application reflects an untrusted header value in the response body, an attacker could use this to perform cross-site scripting (XSS) through the cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/#do-not-trust-data-in-http-headers
- [definition] Do not trust GET request bodies — Cloudflare caches contents of GET request bodies, but they are not included in the cache key. GET request bodies should be considered untrusted and should not modify the contents of a response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/#do-not-trust-get-request-bodies
- [definition] Monitor web security advisories — To keep informed about Internet security threats, Cloudflare recommends that you monitor web security advisories on a regular basis. Some of the more popular advisories include: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/#monitor-web-security-advisories
- [concept] A cache poisoning attack uses an HTTP request to trick an origin web server into responding with a harmful resource that shares the same cache key as a clean request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/
- [fact] Cloudflare relies on cache keys to compare new requests against cached resources to determine whether to serve from cache or request from the origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/
- [actionable] Review your origin web server's caching configuration to ensure you are only caching files that are truly static and do not depend on user input. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/
- [idea] Do not rely on values in HTTP headers if they are not part of your cache key. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/
- [problem] Attackers can exploit HTTP headers to inject malicious content into cached responses, potentially performing cross-site scripting (XSS) through the cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/
- [actionable] Do not include untrusted header values in your response body to reduce the risk of cache poisoning. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/
- [fact] Cloudflare caches contents of GET request bodies, but they are not included in the cache key. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/
- [problem] If a GET request body can change the contents of a response, it creates a vulnerability because the body is untrusted and not part of the cache key. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/
- [actionable] Consider bypassing cache or using a POST request if a GET body can change the contents of a response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/
- [idea] Monitor web security advisories regularly to keep informed about Internet security threats. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/avoid-web-poisoning/

## Cache Deception Armor
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/>

- [definition] Cache Deception Armor — Last updated May 6, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/#cache-deception-armor
- [definition] Web Cache Deception attacks — A Web Cache Deception attack tricks a user into visiting a URL that appears to point to a static asset but actually returns dynamic, personalized content from the origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/#web-cache-deception-attacks
- [definition] Cache Deception Armor protects against attacks — You can protect users from Web Cache Deception attacks by [creating a cache rule](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/#enable-cache-deception-armor). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/#cache-deception-armor-protects-against-attacks
- [definition] Enable Cache Deception Armor — To enable Cache Deception Armor, you need to start by creating a [cache rule](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/cache-rules/). Follow the steps below for guidance: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/#enable-cache-deception-armor
- [concept] A Web Cache Deception attack tricks a user into visiting a URL that appears to point to a static asset but actually returns dynamic, personalized content from the origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [fact] The attack works when an origin treats requests to non-existent paths as equivalent to a parent path, such as serving `/newsfeed/foo.jpg` with the same response as `/newsfeed`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [problem] Because the path ends in `.jpg`, Cloudflare caches the response by default, allowing an attacker to receive the cached copy of a user's personalized content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [concept] Cache Deception Armor protects users by verifying that a URL's extension matches the returned `Content-Type` header. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [fact] When a mismatch is found between the URL extension and the `Content-Type`, Cloudflare does not cache the response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [idea] You can protect users from Web Cache Deception attacks by creating a cache rule that enables Cache deception armor. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [fact] If the returned `Content-Type` is `application/octet-stream`, the extension does not matter because it signals the browser to save the asset instead of displaying it. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [fact] Cloudflare allows `.jpg` to be served as `image/webp` or `.gif` as `video/webm` without triggering protection, as these are unlikely to be attacks. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [problem] Cache Deception Armor depends upon Origin Cache Control, meaning a `Cache-Control` header from the origin or an Edge Cache TTL Cache Rule may override the protection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [actionable] To enable Cache Deception Armor, go to the Cloudflare dashboard and navigate to the **Cache Rules** page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [actionable] Select **Create rule**, define a [rule expression](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ruleset-engine/rules-language/expressions/edit-expressions/#expression-builder) under **When incoming requests match**, and select **Eligible for cache** in the **Cache eligibility** section. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/
- [actionable] Add the **Cache Key** setting to the rule and turn on **Cache deception armor** before selecting **Deploy** or **Save as Draft**. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/cache-security/cache-deception-armor/

## Head Requests and Set-Cookie Headers
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-beh — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cach` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/#on-this-page
- [definition] Head Requests and Set-Cookie Headers — Last updated May 6, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/#head-requests-and-set-cookie-headers
- [definition] Interaction of `HEAD` requests with Cache — Cloudflare converts `HEAD` requests to `GET` requests for [cacheable requests](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/#default-cached-file-extensions). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/#interaction-of-head-requests-with-cache
- [definition] Interaction of `Set-Cookie` response header with Cache — For non-cacheable requests, `Set-Cookie` is always preserved. For cacheable requests, there are three possible behaviors: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/#interaction-of-set-cookie-response-header-with-cache
- [concept] Cloudflare converts HEAD requests to GET requests for cacheable resources. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/
- [fact] When a HEAD request results in a cache miss, Cloudflare sends a GET request to the origin, caches the full response, and returns only the response headers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/
- [problem] If the origin server is not configured to handle GET requests, compatibility issues may arise since Cloudflare converts HEAD to GET. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/
- [fact] For non-cacheable requests, the Set-Cookie header is always preserved by Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/
- [concept] When origin cache control is disabled and a Set-Cookie header is present, Cloudflare removes the header and caches the asset using the default cache level. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/
- [fact] If origin cache control is enabled and a Set-Cookie header is returned, Cloudflare does not cache the asset, preserves the header, and returns a BYPASS cache status. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/
- [fact] When using Cache Everything or Eligible for cache settings with a Set-Cookie header, Cloudflare preserves the header but does not cache the asset, resulting in a MISS status. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/
- [fact] If Cache Everything or Eligible for cache is used with an explicit edge cache TTL, Cloudflare removes the Set-Cookie header and caches the asset. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/
- [idea] Ensure your origin server handles GET requests to maintain compatibility with Cloudflare's conversion of HEAD requests. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-behavior/

- [definition] STALE — The resource was served from Cloudflare's cache but was expired. Cloudflare could not contact the origin web server to retrieve an updated resource. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-responses/#stale
- [definition] BYPASS — Cloudflare considered the asset eligible for cache at request time — either because it matches the [default cached file extensions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/#default-cached-file-extensions), or because a [Cache… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-responses/#bypass
- [definition] REVALIDATED — The origin confirmed the cached resource was unchanged via a conditional request (`If-Modified-Since` or `If-None-Match`), and the response is served from Cloudflare's cache. This status reflects the synchronous validation path — the request waits for the origin to respond before being served. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-responses/#revalidated
- [definition] UPDATING — The resource was expired but served from Cloudflare's cache while the origin updates it in the background. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-responses/#updating
- [definition] DYNAMIC — Cloudflare determined at request time that the asset is not eligible for cache, so the request went to the origin web server without a cache lookup. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-responses/#dynamic

- [fact] Cloudflare caches a website's robots.txt file by default. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [problem] Origin Cache Control is enabled for Enterprise customers to strictly respect Cache-Control directives, while Free, Pro, and Business customers have it enabled by default. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [concept] Clients can use the Range header to send range requests served from the cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [fact] If an origin response includes a Content-Length header, Cloudflare returns the specified byte range with an HTTP 206 response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [fact] If an origin response lacks a Content-Length header, Cloudflare returns the full content with an HTTP 200 response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [concept] Request collapsing uses a cache lock to prevent duplicate origin requests when multiple simultaneous requests miss the cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [fact] During request collapsing, only the first request is forwarded to the origin while others wait for completion. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [idea] To cache additional content types beyond defaults, create a Cache Rule to cache everything. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [fact] Free, Pro, and Business customers have a maximum cacheable file size limit of 512 MB. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [fact] Enterprise customers have a default maximum cacheable file size of 5 GB. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [problem] Cloudflare will not start caching content if a visitor disconnects before the origin responds to Cloudflare's request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [fact] If Cloudflare has already started fetching content from the origin, it will complete the retrieval and cache the entire content even if the visitor disconnects. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [actionable] Customers can reduce the Maximum Upload Size from the zone's Network page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [idea] For larger uploads, group requests into smaller chunks or use a DNS-only (unproxied) DNS record. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/
- [actionable] To increase cacheable file size limits beyond defaults, contact your account team or upgrade your plan. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/

## Retention vs Freshness (TTL)
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cach` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/#on-this-page
- [definition] Retention vs Freshness (TTL) — Last updated May 6, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/#retention-vs-freshness-ttl
- [definition] Retention — When a resource is requested, Cloudflare caches it so that subsequent requests can be served without contacting the origin server. If a cached object is not requested again, it is eventually removed to make room for newer, more popular content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/#retention
- [definition] Freshness (TTL) — Freshness, also known as Time to Live (TTL), determines how long a cache can use an object without checking with the origin again. For example, if an object has a TTL of five minutes, the cache serves it directly for five minutes after first receiving it. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/#freshness-ttl
- [concept] Freshness (TTL) determines how long a cache can use an object without checking with the origin again. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/
- [concept] Retention refers to how long an object stays in cache before being removed via eviction. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/
- [fact] Cloudflare uses a Least Recently Used (LRU) algorithm to decide which objects to evict when the cache is full. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/
- [fact] Retention is determined by the object's relative popularity and the size of the cache, and is not configurable. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/
- [fact] If an object has a TTL of five minutes, the cache serves it directly for five minutes after first receiving it. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/
- [actionable] Configure TTLs by including Origin Cache Control or CDN Cache Control directives like `max-age` or `s-maxage` in the origin cache-control response header. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/
- [actionable] Configure TTLs using Cache Rules or Workers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/
- [concept] When an object is no longer fresh, Cloudflare revalidates it with the origin to confirm validity. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/
- [fact] When `stale-while-revalidate` is set, revalidation happens asynchronously at expiry so visitors continue to be served from cache while a fresh copy is fetched in the background. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/
- [problem] Without the `stale-while-revalidate` directive, incoming requests wait for the origin to respond before receiving content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/
- [fact] During revalidation, the origin can either confirm the cached object is still valid (refreshing its TTL) or return a new version to replace it. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/retention-vs-freshness/

## Revalidation
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/>

- [definition] Stale-while-revalidate — When a cached asset expires, Cloudflare uses the [stale-while-revalidate](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-control/#revalidation) directive in `Cache-Control` to determine whether it can continue serving the stale asset while fetching a fresh copy from the origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/#stale-while-revalidate
- [definition] Asynchronous revalidation — Revalidation is fully asynchronous. When a cached asset expires and `stale-while-revalidate` is set, the first request that arrives after expiry triggers revalidation in the background. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/#asynchronous-revalidation
- [definition] Controlling stale behavior — Cloudflare only serves stale content during revalidation if your origin includes the `stale-while-revalidate` directive in its `Cache-Control` header. Without this directive, visitors wait for the origin to respond before receiving content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/#controlling-stale-behavior
- [definition] Directives that disable stale-while-revalidate — When [Origin Cache Control](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-control/#enable-origin-cache-control) is enabled, the following `Cache-Control` directives prevent Cloudflare from serving stale content, per [RFC 9111 §4.2.4… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/#directives-that-disable-stale-while-revalidate
- [definition] Smart revalidation towards users — When both [Last-Modified ↗](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7232?cf%5Fhistory%5Fstate=%7B%22guid%22%3A%22C255D9FF78CD46CDA4F76812EA68C350%22%2C%22historyId%22%3A15%2C%22targetId%22%3A%226C8153BAEF7BC0C5A331E28F8BCF1ABA%22%7D#section-2.2) and [Etag… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/#smart-revalidation-towards-users
- [concept] Cloudflare uses the stale-while-revalidate directive in Cache-Control to serve expired content while fetching a fresh copy from the origin in the background. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [fact] If stale-while-revalidate is present and the asset is within the allowed staleness window, Cloudflare serves expired content to visitors. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [concept] Cloudflare validates content without fully re-fetching it by using headers like If-Modified-Since and ETag, which reduces origin traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [fact] Revalidation is fully asynchronous; the first request after expiry triggers revalidation in the background. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [concept] When revalidation is triggered, the immediate request receives stale content with an UPDATING status instead of blocking until the origin responds. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [fact] All following requests also receive stale content with an UPDATING status until the origin responds and revalidation completes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [concept] Once revalidation completes, subsequent requests receive fresh content with a HIT status. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [fact] If the stale content is still valid, Cloudflare sets a new TTL; if it has changed, the origin provides fresh content to replace the old. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [problem] Without the stale-while-revalidate directive in the origin's Cache-Control header, visitors must wait for the origin to respond before receiving content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [actionable] You can disable stale serving by using the Serve stale content while revalidating setting in Cache Rules to override an origin's directive. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [problem] When Origin Cache Control is enabled, directives like must-revalidate, proxy-revalidate, s-maxage, and no-cache prevent Cloudflare from serving stale content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [fact] If any disabling directives are present alongside stale-while-revalidate, requests return EXPIRED instead of UPDATING. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [idea] To use stale-while-revalidate with different TTLs for Cloudflare and browsers, do not use s-maxage; instead configure max-age with stale-while-revalidate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [actionable] Use Edge Cache TTL in Cache Rules to set a separate TTL for Cloudflare when configuring max-age with stale-while-revalidate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [concept] Smart Edge Revalidation uses the time the object was cached on Cloudflare's global network as the Last-Modified header value when origin headers are absent. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
- [fact] When browser revalidation requests use If-Modified-Since or If-None-Match, Cloudflare's global network answers using the generated Last-Modified header. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/revalidation/
