- [definition] How Vary affects cache keys — When Cloudflare caches a response with a `Vary` header, the listed request headers become part of the cache key for that response, following the HTTP caching behavior described in [RFC 9111 ↗](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html#name-calculating-cache-keys-with). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#how-vary-affects-cache-keys
- [definition] Actions — Each configured header uses one of three actions: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#actions
- [definition] Normalize — `normalize` reduces unnecessary cached versions by converting equivalent request header values into the same cache key value. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#normalize
- [definition] Passthrough — `passthrough` uses the raw request header value when selecting a cached version. Semantically equivalent values can still create different cached versions if the bytes differ. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#passthrough
- [definition] Bypass — `bypass` tells Cloudflare not to cache a response when the origin's `Vary` response includes that header name. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#bypass
- [definition] Normalization behavior — Vary normalization is the normalization performed when the configured action is `normalize`. It affects how Cloudflare selects a cached version and, for some headers, what Cloudflare forwards to the origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#normalization-behavior
- [definition] Origin request headers — For `Accept`, `Accept-Language`, and `Accept-Encoding` with [Respect Strong ETags](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/cache-rules/settings/#respect-strong-etags) enabled, Cloudflare may also forward the normalized header value to the origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#origin-request-headers
- [definition] Accept — Cloudflare normalizes the `Accept` request header in the following steps: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#accept
- [definition] Accept-Language — Cloudflare normalizes the `Accept-Language` request header in the following steps: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#accept-language
- [definition] Accept-Encoding — By default, Cloudflare's CDN overrides the `Accept-Encoding` header based on the enabled compression encodings. If Brotli compression is enabled, the `Accept-Encoding` forwarded to the origin is `gzip, br`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#accept-encoding
- [definition] Other headers — For any header other than `Accept`, `Accept-Language`, and `Accept-Encoding`, Cloudflare does not know the field's semantics. Normalization is restricted to transformations that are safe for any header: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#other-headers
- [definition] Purge behavior — Purging a URL purges all cached versions for that URL. You do not need to send a separate [purge](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/purge-cache/) request for each `Vary` header value. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#purge-behavior
- [concept] The Vary HTTP response header tells Cloudflare that an origin can serve different responses for the same URL depending on request headers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] A response containing Vary: * always bypasses cache, regardless of your Vary configuration. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [concept] When Cloudflare caches a response with a Vary header, the listed request headers become part of the cache key for that response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] Cloudflare does not vary every cached response just because Vary is configured in a Cache Rule; the origin response must include a Vary header. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] If the origin response includes a Vary header name configured to bypass cache, Cloudflare does not store that response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [concept] The normalize action reduces unnecessary cached versions by converting equivalent request header values into the same cache key value. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] Under passthrough, semantically equivalent values can create different cached versions if the bytes differ. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [idea] Use passthrough only when the exact header value matters to your origin and should matter to the cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] Normalization is optional but recommended for most deployments because it reduces the number of cached versions and improves cache hit ratio. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [concept] For Accept, Accept-Language, and Accept-Encoding with Respect Strong ETags enabled, Cloudflare may forward the normalized header value to the origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] The origin request rewrite applies only to Accept, Accept-Language, and Accept-Encoding headers configured with normalize. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] If normalization reduces a header to an empty value, Cloudflare removes that header from the origin request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [concept] Cloudflare normalizes the Accept request header by converting MIME types to lowercase, stripping whitespace, sorting by quality value, and stripping parameters. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] For Accept normalization, q=0 is preserved because it means 'not acceptable' and should remain distinguishable from a low-priority value. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [concept] Cloudflare normalizes the Accept-Language request header by converting languages to lowercase, stripping whitespace, sorting by quality value, and stripping region variants. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] For Accept-Language normalization, if an item in the optional languages list specifies a region variant and there is a matching item in the request header, the region variant is retained. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] By default, if Brotli compression is enabled, Cloudflare forwards Accept-Encoding: gzip, br to the origin; otherwise it forwards gzip. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] Accept-Encoding normalization only rewrites the origin request when Respect Strong ETags is turned on. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [concept] For headers other than Accept, Accept-Language, and Accept-Encoding, Cloudflare combines multiple field lines into a single comma-separated value and trims whitespace. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] For generic headers, values are not reordered, lowercased, or deduplicated because the order and contents may be significant. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [fact] Purging a URL purges all cached versions for that URL regardless of Vary header values. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [problem] Changing Vary configuration does not itself purge cached content, which may cause requests to miss and refill under new cache keys until old entries expire. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/
- [idea] To apply a new Vary configuration immediately, you must purge the cached content manually or wait for expiration. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/

## Glossary
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#page","h — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cach` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#on-this-page
- [parameter] cache: A temporary storage area where frequently accessed data is stored for quick retrieval. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] cache hit: When a requested piece of content is found in the cache, reducing the need to fetch it from the origin server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] cache lock: Cache lock (or mutex) is a mechanism employed by CDN data centers, comprising numerous servers, to prevent the overloading of origin servers. This mechanism ensures that only one server can request a specific file from the origin at any given time, facilitating efficient coordination among the servers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] cache miss: When a requested piece of content is not found in the cache, requiring the server to fetch it from the origin server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] cached bandwidth (cached egress bandwidth): The amount of bandwidth served from Cloudflare without hitting the origin server. Cached bandwidth is the sum of all EdgeResponseBytes where CacheCacheStatus equals hit, stale, updating, ignored, or revalidated. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] cached requests: The number of requests served from Cloudflare without having to hit the origin server. Cached requests are the sum of all requests where CacheCacheStatus equals hit, stale, updating, ignored. This does not include revalidated since the request had to be sent to the origin server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] caching: The process of storing copies of files or data in a cache to accelerate future requests. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] dynamic content: Dynamic content refers to website content that changes based on factors specific to the user such as time of visit, location, and device. News websites or social media are examples of this type of content. For this type of website, content has to be fetched from the origin server every time it is requested. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] edge server: A server located at the edge of a network, typically within a CDN, that serves content to end-users. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] origin bandwidth (origin egress bandwidth): The amount of data transferred from the origin server to Cloudflare within a certain period of time. Origin bandwidth is the sum of all EdgeResponseBytes where OriginResponseStatus does not equal 0. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] origin server: The original server where the web content is hosted before it is distributed to edge servers in a CDN. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] purge: The process of removing outdated content from the cache to make room for updated content and ensure the delivery of the latest content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] saved bandwidth (saved egress bandwidth): The percentage of bandwidth saved by caching on the Cloudflare network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] static content: Static content, like images, stylesheets, and JavaScript, remains the same for all users. It can be directly served from the cache without fetching from the origin server because it does not change without manual intervention. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] time-to-live (TTL): The duration for which a cached copy of a resource is considered valid before it needs to be refreshed or revalidated. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] total bandwidth (total egress bandwidth, edge bandwidth): Total bandwidth is the amount of data transferred from Cloudflare to end users within a certain period of time. Total bandwidth equals the sum of all EdgeResponseBytes for a certain period of time. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] uncached bandwidth (uncached egress bandwidth): Uncached bandwidth is the amount of bandwidth that is not cached and therefore is served from the origin. Uncached bandwidth is the sum of all EdgeResponseBytes where CacheCacheStatus does not equal hit, stale, updating, ignored, or revalidated. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] uncached requests: Uncached requests are requests that are not cached and therefore are served from the origin server. Uncached requests are the sum of all requests where CacheCacheStatus does not equal to hit, stale, updating, or ignored. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/glossary/#glossary

- [concept] Cloudflare's Always Online feature integrates with the Internet Archive to serve static portions of a website when the origin server is unreachable and no cached version exists. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [fact] When enabled, Cloudflare shares hostnames and popular URL paths with the Internet Archive so its crawler can store pages for archiving. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [fact] Cloudflare identifies target URLs for the crawler based on the most popular GET requests that returned a 200 HTTP status code in the previous five hours. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [problem] Cloudflare does not save every page of a website and cannot serve dynamic content while the origin is offline. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [fact] If a requested page is not found in the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine, the visitor sees the actual error page caused by the offline origin web server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [fact] Crawling intervals are limited by Cloudflare to ensure service stability, with limits varying according to the user's Cloudflare plan. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [fact] When Always Online with Internet Archive integration is enabled, visitors see a banner at the top of the webpage explaining they are viewing an archived version. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [actionable] Visitors can select the Refresh button to check whether the origin has recovered and fresh content is available. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [fact] When Cloudflare cannot reach an origin server, it returns an HTTP response status code in the range 520–527 to indicate unreachability. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [problem] Always Online only activates when Cloudflare cannot connect to the origin; it does not activate if the origin is reachable but returning error responses. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [fact] If an origin returns a 5xx status code (such as a 520) while reachable, Always Online will not trigger because the origin is considered online. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [problem] Visitors interacting with dynamic parts of a website, such as a shopping cart or comment box, will see an error page caused by the offline origin web server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [actionable] To enable Always Online, go to the Configuration page in the Cloudflare dashboard and choose the domain that will use the feature. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [actionable] Under the Always Online section in the dashboard, set the toggle to On to enable the feature. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/
- [fact] Turning on Always Online automatically enables the Internet Archive integration. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/always-online/

- [definition] Strong ETags — Strong ETag headers ensure the resource in browser cache and on the web server are byte-for-byte identical. - [definition] Behavior with Respect Strong ETags enabled — When you enable **Respect Strong ETags** in a cache rule, Cloudflare will use strong ETag header validation to ensure that resources in the Cloudflare cache and on the origin server are byte-for-byte identical. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/reference/etag-headers/#behavior-with-respect-strong-etags-enabled
- [definition] Behavior with Respect Strong ETags disabled — When **Respect Strong ETags** is disabled, Cloudflare will preserve strong ETag headers set by the origin web server if all the following conditions apply: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/reference/etag-headers/#behavior-with-respect-strong-etags-disabled

- [definition] Before you start — A recent [Purge Everything](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/purge-cache/purge-everything/), [purge by URL](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/purge-cache/purge-by-single-file/), [purge by… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/investigating-uncached-responses/#before-you-start
- [definition] DYNAMIC — request not eligible for cache — Cloudflare made the "do not cache" decision at request time, before looking in the cache. Common causes: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/investigating-uncached-responses/#dynamic-request-not-eligible-for-cache
- [definition] BYPASS — origin response is not cacheable — The request was eligible for cache, but the origin response or configuration prevented Cloudflare from storing it. Common causes: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/investigating-uncached-responses/#bypass-origin-response-is-not-cacheable
- [definition] Repeated MISS — cacheable but not in cache — `MISS` on the first request in each data center is expected — that request populates the cache. If the same URL keeps returning `MISS` across consecutive requests, one of the following is happening. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/investigating-uncached-responses/#repeated-miss-cacheable-but-not-in-cache
- [definition] Cache key variance — Cloudflare builds the cache key from the origin scheme, host, path, and query string by default. Cookies, headers, and device type can also contribute when configured. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/investigating-uncached-responses/#cache-key-variance
- [definition] Eviction and low-traffic assets — Low-traffic assets can be evicted from the cache before the next request arrives. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/investigating-uncached-responses/#eviction-and-low-traffic-assets
- [definition] Confirm the response reaches cache — After adjusting configuration, request the URL twice from the same client and verify the expected outcome for your configuration: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/investigating-uncached-responses/#confirm-the-response-reaches-cache

## Issues with MP4 videos on iOS and Safari
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/mp4-videos-on-ios-and-safari/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/mp — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cach` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/mp4-videos-on-ios-and-safari/#on-this-page
- [definition] Issues with MP4 videos on iOS and Safari — Last updated May 4, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/mp4-videos-on-ios-and-safari/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/mp4-videos-on-ios-and-safari/#issues-with-mp4-videos-on-ios-and-safari
- [definition] 1\. Create the strong ETags rule — Create a [cache rule](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/cache-rules/create-dashboard/) that applies to all MP4 files, marks them as eligible for cache, and turns on the Respect Strong ETags setting. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/mp4-videos-on-ios-and-safari/#1-create-the-strong-etags-rule
- [definition] 2\. Create the bypass cache rule — Create another cache rule that applies to all MP4 files and bypasses cache entirely. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/mp4-videos-on-ios-and-safari/#2-create-the-bypass-cache-rule
- [definition] Why this order matters — The first rule preserves strong ETags for MP4 files, which satisfies Safari's requirements for range request handling. The second rule bypasses cache so that Cloudflare forwards range requests to the origin server instead of serving cached responses with potentially mismatched ETags. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/mp4-videos-on-ios-and-safari/#why-this-order-matters

- [definition] Why is my ICP filing/license revoked? — The application and revocation of ICP filings or licenses is managed by China's local authorities. Usually, either the customer or the agency processing the ICP application will receive a notification with more details. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/china-network/faq/#why-is-my-icp-filinglicense-revoked
- [definition] What would happen if my ICP filing/license got revoked? — Cloudflare's partner JD Cloud and the local authorities continuously track the status of the ICP. - [definition] What is content vetting and why do I need JD Cloud to vet my domain's content before onboarding? — The JD Cloud network is proxying content inside of China for customers who have purchased Cloudflare China Network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/china-network/faq/#what-is-content-vetting-and-why-do-i-need-jd-cloud-to-vet-my-domains-content-before-onboarding
- [definition] How does IPv6 work on China Network? — All sites hosted in Mainland China must have IPv6 enabled. China Network automatically enables IPv6 for domains to fulfill this requirement and it is not possible to disable it. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/china-network/faq/#how-does-ipv6-work-on-china-network
- [definition] Is Turnstile available in Mainland China? — [Turnstile](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/) is not supported in Mainland China. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/china-network/faq/#is-turnstile-available-in-mainland-china

## Concepts
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#page","hea — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#on-this-page
- [parameter] A: Name=blog; Content=192.0.2.1; Proxy status=Proxied; TTL=Auto — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#zone-apex
- [parameter] A: Name=blog; Content=192.0.2.1; Proxy status=Proxied; TTL=Auto — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#zone-apex
- [parameter] A: Name=@; Content=192.0.2.1; Proxy status=Proxied; TTL=Auto — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#zone-apex
- [parameter] A: Name=@; Content=192.0.2.1; Proxy status=Proxied; TTL=Auto — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#zone-apex
- [definition] Concepts — Last updated Apr 16, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#concepts
- [definition] Domain — Also known as domain name, a domain is the string of text that identifies a specific website, such as `google.com` or `facebook.com`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#domain
- [definition] Registrar — Before you can start using the Cloudflare DNS service, you must first have a domain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#registrar
- [definition] Nameserver — DNS resolution — the process of translating a domain name into an IP address — involves several types of servers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#nameserver
- [definition] Authoritative DNS — Authoritative DNS refers to the service whose nameservers provide the final answer mapping a hostname (such as `example.com` or `blog.example.com`) to the IP address that hosts the corresponding content or resources. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#authoritative-dns
- [definition] DNS setups — It is also possible that one same company will use more than one DNS provider. Usually, this relates to making a domain more resilient - if one provider faces an outage, the nameservers operated by the other DNS provider will most likely still be available. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#dns-setups
- [definition] DNS records — DNS records are instructions that live in the authoritative DNS servers and provide information about a [zone](#zone). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#dns-records
- [definition] Zone — A DNS zone is an administrative boundary that defines who controls the DNS records for a given domain and its subdomains. For example, the zone for `example.com` contains the records for `example.com` and its subdomains like `blog.example.com`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#zone
- [definition] Zone apex — The zone apex is the highest-level domain within a zone — the starting point from which all DNS records in that zone are managed. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#zone-apex
- [definition] DNSSEC — Without additional protection, DNS responses can be spoofed — an attacker could return a forged response and redirect visitors to a malicious site. DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) addresses this by adding cryptographic signatures to DNS records. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/concepts/#dnssec

- [definition] 1\. Add your domain to Cloudflare — 1. Log in to the [Cloudflare dashboard ↗](https://dash.cloudflare.com). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#1-add-your-domain-to-cloudflare
- [definition] 2\. Review your DNS records — Your DNS records must be accurate for your domain to work properly. If you don't know what DNS records are, consider the video below for a quick explanation. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#2-review-your-dns-records
- [definition] Common records — Since the quick scan is not guaranteed to find all existing DNS records, you need to review your records, paying special attention to the following: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#common-records
- [definition] Proxy status — Each A, AAAA, and CNAME record has a [proxy status](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/) toggle: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#proxy-status
- [definition] 3\. Change your nameservers — Your domain will be assigned two authoritative Cloudflare nameservers. Nameservers are specialized servers that store your domain's DNS records and "answer" requests from browsers by providing the specific IP address needed to connect to your website. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#3-change-your-nameservers
- [definition] 3.1\. Get nameserver names — Your assigned nameservers are displayed as part of the onboarding flow. If you need to find them once again, go the zone **Overview** page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#31-get-nameserver-names
- [definition] 3.2\. Log in to your registrar — Log in to the admin account for your domain registrar. If you do not know your provider, use [ICANN Lookup ↗](https://lookup.icann.org/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#32-log-in-to-your-registrar
- [definition] 3.3\. Turn off DNSSEC — If your domain has [DNSSEC](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/)[1](#user-content-fn-1) active, you must [turn it off](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/#disable-dnssec) at your registrar before replacing nameservers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#33-turn-off-dnssec
- [definition] 3.4\. Update your registrar — 1. Remove your existing authoritative nameservers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#34-update-your-registrar
- [definition] 3.5\. Verify changes — Wait up to 24 hours while your registrar updates your nameservers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#35-verify-changes
- [definition] 4\. Re-enable DNSSEC — If you turned off DNSSEC before updating your nameservers, you can now [re-enable DNSSEC through Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/) to protect your domain from spoofing. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#4-re-enable-dnssec
- [definition] Footnotes — 1. A security feature that protects DNS records from spoofing [↩](#user-content-fnref-1) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/setup/#footnotes

## Troubleshooting
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/troubleshooting/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-set — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/troubleshooting/#on-this-page
- [definition] Troubleshooting — Last updated Jul 29, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/troubleshooting/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/troubleshooting/#troubleshooting
- [definition] Is a DS record present at your registrar? — You need to remove any pre-Cloudflare **DS** records at your registrar to update your authoritative nameservers. This will disable DNSSEC and allow Cloudflare to resolve your domain name. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/troubleshooting/#is-a-ds-record-present-at-your-registrar
- [definition] Do the nameservers at your registrar exactly match the values provided by Cloudflare? — If the nameservers in your registrar do not exactly match those provided by Cloudflare, your domain will not resolve correctly. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/troubleshooting/#do-the-nameservers-at-your-registrar-exactly-match-the-values-provided-by-cloudflare
- [definition] Are additional nameservers listed at your registrar? — If so, you should remove these nameservers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/troubleshooting/#are-additional-nameservers-listed-at-your-registrar
- [definition] Have you waited longer than 24 hours? — For some registrars, you will need to wait up to 24 hours for updates to your nameservers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/troubleshooting/#have-you-waited-longer-than-24-hours

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial- — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/#on-this-page

- [definition] DNS resolution — When you have a partial zone ([CNAME setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/)), Cloudflare resolves [DNS records differently](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/dns-resolution/) than for primary zones (full setup). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/#dns-resolution
- [definition] CNAME flattening — A CNAME setup (partial) requires the proxied hostname to be pointed to Cloudflare via a CNAME record. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/#cname-flattening
- [definition] DDoS protection — [DDoS protection](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/) for attacks against DNS infrastructure is only available for domains on [primary setup (full)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/#ddos-protection
- [definition] Domain ownership — Enterprise customers can use [zone holds](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/account/account-security/zone-holds/) to prevent other teams in the organization from adding zones that are already active in another Cloudflare account. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/#domain-ownership

- [definition] IP address resolution — At least one **IP address resolution** record is required for each domain on Cloudflare. These records are the only ones you can [proxy](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/) through Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#ip-address-resolution
- [definition] A and AAAA — [A and AAAA records ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dns-a-record/) map a domain name to one or multiple IPv4 or IPv6 address(es). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#a-and-aaaa
- [definition] CNAME — [CNAME records ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dns-cname-record/) map a domain name to another (canonical) domain name. They can be used to resolve other record types present on the target domain name. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#cname
- [definition] Email authentication — These records are recommended regardless of whether your domain sends email messages. Creating [secure email records ↗](https://blog.cloudflare.com/tackling-email-spoofing/) can help protect your domain against email spoofing. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#email-authentication
- [definition] MX — A mail exchange (MX) record is required to deliver email to a mail server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#mx
- [definition] DKIM — A DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) record ensures email authenticity by cryptographically signing emails: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#dkim
- [definition] SPF — A Sender Policy Framework (SPF) record lists authorized IP addresses and domains that can send email on behalf of your domain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#spf
- [definition] DMARC — A Domain-based Message Authentication Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) record helps generate aggregate reports about your email traffic and provide clear instructions for how email receivers should treat non-conforming emails. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#dmarc
- [definition] TXT — A [text (TXT) record ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dns-txt-record/) lets you enter text into the DNS system. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#txt
- [definition] CAA — A [Certificate Authority Authorization (CAA) record](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/caa-records/) specifies which Certificate Authorities (CAs) are allowed to issue certificates for a domain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#caa
- [definition] SRV — A [service record (SRV) ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dns-srv-record/) specifies a host and port for specific services like voice over IP (VOIP), instant messaging, and more. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#srv
- [definition] SVCB and HTTPS — Service Binding (SVCB) and HTTPS Service (HTTPS) records allow you to provide a client with information about how it should connect to a server upfront, without the need of an initial plaintext HTTP connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#svcb-and-https
- [definition] PTR — A [pointer (PTR) record ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dns-ptr-record/) specifies the allowed hosts for a given IP address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#ptr
- [definition] SOA — A start of authority (SOA) record stores information about your domain such as admin email address, when the domain was last updated, and more. Refer to [What is a DNS SOA record ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dns-soa-record/) for an example. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#soa
- [definition] NS — A [nameserver (NS) record ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dns-ns-record/) indicates which server should be used for authoritative DNS. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#ns
- [definition] DS and DNSKEY — [DS and DNSKEY ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dnskey-ds-records/) records help implement DNSSEC, which cryptographically signs DNS records to prevent domain spoofing. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#ds-and-dnskey
- [definition] Other — Cloudflare also supports other record types that are less common, such as URI, NAPTR, and certificate-related record types (SSHFP, TLSA, SMIMEA, and CERT). Refer to our [blog post ↗](https://blog.cloudflare.com/additional-record-types-available-with-cloudflare-dns/) for more information. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#other

- [definition] Comments — Comments are treated as [graphic Unicode characters ↗](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphic%5Fcharacter), meaning that they are case-sensitive and do not have any character limitations. - [definition] Tags — Tags are treated as an array of `name:value` pairs, meaning that tag names are not case-sensitive and can only contain letters, numbers, `-`, and `_`. For tag values, the same character restrictions apply as for comments. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/record-attributes/#tags

- [definition] Cause — A wildcard (`*`) record at your previous authoritative DNS provider may have been imported into Cloudflare in a way that creates additional records. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/troubleshooting/unexpected-dns-records/#cause

- [definition] Cause — When your `MX` or `SRV` record resolves to a domain configured to [proxy](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/) through Cloudflare, Cloudflare dynamically inserts a record into DNS responses that resolves to the origin IP address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/troubleshooting/unexpected-dns-records/#cause
- [definition] Solution — These records are safe — they ensure your mail traffic reaches your server correctly. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/troubleshooting/unexpected-dns-records/#solution
- [definition] Incorrect results for DNS queries — You notice DNS queries returning incorrect results even after you waited for the [TTL](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/ttl/) to expire. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/troubleshooting/unexpected-dns-records/#incorrect-results-for-dns-queries
- [definition] Cause — Third-party tools can sometimes fail to return correct DNS results if a recursive DNS cache fails to refresh. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/troubleshooting/unexpected-dns-records/#cause
- [definition] Solution — In this circumstance, purge your public DNS cache via these methods: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/troubleshooting/unexpected-dns-records/#solution

- [definition] DNS-only records — When an A, AAAA, or CNAME record is **DNS-only** — shown as a gray cloud icon in the dashboard, also known as "gray-clouded" — DNS queries for these will resolve to the record's actual origin IP address, as described in the [example](#example). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/#dns-only-records

## Proxying limitations
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/limitations/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/limitat — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/limitations/#on-this-page
- [definition] Proxying limitations — Last updated Apr 21, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/limitations/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/limitations/#proxying-limitations
- [definition] Proxy eligibility — Only A, AAAA, and CNAME records that serve HTTP or HTTPS traffic can be proxied. Other DNS record types cannot be proxied. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/limitations/#proxy-eligibility
- [definition] Pre-signed DNSSEC — If you use Cloudflare as your [secondary DNS provider](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/zone-transfers/cloudflare-as-secondary/) and leverage [Secondary DNS Overrides](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/zone-transfers/cloudflare-as-secondary/proxy-traffic/) to set… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/limitations/#pre-signed-dnssec
- [definition] Ports and protocols — To proxy HTTP/HTTPS traffic on [non-standard ports](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/reference/network-ports/) or to proxy a TCP or UDP based application, use [Cloudflare Spectrum](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/limitations/#ports-and-protocols
- [definition] Pending domains — When you [add a domain](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/manage-domains/add-site/) to Cloudflare, Cloudflare protection will be in a [pending state](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/reference/domain-status/) until we can verify ownership. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/limitations/#pending-domains
- [definition] Windows authentication — Because Microsoft Integrated Windows Authentication, NTLM, and Kerberos violate HTTP/1.1 specifications, they are not compatible with proxied DNS records. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/limitations/#windows-authentication

## Use cases
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cas — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#on-this-page
- [definition] Use cases — Last updated Apr 23, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#use-cases
- [definition] Proxied records — You should proxy all A, AAAA, and CNAME records that serve HTTP or HTTPS web traffic. This includes records for: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#proxied-records
- [definition] Source IP changes — Your origin server sees Cloudflare IP addresses as the source of all requests instead of the end-user's IP address. Applications that rely on the source IP for authentication, rate limiting, or geolocation will not function as expected without additional configuration. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#source-ip-changes
- [definition] Client certificate (mTLS) validation — When a record is proxied, TLS terminates at Cloudflare's global network. Cloudflare establishes a separate TLS connection to your origin server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#client-certificate-mtls-validation
- [definition] Header modifications — Cloudflare adds and modifies HTTP request headers when proxying traffic, including headers for [visitor IP identification](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/reference/http-headers/), diagnostics, and connection management. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#header-modifications
- [definition] DNS only — The following records should be set to DNS-only because the services they support are not compatible with Cloudflare's HTTP proxy. Proxying these records causes the associated service to break. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#dns-only
- [definition] Email — MX records cannot be proxied. If an A or AAAA record is used exclusively for email (for example, `mail.example.com`), it should also be set to DNS-only. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#email
- [definition] Domain verification — Third-party services often require CNAME or TXT records to verify domain ownership. Proxying a verification CNAME record returns Cloudflare IP addresses instead of the expected verification target. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#domain-verification
- [definition] SaaS-hosted websites — If your site is hosted on a SaaS platform (for example, [Wix](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/vendor-specific-records/#wix), Squarespace, Webflow), the platform serves your site from its own infrastructure. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#saas-hosted-websites
- [definition] Non-HTTP services — Records used for FTP, SSH, RDP, game servers, or other non-HTTP protocols must be DNS-only. Cloudflare's proxy only handles HTTP and HTTPS traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#non-http-services
- [definition] Other CDN or proxy providers — If a CNAME record points to another CDN or proxy provider (for example, AWS CloudFront, Akamai, Fastly), proxying it through Cloudflare can cause conflicts between the two proxies: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#other-cdn-or-proxy-providers
- [definition] API and webhook origin validation — Some third-party services validate the origin IP address of incoming API calls or webhook deliveries. When you proxy the DNS record for an endpoint that sends outbound requests or receives webhooks, the remote service sees Cloudflare's IP addresses instead of your server's IP address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/use-cases/#api-and-webhook-origin-validation

## Set up a private origin via Cloudflare WAN
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/>

- [snippet] Send a request from an external client: curl -v https://<YOUR_DOMAIN>/ — `curl -v https://<YOUR_DOMAIN>/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#send-a-request-from-an-external-client
- [snippet] Confirm traffic on the origin: sudo tcpdump -n -i any 'src net 100.64.0.0/12 and dst port 443' — `sudo tcpdump -n -i any 'src net 100.64.0.0/12 and dst port 443'` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#confirm-traffic-on-the-origin
- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set- — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#on-this-page
- [parameter] Connection timeouts from clients: Cloudflare Source IP is set to a public range. Set it to a private /12. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#common-pitfalls
- [parameter] Request times out, no response on the origin: The network where your origin lives has no return route for the Cloudflare Source IP range. Add a route that sends that range back through the tunnel. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#common-pitfalls
- [parameter] Tunnel shows IKE established but health checks fail: ICMP is blocked on the path or the health check is misconfigured. Allow ICMP between the tunnel endpoints and confirm the health check direction is bidirectional and type is reply. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#common-pitfalls
- [parameter] Traffic tries to route over the public Internet: The **Use private network routing** toggle is not turned on for the DNS record. Edit the record and turn the toggle on. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#common-pitfalls
- [definition] Set up a private origin via Cloudflare WAN — Last updated May 7, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#set-up-a-private-origin-via-cloudflare-wan
- [definition] 1\. Verify your Cloudflare Source IP allocation — A misconfigured Cloudflare Source IP is the most common cause of failure. If the Source IP is left as a public range, the network where your origin lives has no return route and requests time out before reaching the application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#1-verify-your-cloudflare-source-ip-allocation
- [definition] 2\. Create a DNS record with private network routing — Create an `A` or `AAAA` record that points to the private IP address of your origin, with proxy status enabled and **Use private network routing** turned on. This tells Cloudflare to send traffic for the hostname through your Cloudflare WAN tunnel instead of over the public Internet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#2-create-a-dns-record-with-private-network-routing
- [definition] 3\. Verify end-to-end connectivity — After the DNS record is in place, validate the path from the Cloudflare network through your tunnel to the origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#3-verify-end-to-end-connectivity
- [definition] Check tunnel health — In the Cloudflare dashboard, confirm that your IPsec tunnel is healthy. Refer to [Check tunnel health on the dashboard](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/common-settings/check-tunnel-health-dashboard/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#check-tunnel-health
- [definition] Send a request from an external client — From a machine outside your private network, send an HTTPS request to the proxied hostname: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#send-a-request-from-an-external-client
- [definition] Confirm traffic on the origin — On the origin VM, verify that requests are arriving from the Cloudflare Source IP range. For example, to watch for incoming traffic from `100.64.0.0/12` on port `443`: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/set-up-via-cloudflare-wan/#confirm-traffic-on-the-origin

- [definition] Setting seems off but traffic routes through tunnel — Check for other records on the same name. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/troubleshooting/#setting-seems-off-but-traffic-routes-through-tunnel
- [definition] Traffic not reaching origin — If traffic is not reaching your private origin: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/troubleshooting/#traffic-not-reaching-origin

- [definition] Request times out with no response on the origin — The network where your origin lives has no return route for the Cloudflare Source IP range. Add a route that sends that range back through the tunnel. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/troubleshooting/#request-times-out-with-no-response-on-the-origin
- [definition] Tunnel shows IKE established but health checks fail — ICMP is blocked on the path or the health check is misconfigured. Allow ICMP between the tunnel endpoints and confirm the health check direction is `bidirectional` and type is `reply`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/troubleshooting/#tunnel-shows-ike-established-but-health-checks-fail
- [definition] Traffic tries to route over the public Internet — The **Use private network routing** toggle is not turned on for the DNS record. Edit the record and turn the toggle on. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/private-origins/troubleshooting/#traffic-tries-to-route-over-the-public-internet

- [definition] Logs — You can [set up Logpush](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/) to deliver [DNS Firewall logs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/logpush-job/datasets/account/dns%5Ffirewall%5Flogs/) to a storage service, SIEM, or log management provider. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dns-firewall/analytics/#logs

- [definition] How does DNS Firewall choose a backend nameserver to query upstream? — DNS Firewall alternates between a customer's nameservers, using an algorithm that is more likely to send queries to the faster upstream nameservers than slower nameservers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dns-firewall/faq/#how-does-dns-firewall-choose-a-backend-nameserver-to-query-upstream
- [definition] How long does DNS Firewall cache a stale object? — DNS Firewall sets cache longevity according to allocated memory. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dns-firewall/faq/#how-long-does-dns-firewall-cache-a-stale-object
- [definition] Does the DNS Firewall cache SERVFAIL? — Yes. `SERVFAIL` is treated like any other negative answer for caching purposes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dns-firewall/faq/#does-the-dns-firewall-cache-servfail
- [definition] Does DNS Firewall support EDNS Client Subnet (ECS)? — Yes. Often, DNS providers want to see a client's IP via EDNS Client Subnet (ECS) ([RFC 7871 ↗](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7871.html)) because they serve geographically specific DNS answers based on the client's IP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dns-firewall/faq/#does-dns-firewall-support-edns-client-subnet-ecs
- [definition] Does DNS Firewall cache negative answers? — Yes. The default TTL is 30 seconds. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dns-firewall/faq/#does-dns-firewall-cache-negative-answers
- [definition] How can I set PTR records for nameserver hostnames? — To set up PTR records for the DNS Firewall cluster IPs that point to your nameserver hostnames, use the following API endpoints: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dns-firewall/faq/#how-can-i-set-ptr-records-for-nameserver-hostnames

- [definition] Common causes and resolutions — Below are the most common causes for DNS resolution errors along with suggested solutions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/troubleshooting/dns-issues/#common-causes-and-resolutions
- [definition] Mistyped domain or subdomain — Verify that the domain or subdomain was correctly spelled in the request URL. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/troubleshooting/dns-issues/#mistyped-domain-or-subdomain
- [definition] Missing DNS records — Ensure that you have the necessary DNS records for the domain or subdomain that is presenting the error. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/troubleshooting/dns-issues/#missing-dns-records
- [definition] DNSSEC was not disabled before the domain was added to Cloudflare — DNS resolution failures occur if [DNSSEC is not disabled](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/#disable-dnssec) at your domain provider before you add the domain to Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/troubleshooting/dns-issues/#dnssec-was-not-disabled-before-the-domain-was-added-to-cloudflare
- [definition] Nameservers no longer point to Cloudflare — If you manage DNS records via the Cloudflare dashboard and your domain stops pointing to Cloudflare's nameservers, DNS resolution will stop functioning. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/troubleshooting/dns-issues/#nameservers-no-longer-point-to-cloudflare
- [definition] Unresolved IP address — In rare cases, the DNS resolver in the client requesting the URL might fail to resolve a DNS record to a valid IP address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/troubleshooting/dns-issues/#unresolved-ip-address
- [definition] Newly created record still does not resolve — If you recently created a DNS record and resolvers still return `NXDOMAIN` (Non-Existent Domain) or no answer, it is likely because a negative response is currently stored in the resolver's cache. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/troubleshooting/dns-issues/#newly-created-record-still-does-not-resolve
- [definition] Account recovery — If you are locked out of the Cloudflare account that contains your DNS configuration, refer to [Account recovery](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/user-profiles/account-recovery/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/troubleshooting/dns-issues/#account-recovery

- [definition] Is Cloudflare a free DNS (domain nameserver) provider? — Yes. Cloudflare offers [free DNS services ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/dns) to customers on all plans. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#is-cloudflare-a-free-dns-domain-nameserver-provider
- [definition] Does Cloudflare charge for or limit DNS queries? — Cloudflare never limits or caps DNS queries, but the pricing depends on your plan level. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#does-cloudflare-charge-for-or-limit-dns-queries

- [definition] Does Cloudflare support EDNS0 (extension mechanisms for DNS)? — Yes, EDNS0 is a building block for modern DNS implementations and is enabled for all Cloudflare customers. EDNS0 adds support for signaling if the DNS Resolver (recursive DNS provider) supports larger message sizes and DNSSEC. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#does-cloudflare-support-edns0-extension-mechanisms-for-dns
- [definition] Where can I find my Cloudflare nameservers? — On the **DNS Records** page, locate the **Cloudflare Nameservers** card. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#where-can-i-find-my-cloudflare-nameservers
- [definition] Where do I change my nameservers to point to Cloudflare? — Make the change at your registrar, which is where you registered your domain. This may or may not be your hosting provider - refer to [Update nameservers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/nameservers/update-nameservers/) for further context. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#where-do-i-change-my-nameservers-to-point-to-cloudflare
- [definition] Why have I received an email: (mydomain) stopped using Cloudflare's nameservers? — For domains where Cloudflare hosts the DNS, Cloudflare continuously checks whether the domain uses Cloudflare's nameservers for DNS resolution. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#why-have-i-received-an-email-mydomain-stopped-using-cloudflares-nameservers
- [definition] Why does my new zone have different nameservers than my other zones? — Nameserver assignments happen at zone creation and [cannot be changed](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/nameservers/nameserver-options/#assignment-method) afterwards, even by Cloudflare Support. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#why-does-my-new-zone-have-different-nameservers-than-my-other-zones
- [definition] Does Cloudflare limit the number of DNS records a domain can have? — Yes. Refer to [DNS records quota](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/#dns-records-quota) for current limits per plan and details on how quotas are enforced. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#does-cloudflare-limit-the-number-of-dns-records-a-domain-can-have
- [definition] How long does it take for a DNS change I made to push out? — By default, any changes or additions you make to your Cloudflare zone file will take effect globally within 5 minutes, usually much less. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#how-long-does-it-take-for-a-dns-change-i-made-to-push-out
- [definition] Why can't I make ANY queries to Cloudflare DNS servers? — `ANY` queries are special and often misunderstood. They are usually used to get all record types available on a DNS name, but what they return is just any type in the cache of recursive resolvers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#why-cant-i-make-any-queries-to-cloudflare-dns-servers
- [definition] How do I add ANAME records on Cloudflare? — ANAME or ALIAS are DNS records used by specific DNS providers. If your previous provider was using ANAME or ALIAS, you can recreate these records on Cloudflare as CNAME records. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#how-do-i-add-aname-records-on-cloudflare
- [definition] Footnotes — 1. A process in which Cloudflare returns an IP address instead of the target hostname that a CNAME record points to. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#footnotes
- [definition] Why does my TXT record show a double quote in the middle of the value? — This is expected behavior. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#why-does-my-txt-record-show-a-double-quote-in-the-middle-of-the-value
- [definition] Why are Cloudflare's A or AAAA records / IP addresses for my domain's DNS responses appearing? — For DNS records proxied to Cloudflare, Cloudflare's IP addresses are returned in DNS queries instead of your original server IP address. This allows Cloudflare to optimize, cache, and protect all requests for your website. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/#why-are-cloudflares-a-or-aaaa-records-ip-addresses-for-my-domains-dns-responses-appearing

## Glossary
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#page","hea — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#on-this-page
- [parameter] active zone: A DNS zone that is active on Cloudflare requires changing its nameservers to Cloudflare's for management. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] apex domain: Apex domain is used to refer to a domain that does not contain a subdomain part, such as example.com (without www.). It is also known as "root domain" or "naked domain". — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] CNAME setup: Also known as partial setup, a CNAME setup allows you to use Cloudflare's reverse proxy without using Cloudflare for your authoritative nameservers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] DNS over HTTPS: DNS over HTTPS (DoH) is a standard for encrypting DNS traffic via the HTTPS protocol, preventing tracking and spoofing of DNS queries. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] DNS over TLS: DNS over TLS (DoT) is a standard for encrypting DNS traffic using its own port (853) and TLS encryption. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] DNS record: DNS records are instructions that live in authoritative DNS servers and provide information about a domain, including what IP address is associated with that domain and how to handle requests for that domain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] DNS server: DNS servers translate human-readable domain names into IP addresses, eliminating the need to remember complex IP addresses. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] DNS zone: A portion of the DNS namespace that is managed by a specific organization or administrator. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Domain Name System (DNS): The Domain Name System (DNS) is the phonebook of the Internet. DNS translates domain names to IP addresses. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] EDNS Client Subnet (ECS): ECS is a DNS extension that enables recursive DNS resolvers to include client IP address information in their DNS queries. Not all resolvers use ECS but, if they do, usually a part of the IP address is omitted. Sending ECS headers is generally intended to reduce latency and speed up content delivery in connection to… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] hostname: The name given to a server or node on a network, often the public DNS name of a server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] nameserver: A nameserver is a dedicated server that translates human readable hostnames (www.example.com) into IP addresses. Nameservers like root servers, TLD servers, and [authoritative nameservers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/nameservers/) are fundamental components of the Domain Name System (DNS). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] proxy status: The proxy status of a DNS record defines whether requests for your domain will route through Cloudflare (proxied) or not (DNS-only). When a [DNS record is proxied](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/), requests are processed according to your configurations, and Cloudflare can optimize, cache, and protect your domain. Refer to [How Cloudflare… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] zone apex: Zone apex refers to the domain or subdomain on which the control of DNS records starts. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary
- [definition] Glossary — Last updated Apr 16, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/glossary/#glossary

- [definition] Active - Passive Failover — An **active-passive failover** sends traffic to the endpoints in your active pool until a failure threshold (configurable) is reached. - [definition] Active - Active Failover — An **active-active failover** distributes traffic to endpoints in the same pool until the pool reaches its failure threshold (configurable). At the point of failure, your load balancer would then re-direct traffic to the **fallback pool**. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/load-balancers/common-configurations/#active-active-failover

- [definition] API commands — The Cloudflare API supports the following commands for monitors. Examples are given for user-level endpoint but apply to the account-level endpoint as well. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/monitors/#api-commands
- [definition] Supported protocols — The following table summarizes the different types of monitors available in Cloudflare Load Balancing, their monitoring types, and how each health check process evaluates the success criteria to determine endpoint health: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/monitors/#supported-protocols

- [definition] Result handling for different intervals — If monitors in a group have different check intervals, the group uses the last available result from each monitor until it is refreshed. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/monitors/monitor-groups/#result-handling-for-different-intervals

## Load shedding
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/>

- [snippet] Configure via API: curl --request PATCH \ — `curl --request PATCH \` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#configure-via-api
- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additiona — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/load` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#on-this-page
- [definition] Load shedding — Last updated May 5, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#load-shedding
- [definition] Step 1 — Identify at-risk endpoints — Using your internal metrics, identify endpoints at risk of reaching their failure threshold. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#step-1-identify-at-risk-endpoints
- [definition] Step 2 — Shed default traffic from a pool — Once you have identified an at-risk endpoint, shed a small amount of **Default** traffic from that endpoint's pool. This traffic is not affiliated with existing [Session affinity](https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/session-affinity/) sessions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#step-2-shed-default-traffic-from-a-pool
- [definition] Configure via dashboard — To enable load shedding for a specific pool via the dashboard: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#configure-via-dashboard
- [definition] Configure via API — To enable load shedding for a specific pool via the API, [update the values](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/load%5Fbalancers/subresources/pools/methods/update/) for the pool's `load_shedding` object. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#configure-via-api
- [definition] Step 3 — Monitor traffic — Once you have started shedding default traffic, evaluate the effects by reviewing the [**Overview** metrics](https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/reference/load-balancing-analytics/) in Load Balancing analytics. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#step-3-monitor-traffic
- [definition] Step 4 — Shed additional traffic (optional) — If you need to shed additional pool traffic: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#step-4-shed-additional-traffic-optional
- [definition] Step 5 — Disable load shedding — Once an endpoint is no longer at risk, remove load shedding from the pool. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#step-5-disable-load-shedding
- [definition] Shedding policies — For **Default traffic**, you have two choices for shedding policy. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#shedding-policies
- [definition] Fallback pools — If all pools within a load balancer have _Load shedding_ enabled, some traffic will go to the fallback pool. To prevent any traffic from reaching the fallback pool, ensure at least one pool within the load balancer **does not** have load shedding enabled. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#fallback-pools
- [definition] Pools in multiple load balancers — If you enable load shedding on a pool, it will shed the same percentage of traffic across all your load balancers. If you need an endpoint to shed different percentages of traffic for different load balancers, put that endpoint in multiple pools. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/load-shedding/#pools-in-multiple-load-balancers

- [definition] Solution — This typically occurs when there is a network failure between Cloudflare and your endpoint, and/or a firewall refused to allow our connection. - [definition] Alternate cause — You may also see this issue if you have a monitor configured to use HTTP connections and your endpoint is redirecting to HTTPS. - [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understan — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/load` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/session-affinity/#on-this-page

- [definition] Types — Session affinity specifies the type of session affinity the load balancer should use unless specified as `"none"` or `""` (default). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/session-affinity/#types
- [definition] By Cloudflare cookie only — On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a cookie is generated, encoding information of which endpoint the request will be forwarded to. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/session-affinity/#by-cloudflare-cookie-only
- [definition] By Cloudflare cookie and Client IP fallback — This behaves similar to `cookie` except the initial endpoint selection is stable and based on the client's IP address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/session-affinity/#by-cloudflare-cookie-and-client-ip-fallback
- [definition] By HTTP header — On the first request to a proxied load balancer, a session key based on the configured HTTP headers is generated. The session key encodes the request headers used for storing which endpoint the request will be forwarded to during the load balancer session state. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/session-affinity/#by-http-header
- [definition] Enabling Session Affinity from the Cloudflare dashboard — Enable Session Affinity when you [create or edit a load balancer](https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/load-balancers/create-load-balancer/), during the **Hostname** step. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/session-affinity/#enabling-session-affinity-from-the-cloudflare-dashboard
- [definition] Enabling Session Affinity via the Cloudflare API — Session affinity is a property of load balancers, which you can set with the following endpoints: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/session-affinity/#enabling-session-affinity-via-the-cloudflare-api
- [definition] Endpoint Drain — Drain or remove all traffic from an endpoint without affecting any active customers using endpoint drain. For more details on endpoint drain, refer to [Performing planned maintenance](https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/additional-options/planned-maintenance/#gradual-rotation). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/session-affinity/#endpoint-drain
- [definition] Zero-Downtime Failover — Zero-Downtime Failover automatically sends traffic to endpoints within a pool during transient network issues. This helps reduce errors shown to your users when issues occur in between active health monitors. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/session-affinity/#zero-downtime-failover

- [definition] Limitation when using Workers — Hash Steering relies on the `x-forwarded-for` header to determine the originating IP address of a request. However, when a [Cloudflare Worker](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/) is used in front of a load balancer, this can affect how Hash Steering functions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/traffic-steering/origin-level-steering/hash-origin-steering/#limitation-when-using-workers
- [definition] Workaround — To ensure Hash Steering works correctly when using a Worker in front of a Load Balancer, manually set the `x-forwarded-for` header in the Worker to the client's original IP address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/understand-basics/traffic-steering/origin-level-steering/hash-origin-steering/#workaround
