## Glossary
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#page" — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/spec` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#on-this-page
- [parameter] ACK (Acknowledge): The final step in the TCP three-way handshake, confirming the establishment of a connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] FTP (File Transfer Protocol): A standard network protocol used for transferring files from one host to another over a TCP-based network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] FTPS (File Transfer Protocol Secure): An extension of FTP that adds support for the Transport Layer Security (TLS) or Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) cryptographic protocols. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] layer 3: The network layer in the OSI model, responsible for logical addressing, routing, and forwarding of data between devices on different networks. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] layer 4: The transport layer in the OSI model, managing end-to-end communication, error-checking, and flow control. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport): A lightweight, publish-subscribe messaging protocol often used for communication in the Internet of Things (IoT) and other resource-constrained scenarios. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] OSI model (Open Systems Interconnection model): A conceptual framework that standardizes the functions of a telecommunication or computing system into seven abstraction layers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] proxy protocol: A protocol used by network proxies to convey client connection information to the destination server, facilitating proper handling of client requests. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] reverse proxy: A server that handles requests on behalf of clients, forwarding them to backend servers and managing tasks like load balancing and security. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol): A secure file transfer protocol that uses the Secure Socket Shell (SSH) protocol for encryption and authentication. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SMTP Server (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol Server): A server responsible for sending, receiving, and relaying email messages over a network, following the SMTP protocol. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SYN (Synchronize): The initial step in establishing a TCP connection, where a device requests a connection with another by sending a SYN packet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SYN-ACK (Synchronize-Acknowledge): The second step in the TCP three-way handshake, where the server responds to a SYN request with a SYN-ACK packet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] TCP (Transmission Control Protocol): A connection-oriented protocol in the transport layer of the Internet Protocol Suite, providing reliable and ordered delivery of data between devices. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] UDP (User Datagram Protocol): UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is a connectionless transport layer protocol that provides fast and lightweight data transmission between devices on a network, prioritizing speed over reliability. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary
- [definition] Glossary — Last updated Apr 16, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/glossary/#glossary

## Limitations
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limit — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/spec` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#on-this-page
- [definition] Limitations — Last updated Jun 22, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#limitations
- [definition] HTTPS — At the moment, HTTPS applications do not support HTTP/3. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#https
- [definition] UDP — Cloudflare does not support packet fragmentation for UDP packets. If packets are fragmented, they will be dropped at Cloudflare’s edge. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#udp
- [definition] Minecraft — Minecraft Java Edition is supported but Minecraft Bedrock Edition is not supported. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#minecraft
- [definition] Universal SSL — [Universal SSL](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/) is not compatible with Cloudflare Spectrum. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#universal-ssl
- [definition] Private Network Load Balancing — When using [Spectrum](https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/private-network/#on-ramps) as an on-ramp into Private Network Load Balancing, the [proxy protocol](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/how-to/enable-proxy-protocol/) setting in Spectrum is not supported. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#private-network-load-balancing
- [definition] Cloudflare Tunnel — Integrating Spectrum with [Cloudflare Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/) is only supported for **HTTP/HTTPS** applications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#cloudflare-tunnel
- [definition] Listen on ports configuration — By default, Spectrum is configured to listen on all ports, which can raise concerns for security auditors. However, it is important to note that Spectrum will only proxy connections from edge ports that are specifically configured within Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#listen-on-ports-configuration
- [definition] IP access control — Currently, [custom rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/custom-rules/) do not work with Spectrum applications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/limitations/#ip-access-control

## Simple Proxy Protocol Header
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/>

- [snippet] Simple Proxy Protocol Header: 0                   1                   2                   3 — ` 0                   1                   2                   3` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/#simple-proxy-protocol-header
- [snippet] Payload: struct { — `struct {` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/#payload
- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simpl — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/spec` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/#on-this-page
- [definition] Simple Proxy Protocol Header — Last updated Apr 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/#simple-proxy-protocol-header
- [definition] Magic Number — 16-bit fixed value set to 0x56EC for SPP. This field should be used to identify the SPP protocol and its SPP 38-byte header. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/#magic-number
- [definition] Client Address — 128-bit address of the originator of the proxied UDP datagram, that is, the client. An IPv6 address if the client used IPv6 addressing, or an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (refer to [RFC 4291 ↗](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4291)) in case of an IPv4 client. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/#client-address
- [definition] Proxy address — 128-bit address of the recipient of the proxied UDP datagram, that is the proxy. Contents should be interpreted in the same way as the Client Address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/#proxy-address
- [definition] Client port — 16-bit source port number of the proxied UDP datagram. In other words, the UDP port number from which the client sent the datagram. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/#client-port
- [definition] Proxy port — 16-bit destination port number of the proxied UDP datagram. In other words, the UDP port number on which the proxy received the datagram. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/#proxy-port
- [definition] Payload — Data following the header carried by the datagram. Magic number, addresses, and port numbers are encoded in network byte order. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/simple-proxy-protocol-header/#payload

- [definition] Cause — Cloudflare does not support having both a manually-created proxied DNS record (`A`, `AAAA`, or `CNAME`) and a Spectrum application on the same hostname. This is because Spectrum provisions and manages its own DNS record for the application, which conflicts with the existing manually-created record. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/troubleshooting/#cause
- [definition] Solution — If you only need Spectrum applications on the hostname (for example, an HTTP/HTTPS Spectrum application alongside a TCP/UDP Spectrum application), you do not need a workaround — create the additional Spectrum application on the same hostname. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/troubleshooting/#solution
- [definition] Cause — Spectrum operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP). When Edge TLS Termination is set to **off** (Passthrough), Spectrum forwards the raw TCP payload to the origin without modification. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/troubleshooting/#cause
- [definition] Solution — To send encrypted traffic from Cloudflare to your origin, you must turn on **Edge TLS Termination** on the Spectrum application and set it to **Full** or **Full (Strict)**: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/troubleshooting/#solution
- [definition] Cause — The TLS handshake between Cloudflare and your origin server failed. Common causes include: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/troubleshooting/#cause
- [definition] Solution — 1. Verify that your origin server has a valid TLS certificate and is configured to accept TLS connections on the origin port. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/troubleshooting/#solution
- [definition] Common Spectrum event log status codes — Spectrum uses its own set of connection status codes that are distinct from HTTP status codes used by Cloudflare's CDN layer. Some codes share numbers (for example, 444, 499) but have different meanings. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/reference/troubleshooting/#common-spectrum-event-log-status-codes

## Understand test results
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-r — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/spee` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#on-this-page
- [parameter] Time to First Byte ([TTFB ↗](https://web.dev/ttfb/)): Measures the time between the request for a resource and when the first byte of a response begins to arrive. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#synthetic-tests-and-real-user-monitoring-metrics
- [parameter] First Contentful Paint ([FCP ↗](https://web.dev/first-contentful-paint/)): Measures the time from when the page starts loading to when any part of the page's content is rendered on the screen. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#synthetic-tests-and-real-user-monitoring-metrics
- [parameter] Largest Contentful Paint ([LCP ↗](https://web.dev/lcp/)): CP reports the render time of the largest image or text block visible within the viewport. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#synthetic-tests-and-real-user-monitoring-metrics
- [parameter] Cumulative Layout Shift ([CLS ↗](https://web.dev/cls/)): Measures the largest burst of layout shift scores for every unexpected layout shift that occurs during the entire lifespan of a page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#synthetic-tests-and-real-user-monitoring-metrics
- [parameter] Time to Interactive ([TTI ↗](https://web.dev/tti/)): Measures the time from when the page starts loading to when its main sub-resources have loaded and it is capable of reliably responding to user input quickly. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#synthetic-tests-metrics
- [parameter] Total Blocking Time ([TBT ↗](https://web.dev/tbt/)): Measures the total amount of time between First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Time to Interactive (TTI) where the main thread was blocked for long enough to prevent input responsiveness. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#synthetic-tests-metrics
- [parameter] [Speed index ↗](https://web.dev/speed-index/): Measures how quickly content is visually displayed during page load. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#synthetic-tests-metrics
- [parameter] Interaction to Next Paint ([INP ↗](https://web.dev/inp/)): Aims to represent a page's overall responsiveness by measuring all click, tap, and keyboard interactions made with a page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#real-user-monitoring-metrics
- [parameter] Wait Time: Measures the time spent waiting for the server to send back the first byte of a response after a request is made. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#network-monitoring-metrics
- [parameter] Load Time: Measures the total time it takes for a web page to fully load in a user’s browser from the network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#network-monitoring-metrics
- [parameter] Time to First Byte ([TTFB ↗](https://web.dev/articles/ttfb)): Measures the duration between initiating a web page request and receiving the first byte from the server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#network-monitoring-metrics
- [parameter] Server Response Time: Measures the time it takes for a server to respond to a request from a user's browser. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#network-monitoring-metrics
- [parameter] Connect Time: Measures the time taken to establish a connection between the user's browser and the web server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#network-monitoring-metrics
- [parameter] TLS Time: Measures the time required to complete the TLS/SSL handshake between the user's browser and the web server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/observatory/test-results/#network-monitoring-metrics

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/origin-analytics/# — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/spee` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/origin-analytics/#on-this-page

- [parameter] [522 connection errors](https://developers.cloudflare.com/support/troubleshooting/http-status-codes/cloudflare-5xx-errors/error-522/): Verify that your firewall allows [Cloudflare IP ranges ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/) and that your origin is listening on the expected port. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/origin-analytics/#common-diagnostic-flows

- [definition] Origin response time — Use this metric to spot slowdowns and catch requests approaching your timeout threshold before they result in [524 errors](https://developers.cloudflare.com/support/troubleshooting/http-status-codes/cloudflare-5xx-errors/error-524/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/origin-analytics/#origin-response-time

## Troubleshooting a slow website

## Glossary
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#page","h — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/spee` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#on-this-page
- [parameter] bandwidth: The maximum rate of data transfer across a network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] brotli compression: Brotli compression is a data compression algorithm developed by Google, optimized for web content, and designed to achieve higher compression ratios than traditional algorithms like Gzip. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] compression: The process of reducing the size of files or data to speed up their transfer over the network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] core web vitals: Core web vitals are a set of user-centric performance metrics, including Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), and First Input Delay (FID), used by Google to assess the overall user experience of a webpage. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] cumulative layout shift (CLS): Cumulative layout shift (CLS) is a web performance metric that quantifies the visual stability of a webpage by measuring the sum of unexpected layout shifts of elements during the page's loading and rendering process. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] first contentful paint (FCP): First contentful paint (FCP) is a web performance metric that measures the time it takes for the first piece of content to be rendered on the screen during the loading of a web page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] first input delay (FID): First input delay (FID) is a web performance metric that measures the delay between a user's first interaction with a page (for example, clicking a button) and the moment the browser responds, indicating the page's interactivity and responsiveness. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] interaction to next paint (INP): Interaction to next paint (INP) is a web performance metric that measures the time it takes for a web page to become interactive and respond to user input after the initial paint, providing insights into the user experience during the interaction phase of page loading. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] largest contentful paint (LCP): Largest contentful paint (LCP) is a web performance metric that measures the time it takes for the largest content element to be fully rendered and visible to the user during the loading of a web page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] latency: The delay between a user action and the corresponding response from the system. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] lazy loading: Loading images or other resources only when they are about to be displayed, rather than loading everything at once. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] minification: The process of removing unnecessary characters from code (such as whitespace or comments) to reduce file size and improve loading times. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] page load time: The time it takes for a web page to fully load in a user's browser. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] real user monitoring (RUM): Real user monitoring (RUM) is a web performance monitoring technique that collects and analyzes data based on actual user interactions and experiences, providing insights into how users interact with a website or application in real-time. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] render time: The time it takes for a browser to display a fully rendered web page after receiving the necessary resources. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] search engine optimization (SEO): SEO, or search engine optimization, is the practice of optimizing online content to improve its visibility and ranking in search engine results, thereby increasing organic traffic and relevance. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] server response time: The time it takes for a server to respond to a request from a user's browser. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] speed index: Speed index is a web performance metric that quantifies how quickly a user perceives a webpage to load by measuring the visual progression of content rendering over time, providing a comprehensive assessment of the overall user experience during page loading. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] synthetic test: A synthetic test is an artificial simulation of user interactions and system behaviors designed to evaluate and measure the performance, responsiveness, and functionality of a website or application under controlled conditions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] time to first byte (TTFB): Time to first byte (TTFB) is the duration measured from the initiation of a web page request to the moment the first byte of data is received by the user's browser from the web server, indicating the server's initial response time. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] time to interactive (TTI): Time to interactive (TTI) is a web performance metric that measures the time it takes for a web page to become fully interactive and responsive to user input, indicating when users can effectively engage with and use the page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] total blocking time (TBT): Total blocking time (TBT) is a web performance metric that measures the total amount of time between First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Time to Interactive (TTI) where the main thread was blocked for long enough to prevent input responsiveness. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary
- [definition] Glossary — Last updated Apr 16, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/glossary/#glossary

- [definition] Content-Length header handling — When Cloudflare compresses a response sent to the website visitor, it may omit the `Content-Length` HTTP header to avoid delivering incorrect length information caused by dynamic transformations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/content/compression/#content-length-header-handling
- [definition] Content compression from origin servers to the Cloudflare network — When requesting content from your origin server, Cloudflare supports Brotli compression, Gzip compression, or no compression. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/content/compression/#content-compression-from-origin-servers-to-the-cloudflare-network
- [definition] Content recompression due to dynamic transformations — Even when using the same compression algorithm end to end (between your origin server and Cloudflare, and between the Cloudflare global network and your website visitor), Cloudflare will need to decompress the response and compress it again if you enable any of the following settings for the… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/content/compression/#content-recompression-due-to-dynamic-transformations
- [definition] Content-Length header — Cloudflare may remove the `Content-Length` HTTP header of responses delivered to website visitors. To ensure that the header is preserved, add a `cache-control: no-transform` HTTP header to the response at the origin server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/content/compression/#content-length-header
- [definition] Between visitors and Cloudflare — By default, Cloudflare uses the following compression methods for content delivery, depending on the zone plan. However, the actual compression applied may also depend on what the visitor's browser requests via the `accept-encoding` header. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/content/compression/#between-visitors-and-cloudflare
- [definition] Between Cloudflare and the origin server — On all plans, Cloudflare requests content from the origin server using the `accept-encoding: br, gzip` header. This means that Cloudflare asks the origin to send the content compressed using Brotli or Gzip, depending on which method the origin server supports. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/content/compression/#between-cloudflare-and-the-origin-server

- [parameter] Available-Dictionary: Direction=Browser → origin; Purpose=Advertises the SHA-256 hash of a dictionary the browser already has for the request URL. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/content/shared-dictionaries/#how-shared-dictionaries-work
- [parameter] Content-Encoding: dcb or dcz: Direction=Origin → browser; Purpose=Delta-compressed against the advertised dictionary, using Brotli (dcb) or Zstandard (dcz). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/content/shared-dictionaries/#how-shared-dictionaries-work
- [parameter] passthrough: Cloudflare forwards shared dictionary request and response headers, accepts dcb/dcz responses from the origin, and varies cache entries. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/content/shared-dictionaries/#1-enable-passthrough-in-cloudflare
- [parameter] disabled: Cloudflare strips shared dictionary headers and does not cache dcb/dcz variants. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/content/shared-dictionaries/#1-enable-passthrough-in-cloudflare

<https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/>

- [parameter] Availability: Free=Yes; Pro=Yes; Business=Yes; Enterprise=Yes — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#availability
- [parameter] Fewer TCP handshakes: Multiple requests share a single long-lived TCP connection, minimizing connection churn. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#benefits
- [parameter] Lower latency: Eliminates repeated TCP/TLS handshakes, reducing round-trip delays for new requests. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#benefits
- [parameter] Reduced origin load: Fewer concurrent connections for the origin to manage, easing load on resource-constrained systems. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#benefits
- [parameter] Adaptive scaling: During surges (for example, failovers), Cloudflare reuses available streams first, then opens new connections as needed. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#benefits
- [parameter] Free / Pro / Business: Default State=Enabled by default; Max concurrent streams per connection=200; Configurable?=No — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#default-behavior-by-plan
- [parameter] Enterprise: Default State=Disabled by default (1 stream per connection); Max concurrent streams per connection=1–200+; Configurable?=Yes — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#default-behavior-by-plan
- [parameter] Proxy Read Timeout: Default / Range=125s (up to 6000s for Enterprise); Error code=524; Description=Origin took too long to respond. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#timeouts-and-error-codes
- [parameter] Proxy Idle Timeout: Default / Range=900s (fixed); Error code=520; Description=Connection closed due to idleness. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#timeouts-and-error-codes
- [parameter] TCP Keep-Alive Interval: Default / Range=30s initial, 15s between probes; Error code=520; Description=After two missed probes, Cloudflare resets the connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#timeouts-and-error-codes
- [parameter] TCP Handshake Timeout: Default / Range=19s; Error code=522; Description=Origin did not complete the SYN handshake. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#timeouts-and-error-codes
- [parameter] TCP ACK Timeout: Default / Range=90s; Error code=522; Description=Origin stopped acknowledging data. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#timeouts-and-error-codes
- [definition] HTTP/2 to Origin — Last updated Aug 14, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#http2-to-origin
- [definition] Disable HTTP/2 to Origin — At Cloudflare, HTTP/2 connection to the origin is enabled by default. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#disable-http2-to-origin
- [definition] Connection multiplexing — Cloudflare supports HTTP/2 multiplexing from its global edge network to your origin servers. Instead of opening a new TCP connection for every incoming request, multiple HTTP/2 streams share a single long-lived TCP connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#connection-multiplexing
- [definition] How it works — When a new request arrives, Cloudflare attempts to reuse an existing HTTP/2 connection to the origin: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#how-it-works
- [definition] Configuration — Connection multiplexing is enabled by default on Free, Pro and Business zones and uses up to 100 concurrent streams by default. Enterprise plans can explicitly configure the maximum number of concurrent streams (often called the “multiplexing ratio”) for a zone in the dashboard or via API. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#configuration
- [definition] Protocol compatibility — Note that if the origin does not support HTTP/2, Cloudflare will initiate an HTTP/1.1 connection. We connect to servers who announce support of HTTP/2 connections via [ALPN ↗](https://blog.cloudflare.com/introducing-http2). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/speed/optimization/protocol/http2-to-origin/#protocol-compatibility

## Concepts
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#page","hea — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#on-this-page
- [definition] Concepts — Last updated Apr 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#concepts
- [definition] SSL/TLS certificate — An SSL/TLS certificate is what enables websites and applications to establish secure connections. With SSL/TLS, a client - such as a browser - can verify the authenticity and integrity of the server it is connecting with, and use encryption to exchange information. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#ssltls-certificate
- [definition] Edge certificate — The [edge certificates](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/) are the ones that Cloudflare presents to clients visiting your website or application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#edge-certificate
- [definition] Origin certificate — [Origin certificates](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/) guarantee the security and authentication on the other side of the network, between Cloudflare and the origin server of your website or application. Origin certificates are managed on your origin server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#origin-certificate
- [definition] Validity period — One common aspect of every SSL/TLS certificate is that they must have a fixed expiration date. If a certificate is expired, clients - such as your visitor's browser - will consider that a secure connection cannot be established, resulting in warnings or errors. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#validity-period
- [definition] Certificate authority (CA) — A [certificate authority (CA)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-authorities/) is a trusted third party that generates and gives out SSL/TLS certificates. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#certificate-authority-ca
- [definition] Validation level — SSL/TLS certificates vary in terms of the level to which a CA has validated them. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#validation-level
- [definition] Origin pull — When visitors request content from your website or application, Cloudflare first attempts to [serve content from the cache ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/cdn/what-is-caching/). If this attempt fails, Cloudflare sends a request back to your origin web server to get the content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#origin-pull
- [definition] Cipher suites — Besides the authentication and integrity aspects that valid certificates guarantee, the other important aspect of SSL/TLS certificates is encryption. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#cipher-suites
- [definition] Trust store — The list of [certificate authority (CA)](#certificate-authority-ca) and intermediate certificates that are trusted by operating systems, web browsers or other software that interacts with SSL/TLS certificates is called trust store. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#trust-store
- [definition] Chain of trust — Depending on your organization requirements, or if you have to troubleshoot an issue with your certificates, for example, you might come across the terms root certificate, intermediate certificate and leaf certificate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/concepts/#chain-of-trust

## Get started
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/get-started/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/get-started/#page"," — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/get-started/#on-this-page

- [definition] Choose your encryption mode — Once you have chosen your edge certificate, [choose an encryption mode](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/ssl-modes/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/get-started/#choose-your-encryption-mode

## Security levels
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/cipher-suites/recommendations/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/ad — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/cipher-suites/recommendations/#on-this-page
- [definition] Security levels — Last updated Apr 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/cipher-suites/recommendations/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/cipher-suites/recommendations/#security-levels
- [definition] Modern — Offers the best security and performance, limiting your range of clients to modern devices and browsers. Supports TLS 1.2-1.3 cipher suites. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/cipher-suites/recommendations/#modern
- [definition] Compatible — Provides broader compatibility with somewhat weaker security. Supports TLS 1.2-1.3 cipher suites. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/cipher-suites/recommendations/#compatible
- [definition] Legacy (default) — Includes all cipher suites that Cloudflare supports today. Broadest compatibility with the weakest security. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/cipher-suites/recommendations/#legacy-default
- [definition] Footnotes — 1. Although configured independently, cipher suites interact with **Minimum TLS version** and **TLS 1.3**. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/cipher-suites/recommendations/#footnotes

- [definition] Limitations — Advanced certificates do not apply to [Cloudflare Pages](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/) or [R2](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/) custom domains. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/advanced-certificate-manager/#limitations

- [definition] Domain name length limits — These limits are defined by internet standards ([RFC 1035 ↗](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1035) and [RFC 5280 ↗](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280)) and apply to all certificates, regardless of the certificate authority: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/advanced-certificate-manager/#domain-name-length-limits
- [definition] Wildcard coverage — Wildcard certificates only cover **one subdomain level**: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/advanced-certificate-manager/#wildcard-coverage
- [definition] Hostnames per certificate — A single advanced certificate can include up to **50 hosts** (SANs) total. The zone apex must be one of these 50, leaving room for up to 49 additional hostnames or wildcards. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/advanced-certificate-manager/#hostnames-per-certificate
- [definition] Consistency across certificate authorities — The character-length limits above (253-character total, 63-character label, 64-character CN) are defined by IETF standards ([RFC 1035 ↗](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1035), [RFC 5280 ↗](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280)) and apply uniformly across all CAs. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/advanced-certificate-manager/#consistency-across-certificate-authorities

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/ch — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/methods/http/#on-this-page

- [definition] Limitations — HTTP DCV is only available for [proxied domains](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/). It is possible to manually add the DCV token to the `.well-known/pki-validation/` directory on your origin web server to pre-validate your certificates. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/methods/http/#limitations
- [definition] Specify DCV method — If you want to use a [Universal SSL certificate](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/enable-universal-ssl/), you will need to edit the `validation_method` [via the API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/ssl/subresources/verification/methods/edit/)… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/methods/http/#specify-dcv-method
- [definition] Review other Cloudflare settings — To make sure your domain does not accidentally block HTTP DCV, review your Cloudflare settings for [common setup issues](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/methods/http/#review-other-cloudflare-settings
- [definition] Complete DCV — Your HTTP token will be available for the certificate authority as soon as you finish your [partial domain setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/setup/#3-add-dns-records). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/methods/http/#complete-dcv
- [definition] Renewal — Even if you manually handle DCV when issuing certificates in a [partial DNS setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/), at certificate renewal, Cloudflare will attempt to automatically perform DCV via HTTP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/methods/http/#renewal

## Troubleshooting
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/>

- [snippet] Redirection: not starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/.well-known/") — `not starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/.well-known/")` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#redirection
- [snippet] Redirection: (http.request.scheme eq "http") and not starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/.well-known/") — `(http.request.scheme eq "http") and not starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/.well-known/")` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#redirection
- [snippet] CAA records: dig example.com CAA +short — `dig example.com CAA +short` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#caa-records
- [snippet] CAA records: Resolve-DnsName -Name example.com -Type CAA — `Resolve-DnsName -Name example.com -Type CAA` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#caa-records
- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/ch — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#on-this-page
- [definition] Troubleshooting — Last updated Jun 19, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#troubleshooting
- [definition] Quick checklist — Use this checklist to identify common DCV issues: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#quick-checklist
- [definition] Blocked validation URL — If you have issues while HTTP DCV is in place, review the following settings: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#blocked-validation-url
- [definition] Redirection — Enabling [Always Use HTTPS](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/always-use-https/) does not impact the validation process. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#redirection
- [definition] DNS settings and records — The errors below refer to situations that have to be addressed at the authoritative DNS provider: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#dns-settings-and-records
- [definition] Certificate authority (CA) errors — A [certificate authority (CA)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-authorities/) is the organization that issues your SSL/TLS certificate. Cloudflare partners with multiple CAs to provide certificates for your domain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#certificate-authority-ca-errors
- [definition] Rate limiting — As mentioned in [Certificate authorities](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-authorities/), specific CAs may have their own limitations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#rate-limiting
- [definition] CAA records block issuance — The error `CAA records block issuance. Please remove all CAA records or add records for this authority` indicates that your domain's [CAA records](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/caa-records/) do not allow the selected certificate authority to issue certificates. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#caa-records-block-issuance
- [definition] Multiple perspective validation errors — Certificate authorities perform domain validation from multiple geographic locations to prevent certain attacks. You may encounter one of these errors: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#multiple-perspective-validation-errors
- [definition] DNS lookup errors — The error `the Certificate Authority had trouble performing a DNS lookup` indicates that the CA could not resolve your domain's DNS records. Common causes include SERVFAIL responses, NXDOMAIN, or DNSSEC validation failures. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#dns-lookup-errors
- [definition] Rejected identifier — The error `The certificate authority will not issue for this domain. Please check your input or try another authority` means the CA has policies that prevent issuing certificates for your specific domain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#rejected-identifier
- [definition] Internal errors — When you see `Internal error with Certificate Authority. Please check later`, the certificate authority encountered a temporary issue during validation. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/changing-dcv-method/troubleshooting/#internal-errors

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/cu — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/custom-certificates/bundling-methodologies/#on-this-page
- [definition] Bundle methodologies — Last updated Apr 16, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/custom-certificates/bundling-methodologies/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/custom-certificates/bundling-methodologies/#bundle-methodologies
- [definition] Intermediate and root certificates — Cloudflare maintains intermediate and root certificates used for bundling on a [GitHub repository ↗](https://github.com/cloudflare/cfssl%5Ftrust). As the certificates expire or are removed by certificate authorities, Cloudflare removes and adds them accordingly. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/custom-certificates/bundling-methodologies/#intermediate-and-root-certificates
- [definition] Compatible — Compatible is the default methodology and uses common and well distributed intermediate certificates to complete the chain. This ensures that the resulting bundle is compatible with as many clients as possible. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/custom-certificates/bundling-methodologies/#compatible
- [definition] Modern — Modern consists of attempts to make the chain as efficient as possible, often by using newer or fewer intermediate certificates. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/custom-certificates/bundling-methodologies/#modern
- [definition] User-defined — User-defined allows you to paste your own certificate chain and present that bundle to clients. If you are using a self-signed certificate (not recommended), you must use this mode. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/custom-certificates/bundling-methodologies/#user-defined

## Limitations
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/un — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#on-this-page
- [definition] Limitations — Last updated Apr 30, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#limitations
- [definition] Proxy status — Cloudflare can only serve an SSL/TLS certificate for a DNS record when you set the record's [proxy status](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/) to **Proxied**. If you do not do this, the origin server your record points to will be responsible for supporting SSL/TLS connections. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#proxy-status
- [definition] Full setup — When you rely only on Universal SSL in a full setup zone, coverage is limited to the root domain (for example, `example.com`) and first-level subdomains (for example, `www.example.com` or `blog.example.com`). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#full-setup
- [definition] CNAME setup — On a [CNAME setup zone](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/), each subdomain (regardless of level) has its own Universal SSL certificate and does not require additional features or purchases. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#cname-setup
- [definition] Certificate authority — For Universal SSL certificates, Cloudflare chooses the certificate authority (CA) used for your certificate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#certificate-authority
- [definition] Validity period — For Universal certificates, Cloudflare controls the validity period. Refer to [validity periods and renewal](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-validity-periods/#universal-ssl) for details. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#validity-period
- [definition] TLS settings — [Customizing cipher suites](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/cipher-suites/customize-cipher-suites/) is only available with [Advanced Certificate Manager](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/advanced-certificate-manager/) or within… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#tls-settings
- [definition] Delegated DCV — Delegated DCV allows zones with [partial DNS setups](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/partial-setup/) to delegate the DCV process to Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#delegated-dcv
- [definition] Spectrum — Universal SSL is not compatible with [Cloudflare Spectrum](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#spectrum
- [definition] Load balancing — Due to internal limitations, Universal SSL certificates do not cover [load balancing hostnames](https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/load-balancers/dns-records/) by default. This behavior will be corrected in the future. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#load-balancing
- [definition] Browser support — For more on browser support, see [Browser compatibility](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-compatibility/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#browser-support
- [definition] SSL invalid brand check — Some domains are not eligible for Universal SSL if they contain words that conflict with trademarked domains. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#ssl-invalid-brand-check
- [definition] Certificate pinning — Cloudflare does not support HTTP public key pinning (HPKP) for universal, advanced, or custom hostname certificates. For details and recommended alternatives, refer to [Certificate pinning](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-pinning/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/#certificate-pinning

- [definition] Forward certificate to server — Last updated Apr 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/client-certificates/forward-a-client-certificate/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/client-certificates/forward-a-client-certificate/#forward-certificate-to-server
- [definition] Add Client-Cert and Client-Cert-Chain headers (RFC 9440) — [RFC 9440 ↗](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9440) defines the `Client-Cert` and `Client-Cert-Chain` HTTP header fields for passing client certificate information to origin servers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/client-certificates/forward-a-client-certificate/#add-client-cert-and-client-cert-chain-headers-rfc-9440
- [definition] Size limits — The encoded leaf certificate is limited to 10 KiB and the encoded chain is limited to 16 KiB. If the encoded value exceeds the limit, the corresponding field contains an empty string. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/client-certificates/forward-a-client-certificate/#size-limits
- [definition] Example Transform Rules — Here we provide an example on how to securely use these fields to construct trusted `Client-Cert` and `Client-Cert-Chain` headers to be forwarded to your origin. The origin can then rely on the presence of the headers to be certain the client presented a valid certificate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/client-certificates/forward-a-client-certificate/#example-transform-rules
- [definition] Cloudflare Workers — You can also construct RFC 9440 headers in a [Cloudflare Worker](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/)using the [tlsClientAuth](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/client-certificates/client-certificate-variables/#workers-variables)properties on the incoming request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/client-certificates/forward-a-client-certificate/#cloudflare-workers
- [definition] Forward a client certificate (legacy) — In addition to enforcing mTLS authentication for your host, you can also forward a client certificate to your origin server as an HTTP header. - [definition] 2\. Upload Keyless SSL Certificates — Before your key servers can be configured, you must next upload the corresponding SSL certificates to Cloudflare’s edge. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/keyless-ssl/configuration/public-dns/#2-upload-keyless-ssl-certificates
- [definition] 3\. - [definition] Cloudflare Keyless SSL key server (“key server”) — The key server is a daemon that you run on your own infrastructure. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/keyless-ssl/glossary/#cloudflare-keyless-ssl-key-server-key-server
- [definition] Cloudflare Keyless SSL client (“keyless client”) — The keyless client is a process that runs on Cloudflare's infrastructure. ## Post-quantum cryptography (PQC)
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptog — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/#on-this-page
- [definition] Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) — Last updated Jul 3, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/#post-quantum-cryptography-pqc
- [definition] Three building blocks of TLS — Before TLS can protect your communications, three cryptographic algorithms have to be agreed on during the [TLS handshake ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/ssl/what-happens-in-a-tls-handshake/): — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/#three-building-blocks-of-tls
- [definition] Hybrid key agreement — With TLS 1.3, [X25519 ↗](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curve25519) \- an Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) protocol - is the most commonly used algorithm in key agreement. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/#hybrid-key-agreement
- [definition] Post-quantum signatures — Recent advances in quantum hardware and algorithms have accelerated the timeline on which a cryptographically relevant quantum computer might exist, which in turn elevates the priority of migrating authentication (signatures) to post-quantum algorithms. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/#post-quantum-signatures
- [definition] Three connections in the life of a request — flowchart LR accTitle: Three connections - from visitor to Cloudflare to origin server accDescr: Diagram showing connections for an uncached request. A[Visitor] subgraph Cloudflare X[(Cloudflare <br />service A)] B[(Cloudflare <br />service B)] end C[(Origin server)] — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/#three-connections-in-the-life-of-a-request
- [definition] 1\. Visitor to Cloudflare — As of [October 2022 ↗](https://blog.cloudflare.com/post-quantum-for-all/), all websites and APIs served through Cloudflare over TLS 1.3 support post-quantum hybrid key agreement. However, the connection is only post-quantum secured if the client also supports PQC. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/#1-visitor-to-cloudflare
- [definition] 2\. Internal connections — As announced in [September 2023 ↗](https://blog.cloudflare.com/post-quantum-cryptography-ga/), most internal connections for Cloudflare's products and systems have been upgraded to use PQC. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/#2-internal-connections
- [definition] 3\. Cloudflare to your origin — Finally, Cloudflare also supports [hybrid key agreements](#hybrid-key-agreement) when connecting to origins. In this case, post-quantum secured connections will depend on the origin servers also supporting PQC. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/#3-cloudflare-to-your-origin
- [definition] Protect corporate network traffic — With [Zero Trust](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/), Cloudflare allows organizations to upgrade their sensitive network traffic to PQC without the hassle of individually upgrading each and every corporate application, system, or network connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/#protect-corporate-network-traffic

- [definition] Post-quantum between Cloudflare and origin servers — Last updated Aug 3, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/pqc-to-origin/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/pqc-to-origin/#post-quantum-between-cloudflare-and-origin-servers
- [definition] Post-quantum key agreement — As explained in [About PQC](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/), Cloudflare has deployed support for hybrid key agreements, which includes both the most common key agreement for TLS 1.3, X25519, and the post-quantum secure ML-KEM. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/pqc-to-origin/#post-quantum-key-agreement
- [definition] ClientHello from Cloudflare — Cloudflare uses [automatic key exchange](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/automatic-key-exchange/) to learn which key agreements a zone's origin servers prefer. Cloudflare applies one preference across the zone. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/pqc-to-origin/#clienthello-from-cloudflare
- [definition] Post-quantum signatures — Since mid-2026, Cloudflare supports [ML-DSA ↗](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/204/final) post-quantum signatures in two origin-facing features: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/pqc-to-origin/#post-quantum-signatures
- [definition] Generate an ML-DSA certificate authority and leaf certificate — The following commands create a private certificate authority and a leaf certificate that chains to it, using ML-DSA-44\. Repeat once for an AOP client certificate, and once for a COTS server-facing certificate if you manage that side too. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/pqc-to-origin/#generate-an-ml-dsa-certificate-authority-and-leaf-certificate
- [definition] Set up Authenticated Origin Pulls with an ML-DSA client certificate — ML-DSA client certificates are supported with both [zone-level](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/authenticated-origin-pull/set-up/zone-level/) and [per-hostname](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/authenticated-origin-pull/set-up/per-hostname/) AOP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/pqc-to-origin/#set-up-authenticated-origin-pulls-with-an-ml-dsa-client-certificate
- [definition] Set up Custom Origin Trust Store with an ML-DSA CA — Upload the ML-DSA CA certificate (the `ca.crt` file generated earlier) as a [Custom Origin Trust Store](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/custom-origin-trust-store/) entry. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/pqc-to-origin/#set-up-custom-origin-trust-store-with-an-ml-dsa-ca
- [definition] Verify end-to-end — Once AOP and COTS are configured, you can verify the post-quantum origin handshake from a host that has ML-DSA support. For example, from a machine with OpenSSL 3.5.0 or later, connect directly to your origin and confirm the handshake uses ML-DSA: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/pqc-to-origin/#verify-end-to-end
- [definition] Avoid downgrades — Presenting an ML-DSA certificate on the authenticating side is not enough on its own. To actually gain post-quantum authentication, the _verifying_ side must reject classical (non-post-quantum) certificates. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/post-quantum-cryptography/pqc-to-origin/#avoid-downgrades

## SSL/TLS FAQ
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#page","headline — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#on-this-page
- [definition] SSL/TLS FAQ — Last updated Apr 16, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#ssltls-faq
- [definition] Does Cloudflare issue both RSA and ECDSA certificates? — Yes. Cloudflare can issue both RSA and ECDSA certificates. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#does-cloudflare-issue-both-rsa-and-ecdsa-certificates
- [definition] Are Cloudflare SSL certificates shared? — No. Cloudflare SSL/TLS certificates are not shared across domains nor across customers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#are-cloudflare-ssl-certificates-shared
- [definition] If I have multiple Cloudflare certificates, which one is used? — Cloudflare certificates are prioritized by a combination of hostname specificity, zone specificity, and certificate type. For more details, refer to [Certificate and hostname priority](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-and-hostname-priority/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#if-i-have-multiple-cloudflare-certificates-which-one-is-used
- [definition] Why do I see a Cloudflare certificate when an SSL certificate is installed at my website? — Cloudflare must decrypt traffic in order to cache and filter malicious traffic. Cloudflare either re-encrypts traffic or sends plain text traffic to the origin web server depending on your domain's [encryption mode](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/ssl-modes/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#why-do-i-see-a-cloudflare-certificate-when-an-ssl-certificate-is-installed-at-my-website
- [definition] Which certificate authorities does Cloudflare use? — Cloudflare uses Let's Encrypt, Google Trust Services, SSL.com, and Sectigo. You can see a complete list of products and available CAs and algorithms in the [certificate authorities reference page](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-authorities/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#which-certificate-authorities-does-cloudflare-use
- [definition] Are there any CA limitations I should know about? — Refer to the [certificate authorities reference page](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-authorities/) for a list of limitations for every CA in our pipeline. There you can also find information about device and browser compatibility. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#are-there-any-ca-limitations-i-should-know-about
- [definition] I do not want to use the CAs that Cloudflare partners with. What can I do? — If you are on a Business or Enterprise plan, you can [upload a certificate](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/custom-certificates/uploading/#upload-a-custom-certificate) from the CA of your choice. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#i-do-not-want-to-use-the-cas-that-cloudflare-partners-with-what-can-i-do
- [definition] I am missing the CAs that Cloudflare uses in my trust store. What should I do? — You can use [CFSSL trust store ↗](https://github.com/cloudflare/cfssl%5Ftrust), which includes all of the CAs that are used by Cloudflare managed certificates. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#i-am-missing-the-cas-that-cloudflare-uses-in-my-trust-store-what-should-i-do
- [definition] What is CAA and how can I create one? — A Certificate Authority Authorization (CAA) DNS record specifies which certificate authorities (CAs) are allowed to issue certificates for a domain. This record reduces the chance of unauthorized certificate issuance and promotes standardization across your organization. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#what-is-caa-and-how-can-i-create-one
- [definition] How does Cloudflare evaluate CAA records? — CAA records are evaluated by a CA, not by Cloudflare. For details, refer to [RFC 8659 ↗](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8659.html#name-relevant-resource-record-se). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#how-does-cloudflare-evaluate-caa-records
- [definition] What are the dangers of setting CAA records? — If you are part of a large organization or one where multiple parties are tasked with obtaining SSL certificates, [include CAA records](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/caa-records/) that allow issuance for all CAs applicable for your organization. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#what-are-the-dangers-of-setting-caa-records
- [definition] What CAA records do I need to allow issuance from Cloudflare CAs? — You can find CAA records associated with every Cloudflare CA in the [certificate authorities reference page](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-authorities/#caa-records). If you are using Cloudflare as your DNS provider, then the CAA records will be added on your behalf. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#what-caa-records-do-i-need-to-allow-issuance-from-cloudflare-cas
- [definition] I am using Universal SSL and I would like to use a different CA. How can I do that? — To be able to specify a CA, you must purchase [Advanced Certificate Manager](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/advanced-certificate-manager/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#i-am-using-universal-ssl-and-i-would-like-to-use-a-different-ca-how-can-i-do-that
- [definition] Does Cloudflare issue both RSA and ECDSA certificates for Universal certificates? — Universal certificates on free zones only receive an ECDSA certificate. Paid zones receive an RSA and ECDSA certificate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#does-cloudflare-issue-both-rsa-and-ecdsa-certificates-for-universal-certificates

## About
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/authenticated-origin-pull/explanation/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/authenticated-origin-pull/explanation/#on-this-page
- [definition] About — Last updated Apr 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/authenticated-origin-pull/explanation/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/authenticated-origin-pull/explanation/#about
- [definition] Simple explanation — When visitors request content from your domain, Cloudflare first attempts to serve content from the cache. If this attempt fails, Cloudflare sends a request — or an `origin pull` — back to your origin web server to get the content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/authenticated-origin-pull/explanation/#simple-explanation
- [definition] Detailed explanation — Cloudflare enforces authenticated origin pulls by adding an extra layer of TLS client certificate authentication when establishing a connection between Cloudflare and the origin web server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/authenticated-origin-pull/explanation/#detailed-explanation
- [definition] Types of handshakes — For more details, refer to [What is a TLS handshake? ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/ssl/what-happens-in-a-tls-handshake/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/authenticated-origin-pull/explanation/#types-of-handshakes
- [definition] Comparison diagrams — Without Authenticated Origin Pulls, Cloudflare performs standard TLS handshakes between a client device and Cloudflare and Cloudflare and your origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/authenticated-origin-pull/explanation/#comparison-diagrams

## Automatic key exchange to origins
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/automatic-key-exchange/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/automatic-key-exchange/#on-this-page
- [parameter] On: Cloudflare scans your origins and sends the zone's preferred key share. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/automatic-key-exchange/#automatic-key-exchange
- [parameter] Off: Cloudflare does not scan or reorder key shares. It uses the default order for your selected compliance requirements. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/automatic-key-exchange/#automatic-key-exchange
- [parameter] No selection: API value=\[\]; Behavior=Allows supported classical and post-quantum key agreements. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/automatic-key-exchange/#compliance-requirements
- [parameter] Post-quantum hybrid: API value=\["pqh"\]; Behavior=Allows only hybrid post-quantum key agreements. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/automatic-key-exchange/#compliance-requirements
- [parameter] Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS): API value=\["fips"\]; Behavior=Allows only key agreements that meet FIPS requirements. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/automatic-key-exchange/#compliance-requirements
- [parameter] Post-quantum hybrid and FIPS: API value=\["pqh", "fips"\]; Behavior=Allows only key agreements that satisfy both requirements. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/automatic-key-exchange/#compliance-requirements

- [definition] How automatic selection works — Cloudflare scans active origins approximately every 24 hours. - [definition] Configuration options — To configure automatic key exchange in the dashboard: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/automatic-key-exchange/#configuration-options

- [definition] TLS 1.3 cipher suites — Although TLS 1.3 uses the same cipher suite space as previous versions of TLS, TLS 1.3 cipher suites are defined differently, only specifying the symmetric ciphers, and cannot be used for TLS 1.2 ([RFC 8446 ↗](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html)). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/cipher-suites/#tls-13-cipher-suites
- [definition] Match on origin — Cloudflare will present the cipher suites to your origin and your server will select whichever cipher suite it prefers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/cipher-suites/#match-on-origin
- [definition] Footnotes — 1. Refer to [TLS 1.3 cipher suites](#tls-13-cipher-suites) for details. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/cipher-suites/#footnotes

- [definition] Use when — Choose **Full** mode when your origin can support an SSL certification, but — for various reasons — it cannot support a valid, publicly trusted certificate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/ssl-modes/full/#use-when

- [definition] Process — To change your encryption mode in the dashboard: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/ssl-modes/full/#process
- [definition] Limitations — The certificate presented by the origin will **not be validated in any way**. It can be expired, self-signed, or not even have a matching CN/SAN entry for the hostname requested. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/origin-configuration/ssl-modes/full/#limitations

## Browser compatibility
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-compatibility/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-co — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-compatibility/#on-this-page
- [definition] Browser compatibility — Last updated May 21, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-compatibility/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-compatibility/#browser-compatibility
- [definition] Universal SSL — Cloudflare Universal SSL only supports browsers and API clients that use the [Server Name Indication (SNI) ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/ssl/what-is-sni/) extension to the TLS protocol. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-compatibility/#universal-ssl
- [definition] Other certificate types — Refer to [Certificate authorities](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-authorities/) for a detailed list of Cloudflare SSL/TLS offerings, the different algorithms available, and browser compatibility for each CA. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-compatibility/#other-certificate-types
- [definition] Non-SNI support — Although [SNI extensions ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/ssl/what-is-sni/) to the TLS protocol were standardized in 2003, some browsers and operating systems only implemented this extension when TLS 1.1 was released in 2006 (or 2011 for mobile browsers). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-compatibility/#non-sni-support
- [definition] HTTPS records — [HTTPS Service (HTTPS) records](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/#svcb-and-https) allow you to provide a client with information about how it should connect to a server upfront, without the need of an initial plaintext HTTP connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-compatibility/#https-records
- [definition] OCSP and HTTP versions — Cloudflare's OCSP implementation uses HTTP/1.1 by default for plain HTTP connections. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/browser-compatibility/#ocsp-and-http-versions
