- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificat — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#on-this-page
- [definition] Rotate ACM certificate packs — Last updated Jun 25, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#rotate-acm-certificate-packs
- [definition] 1\. Create the new certificate pack — 1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, go to the **Edge Certificates** page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#1-create-the-new-certificate-pack
- [definition] 2\. Wait for Active status — After ordering, the new certificate pack moves through several intermediate states before it is ready to serve traffic: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#2-wait-for-active-status
- [definition] 3\. Delete the old certificate pack — Once the new pack is **Active**, it is safe to delete the old one. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#3-delete-the-old-certificate-pack
- [definition] 4\. Expect a brief Pending Deployment state — After the old pack is deleted, the remaining certificate may briefly show **Pending Deployment** before returning to **Active**. This reflects a normal edge re-evaluation cycle as the global network reconciles the change, and typically resolves within a few minutes with no traffic impact. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#4-expect-a-brief-pending-deployment-state
- [definition] Terraform — Certificate packs cannot be updated in place - every attribute of the `cloudflare_certificate_pack` resource forces a new resource on change. Plan your rotation around this constraint. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#terraform
- [definition] Wait for Active automatically — Set `wait_for_active_status = true` on the new resource to have Terraform block the apply until the certificate pack reaches **Active**. This removes the need to manually poll the dashboard or API between steps 1 and 3. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#wait-for-active-automatically
- [definition] Recommended pattern — 1. Add the new `cloudflare_certificate_pack` resource with `wait_for_active_status = true` and run `terraform apply`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#recommended-pattern
- [definition] Let's Encrypt rate limit — Let's Encrypt limits new certificates to five per seven-day window for the same exact set of hostnames. Repeated rotations (for example, during testing or automation loops) can exhaust this limit and block further issuance for up to a week. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#lets-encrypt-rate-limit
- [definition] Pack stuck in Pending Validation — If a new pack remains in **Pending Validation** for more than 15 minutes, check that your DCV method is set up correctly. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#pack-stuck-in-pending-validation
- [definition] Distinction from custom certificate replacement — This page covers **ACM certificate packs** (Cloudflare-managed Domain Validated certificates ordered via Advanced Certificate Manager). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-rotation/#distinction-from-custom-certificate-replacement

- [definition] What can I update when my waiting room is actively queueing? — You can update a [waiting room's template](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/customize-waiting-room) and those changes will be visible to users in near-real time. We recommend these updates as a way to engage with users and provide updated information or expectations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#what-can-i-update-when-my-waiting-room-is-actively-queueing

- [definition] How does Waiting Room interact with other Cloudflare products? — Some Cloudflare products run before a waiting room acts on traffic: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#how-does-waiting-room-interact-with-other-cloudflare-products
- [definition] What happens if a user refreshes their tab when in a waiting room? — A manual tab refresh has no effect on a user's position in your waiting room. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#what-happens-if-a-user-refreshes-their-tab-when-in-a-waiting-room
- [definition] What happens if a queued user leaves the queue? — When a user joins the queue, they are placed into a bucket which is their general position in line. When a user leaves the queue (closes the browser or tab), their place in line is held for five minutes after the last refresh. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#what-happens-if-a-queued-user-leaves-the-queue
- [definition] Why do I observe a few users being queued in the dashboard? — Some users might be queued before your waiting room reaches is limit due to architectural designs. For more details on the behavior and how to fix it, refer to [​​Queueing activation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/monitor-waiting-room#queueing-activation). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#why-do-i-observe-a-few-users-being-queued-in-the-dashboard
- [definition] Why are some users not being queued in my waiting room? — If you notice users not being queued to your waiting room, make sure the path you defined exactly matches the path of your website. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#why-are-some-users-not-being-queued-in-my-waiting-room
- [definition] Why are users being blocked from entering my waiting room? — If you have Rate Limiting, check your [rate limiting rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#why-are-users-being-blocked-from-entering-my-waiting-room
- [definition] Why is the estimated wait time increasing for some users? — Estimated wait times may increase if the rate of users leaving your site decreases. The estimated wait time is updated upon each page refresh based on the most recently available information about the rate of slots opening up on your site and the number of users ahead of the user in line. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#why-is-the-estimated-wait-time-increasing-for-some-users
- [definition] Why is `new users per minute` low when there is capacity available? — The `new users per minute` metric tracks how many users were accepted to the origin in the last minute. It is only incremented when a queued user refreshes and is accepted to the origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#why-is-new-users-per-minute-low-when-there-is-capacity-available
- [definition] Why are my Waiting Room analytics and Google analytics not matching? — Waiting Room relies on a session cookie to count and keep track of active users. The duration for which a user is considered active depends on the waiting room configuration. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#why-are-my-waiting-room-analytics-and-google-analytics-not-matching
- [definition] Why did my traffic exceed the New Users Per Minute threshold? — Waiting Room is a distributed system, and achieving perfect global counting in real time is challenging due to the time required for state propagation across data centers worldwide. The budgeting logic is structured around both data center-specific and global budgets. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/troubleshooting/#why-did-my-traffic-exceed-the-new-users-per-minute-threshold

## Glossary
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#p — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/wait` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#on-this-page
- [parameter] downtime: Downtime is the duration during which a system, service, or equipment is not operational or unavailable for use. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] error page: An error page is a webpage shown to users when they try to access a specific webpage or resource that is unavailable due to a server error, broken link, or other issues. It typically includes details about the encountered error and offers potential solutions or guidance to help users navigate the problem. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] iFrame: An iFrame, short for Inline Frame, is an HTML element used to embed and display external content within a webpage, allowing the incorporation of another document or web page seamlessly within the main document. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] JSON-friendly: JSON-friendly refers to data or formats that are easily and naturally represented in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), a lightweight data interchange format, without requiring complex transformations or modifications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] legitimate traffic: Legitimate traffic refers to authorized and permissible network activity, data transmissions, or communications that adhere to established norms and rules within a given system or network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] non-browser traffic: Non-browser traffic refers to data exchanges and communication occurring between devices or systems that do not involve web browsers, such as a mobile app or web apps. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SEO crawlers: SEO crawlers, or web crawlers, are automated programs employed by search engines to systematically browse and index web content, gathering information about the structure and relevance of pages to determine search result rankings. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Set-Cookie: Set-Cookie is an HTTP header used by web servers to send a cookie to a user's browser during an HTTP response, enabling the server to store information on the client side, often used for session management and user preferences. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] traffic management: The process of controlling and optimizing the flow of network data to ensure efficient and reliable communication. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] virtual waiting room: A virtual waiting room is an online system or feature that manages and controls access to a website or service during periods of high traffic, preventing server overload by placing users in a queue until they can be accommodated, ensuring a more equitable and efficient user experience. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/glossary/#glossary

## Control user session settings
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/control-user-session/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/cont — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/wait` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/control-user-session/#on-this-page
- [definition] Control user session settings — Last updated Jun 30, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/control-user-session/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/control-user-session/#control-user-session-settings
- [definition] Session duration — Once on your site, a user is considered active as long as they make an HTTP request to any URL covered by your waiting room once every **session duration** minutes. Each new request restarts a user’s time to stay active equal to **session duration**. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/control-user-session/#session-duration
- [definition] Disable session renewal to limit browsing time — You can limit each user’s time on your site to only one session duration by checking the box next to Disable Session Renewal from the dashboard. Once a user has been active on your site for **session duration** minutes, if there is active queueing, that user will be sent to the back of the queue. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/control-user-session/#disable-session-renewal-to-limit-browsing-time
- [definition] Revoke a user’s session using origin commands — To terminate a user's session when they perform a specific action, you can send a command to the waiting room using an HTTP header on the response from your origin. This command tells the waiting room to revoke the session of the user associated with the current response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/control-user-session/#revoke-a-users-session-using-origin-commands

## Best practices
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/best-practices/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/b — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/wait` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/best-practices/#on-this-page

- [definition] Total active users — When specifying the **Total active users** in your [configuration settings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/configuration-settings/), set the value to `75%` of your origin's traffic capacity. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/best-practices/#total-active-users
- [definition] Page path — When setting the waiting room **Path** in your [configuration settings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/configuration-settings/), pay attention to potential subpaths. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/best-practices/#page-path
- [definition] Waiting room template — If you want to provide your users with updated information or expectations when they are queueing, Cloudflare recommends that you update your [waiting room template](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/how-to/customize-waiting-room/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/best-practices/#waiting-room-template
- [definition] Configuration settings — When users are actively queueing, only make changes to your [configuration settings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/configuration-settings/) when necessary. These changes may impact the estimated wait time shown to end users, which might lead to user confusion. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/best-practices/#configuration-settings
- [definition] Queueing method — Though you can change your [queueing method](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/), it may affect users if your waiting room is actively queueing: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/best-practices/#queueing-method
- [definition] Waiting Room and SEO — SEO crawlers may end up in a queue during active queueing. When this happens, your sites search results and SEO may be impacted. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/best-practices/#waiting-room-and-seo

## Queueing method
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/q — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/wait` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/#on-this-page
- [definition] Queueing method — Last updated Apr 16, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/#queueing-method
- [definition] First In First Out (FIFO) — Your waiting room orders visitors according to when they entered the waiting room. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/#first-in-first-out-fifo
- [definition] Random — When your application has open spots, your waiting room chooses visitors at random to exit the waiting room and enter your application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/#random
- [definition] Passthrough — Allow all traffic to pass immediately through your waiting room and into your application by setting its `queueing_method` to **passthrough**. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/#passthrough
- [definition] Reject — Prevent any traffic from reaching your application by setting its `queueing_method` to **reject**. Users will get a static page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/#reject
- [definition] Change queueing methods — Though you can change your [queueing method](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/), it may affect users if your waiting room is actively queueing: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waiting-room/reference/queueing-methods/#change-queueing-methods

- [definition] Why am I not seeing all the metrics for single-page application (SPA) or multiple-page application (MPA)? — Every route change that occurs in the single-page app will send the measurement of the route before the route is changed to the beacon endpoint. The measurement for the last route change will be sent whenever the user leaves the tab or closes the browser window. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#why-am-i-not-seeing-all-the-metrics-for-single-page-application-spa-or-multiple-page-application-mpa
- [definition] For the same site, why would I see more data reported with an automatic setup? — Unless you are using Rules to control which pages to be measured, using [automatic setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/get-started/#sites-proxied-through-cloudflare) will inject the JS snippet on all pages (sub-domains) under the zone. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#for-the-same-site-why-would-i-see-more-data-reported-with-an-automatic-setup
- [definition] My website is proxied through Cloudflare, but Web Analytic's automatic setup is not working. — If you have a `Cache-Control` header set to `public, no-transform`, Cloudflare proxy will not be able to modify the original payload of the website. Therefore, the Beacon script will not be automatically injected to your site, and Web Analytics will not work. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#my-website-is-proxied-through-cloudflare-but-web-analytics-automatic-setup-is-not-working
- [definition] Why am I getting a `405 Method Not Allowed` error from `/cdn-cgi/rum`? — The `/cdn-cgi/rum` endpoint only accepts `POST` requests for data ingestion. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#why-am-i-getting-a-405-method-not-allowed-error-from-cdn-cgirum
- [definition] Why am I seeing syntax errors from the beacon script in Internet Explorer? — Internet Explorer 11 was the final version of Internet Explorer and it was [declared completely end-of-life (EOL) in 2022 ↗](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/windows-itpro-blog/internet-explorer-11-desktop-app-retirement-faq/2366549). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#why-am-i-seeing-syntax-errors-from-the-beacon-script-in-internet-explorer
- [definition] I am proxying my site through Cloudflare. Should I manually add the JS beacon? — You can, but you do not have to. Cloudflare Web Analytics is designed primarily for customers who do not use Cloudflare's proxy to measure their web traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#i-am-proxying-my-site-through-cloudflare-should-i-manually-add-the-js-beacon
- [definition] Can I add Web Analytics to my site using a tag manager like Google Tag Manager (GTM)? — Yes. Instead of embedding the script using a tag manager as shown here: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#can-i-add-web-analytics-to-my-site-using-a-tag-manager-like-google-tag-manager-gtm
- [definition] What do I need to add to my Content Security Policy (CSP)? — If your site implements a Content Security Policy (CSP), you'll need to add some entries to this HTTP header to allow browsers to download the beacon script and transmit beacons to Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#what-do-i-need-to-add-to-my-content-security-policy-csp
- [definition] How can I enforce Subresource Integrity (SRI) with the JS beacon? — If you're using the automated injection (i.e. not the manually-embedded script approach mentioned above), Cloudflare automatically includes an `integrity` attribute in the `<script>`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#how-can-i-enforce-subresource-integrity-sri-with-the-js-beacon
- [definition] Can I use the same JS Snippet for a different domain? — No. However, if the apex domain (also known as "root domain" or "naked domain") is the same, you can use the same site tag. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#can-i-use-the-same-js-snippet-for-a-different-domain
- [definition] Can I use automatic setup with a DNS-only domain (CNAME setup)? — No, you can only use the [automatic setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/get-started/#sites-proxied-through-cloudflare) with JS snippet injection if traffic to your domain is proxied through Cloudflare (orange-clouded). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#can-i-use-automatic-setup-with-a-dns-only-domain-cname-setup
- [definition] What prevents the JS Snippet from being added to a page? — For Cloudflare to automatically add the JavaScript snippet, your pages need to have valid HTML. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#what-prevents-the-js-snippet-from-being-added-to-a-page
- [definition] Can I use Real User Monitoring (RUM) with Cloudflare Workers? — Cloudflare's Real User Monitoring (RUM) operates exclusively on the initial client request and cannot collect metrics from Worker subrequests. This is a fundamental architectural limitation designed to ensure accurate performance measurements and prevent duplicate or misleading analytics data. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#can-i-use-real-user-monitoring-rum-with-cloudflare-workers
- [definition] Is the data sampled? — We retain unsampled beacon data for the past 7 days, after this point data is aggregated down to around 10%. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#is-the-data-sampled
- [definition] Can I see server-side analytics by URL? — Web Analytics only displays client-side analytics. All Cloudflare customers who proxy their traffic also get analytics based on traffic at their edge. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#can-i-see-server-side-analytics-by-url
- [definition] What is the period of time I can access data in Web Analytics? — Currently, you can access data for the previous six months. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#what-is-the-period-of-time-i-can-access-data-in-web-analytics
- [definition] Does Cloudflare Web Analytics support UTM parameters? — Not yet. UTM parameters are special query string parameters that can help track where traffic is coming from. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#does-cloudflare-web-analytics-support-utm-parameters
- [definition] Does Web Analytics support custom events? — Not yet, but we may add support for this in the future. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#does-web-analytics-support-custom-events
- [definition] Can I track more than one website with Web Analytics? — Yes. Right now there is a soft limit of ten sites per account, but that can be adjusted by contacting Cloudflare support. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#can-i-track-more-than-one-website-with-web-analytics
- [definition] When does the beacon send metrics to the `/cdn-cgi/rum/` endpoint? — For traditional websites, not Single Page Applications (SPAs), the Web Analytics beacon reports to the `/cdn-cgi/rum/` endpoint when the page has finished loading (load event) and when the user leaves the page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/faq/#when-does-the-beacon-send-metrics-to-the-cdn-cgirum-endpoint

## Page load time
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metri — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#on-this-page
- [definition] Page load time — Last updated Apr 16, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#page-load-time
- [definition] Components — Below is a list of all the components you can inspect: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#components
- [definition] Page load — The total amount of time required to load the page. Note that page load time does not correspond to the sum of the other timings available in Web Analytics. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#page-load
- [definition] DNS (`domainLookupEnd` \- `domainLookupStart`) — How long a DNS query takes. This could appear as zero for reused connections or content stored in the local cache (memory or disk). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#dns-domainlookupend-domainlookupstart
- [definition] TCP (`connectEnd` \- `connectStart`) — How long it takes to establish a TCP connection with the server. If using HTTPS, this process includes TLS negotiation time. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#tcp-connectend-connectstart
- [definition] Request (`responseStart` \- `requestStart`) — The time elapsed between making an HTTP request and receiving the first byte of the response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#request-responsestart-requeststart
- [definition] Response (`responseEnd` \- `responseStart`) — The time elapsed between the first byte and the last byte of the received response. Think of this as a resource download time. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#response-responseend-responsestart
- [definition] Processing (`domComplete` \- `domInteractive`) — How long it took to render the page. This includes loading any resources that block page rendering, including images, scripts, and style sheets. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#processing-domcomplete-dominteractive
- [definition] Load Event (`loadEventEnd` \- `loadEventStart`) — An event triggered by the browser when a document and its resources finish loading. The Load Event duration may be a useful metric if you have additional functions or any logic for the load event. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#load-event-loadeventend-loadeventstart
- [definition] Data collected for Paint Timings — To make Web Analytics work, Cloudflare collects several types of data points. These are the additional data points collected for Paint Timings: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#data-collected-for-paint-timings
- [definition] First Paint — The time between navigation and when the browser renders the first pixels to the screen. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#first-paint
- [definition] First Contentful Paint — Time when the browser renders the first bit of content from the DOM. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/data-metrics/page-load-time-summary/#first-contentful-paint

## Interplanetary File System (IPFS)
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/concepts/ipfs/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/concep — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/concepts/ipfs/#on-this-page
- [definition] Interplanetary File System (IPFS) — Last updated May 1, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/concepts/ipfs/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/concepts/ipfs/#interplanetary-file-system-ipfs
- [definition] Content Identifiers — Every file added to IPFS is given a unique address derived from a hash of the file's content. This address is called a Content Identifier (CID). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/concepts/ipfs/#content-identifiers
- [definition] Uploading to IPFS — IPFS tracks which computers have which files using a [Distributed Hash Table (DHT) ↗](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distributed%5Fhash%5Ftable) — a lookup system that maps CIDs to the network addresses of computers hosting that content. No single computer holds the entire lookup table. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/concepts/ipfs/#uploading-to-ipfs
- [definition] Directories — You can upload more than just individual files. For example, consider a folder called `example`, which has exactly one file, `example_text.txt`, containing the string `I'm trying out IPFS`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/concepts/ipfs/#directories
- [definition] Related resources — For help with additional concepts, refer to the [IPFS ↗](https://docs.ipfs.tech/concepts/) documentation. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/concepts/ipfs/#related-resources

## Troubleshooting
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/>

- [snippet] The nodes with the requested content are not pinning it.: ipfs pin -r <content id> — `ipfs pin -r <content id>` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#the-nodes-with-the-requested-content-are-not-pinning-it
- [snippet] The nodes with the requested content are not pinning it.: ipfs dht provide -rv <content id> — `ipfs dht provide -rv <content id>` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#the-nodes-with-the-requested-content-are-not-pinning-it
- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubl — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#on-this-page
- [definition] Troubleshooting — Last updated May 5, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#troubleshooting
- [definition] No link named "ipfs" — If you get a `no link named "ipfs" under <<CID>>` error message when trying to access content through Cloudflare's IPFS gateway, that means you have created a gateway without a value for the [DNSLink](https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/concepts/dnslink). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#no-link-named-ipfs
- [definition] Check Cloudflare's status — It is worth checking for recent incidents on Cloudflare's [status dashboard ↗](https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/) that may have affected our gateway, but the best place to get up-to-date information about issues facing IPFS is the [IPFS Discussion Forum ↗](https://discuss.ipfs.io/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#check-cloudflares-status
- [definition] Generic IPFS — IPFS is still a developing protocol and content is often unavailable or slow to load for reasons outside of Cloudflare's control. Usually, this happens for one of the following reasons. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#generic-ipfs
- [definition] The content was uploaded to a free/anonymous pinning service. — Free and anonymous pinning services can often be used to get content on IPFS in a pinch, but they'll often stop pinning content soon after it's uploaded. Running your own server or using a pinning service are the recommended alternatives, and will keep your content online more reliably. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#the-content-was-uploaded-to-a-freeanonymous-pinning-service
- [definition] No node with the requested content is online. — Content will only stay on the IPFS network as long as there's at least one node that's serving it. If all of the nodes that were serving a given piece of content go offline, the content will be inaccessible until one of them comes back online. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#no-node-with-the-requested-content-is-online
- [definition] The nodes with the requested content are not publicly addressable. — It's common for people who run an IPFS node on their home Wi-Fi to have very long wait times or a high rate of request failure. This is because the rest of the nodes in the IPFS network have difficulty connecting to them through their NAT (Internet router). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#the-nodes-with-the-requested-content-are-not-publicly-addressable
- [definition] The nodes with the requested content are not pinning it. — If several minutes have passed since files were uploaded to an IPFS node and they're still not discoverable by other gateways, it's possible the node is having trouble announcing the files to the rest of the network. You can make sure the node with the content has pinned it by running: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#the-nodes-with-the-requested-content-are-not-pinning-it
- [definition] The nodes with the requested content are too old. — IPFS issues mandatory updates from time to time that introduce breaking protocol changes. Cloudflare tries to say ahead of these updates and may, as a result, lose connectivity with older nodes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ipfs-gateway/troubleshooting/#the-nodes-with-the-requested-content-are-too-old

## Ethereum network
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/ethereum/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/co — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/ethereum/#on-this-page
- [definition] Ethereum network — Last updated May 1, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/ethereum/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/ethereum/#ethereum-network
- [definition] Smart contracts — Running a smart contract requires paying a fee in Ethereum's currency, ETH. This fee (called "gas") compensates the network's validators for the computational work of executing your transaction and adding it to the blockchain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/ethereum/#smart-contracts
- [definition] Addressing — Transactions are grouped into blocks, and blocks are chained together in sequence to form the blockchain — a complete history of every transaction since the network started. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/ethereum/#addressing
- [definition] Read and write content — To read data from Ethereum — such as checking account balances or querying smart contract state — you need access to an Ethereum node. You can run a node yourself (for example, using [go-ethereum ↗](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/)) or use a gateway like Cloudflare's. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/ethereum/#read-and-write-content
- [definition] Connect your website to the gateway — To access the Ethereum network from a custom domain name — without running your own node — you can [create an Ethereum Gateway](https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/how-to/manage-gateways/#create-a-gateway) through Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/ethereum/#connect-your-website-to-the-gateway
- [definition] Related resources — If you’re interested in learning more, you can read the official [RPC documentation ↗](https://github.com/ethereum/wiki/wiki/JSON-RPC), along with the official documentation [provided by Ethereum ↗](https://www.ethereum.org/use/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/ethereum/#related-resources

## Node types
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/node-types/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/co — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/node-types/#on-this-page
- [definition] Node types — Last updated May 1, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/node-types/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/node-types/#node-types
- [definition] Full nodes — Full nodes store the current state of the blockchain and validate new blocks as they are produced. Once fully synced with the network, a full node can answer queries about any current blockchain data. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/node-types/#full-nodes
- [definition] Light nodes — Light nodes store only block headers (summaries of each block) rather than the full blockchain state. They can query the Ethereum network but rely on full nodes to provide and verify the underlying data. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/node-types/#light-nodes
- [definition] Archive nodes — Archive nodes are full nodes that also store every historical state of the blockchain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/node-types/#archive-nodes
- [definition] Nodes at Cloudflare — Cloudflare's Ethereum Gateway provides access to full and archive nodes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/web3/ethereum-gateway/concepts/node-types/#nodes-at-cloudflare

- [definition] Sequence building — A sequence is a time-ordered list of HTTP API requests made by a specific visitor as they browse a website, use a mobile app, or interact with a B2B partner via API. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/security/sequence-analytics/#sequence-building
- [definition] Sequence scoring — API Shield scores sequences by a metric called precedence score. Sequence Analytics displays sequences by the highest precedence score. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/security/sequence-analytics/#sequence-scoring

- [definition] Repeated sequences — Real-world API usage shows many successively repeated operations. To facilitate exploration, Sequence Analytics collapses successively repeated operations into one. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/security/sequence-analytics/#repeated-sequences
- [definition] Availability — Sequence Analytics is available for all API Shield customers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/security/sequence-analytics/#availability

- [definition] Time limitations — Sequence mitigation rules have a lookback period of 10 minutes. - [definition] Availability — Sequence mitigation is currently in a closed beta and is only available for Enterprise customers. If you would like to be included in the beta, contact your account team. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/security/sequence-mitigation/#availability

## Glossary
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/#pag — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/#on-this-page
- [parameter] API call: Also known as an API request. An API call is a message sent to a server asking an API to provide a service or information. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] API endpoint: The API endpoint is the location where API calls or requests are fulfilled. API Shield defines endpoints as a host, method, and path tuple. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] API schema: The API schema defines which API requests are valid based on several request properties like target endpoint, path or query variable format, and HTTP method. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] session identifier: A session identifier is a unique identifier that a website assigns to identify a specific user for the duration of their visit. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] source endpoint: The source endpoint is the endpoint managed by API Shield in Endpoint Management by its routing feature. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] target endpoint: The target endpoint is the ultimate destination that a request is sent to by API Shield's routing feature. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/#glossary
- [definition] Glossary — Last updated Apr 15, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/api-shield/glossary/#glossary

## Account Abuse Protection (Early Access)
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/account-abuse-protection/>

- [parameter] cf.fraud.email\_risk: Analyzes the randomness (entropy) of characters in an email username and top level domain. For example, a8xk2m9p@example.com has high entropy (very random characters), while john.smith@example.com has low entropy (recognizable pattern). High risk emails indicate high entropy, while medium and low risk emails indicate less randomness in the string of characters. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/account-abuse-protection/#suspicious-emails
- [parameter] cf.fraud\_detection.disposable\_domain: Description=Flags whether a domain for a given email is included in a known list of temporary email providers.; Values=True or False — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/account-abuse-protection/#security-rules
- [parameter] cf.fraud.email\_risk: Description=Measures risk of email based on randomness of characters in the username and domain.; Values=Low represents low risk due to reduced randomness and simple emails. Medium represents medium risk based on larger strings with slightly more randomness. High represents high risk based on larger and random character strings. Unknown — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/account-abuse-protection/#security-rules

## Glossary
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#page","he — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#on-this-page
- [parameter] bot: A software application programmed to do tasks that can be used for good (chatbots, search engine crawlers) or for evil (inventory hoarding, credential stuffing). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] bot score: A score from 1 to 99 that indicates how likely that request came from a bot, in which 1 to 29 is likely automated and 30 to 99 is likely human. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] bot tags: Additional information about a bot request, such as why Cloudflare has given it a bot score and whether the request came from a verified bot or a category of verified bots. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Challenge solve rate (CSR): The percentage of issued challenges that were solved. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] detection ID: Static rules that are used to detect predictable bot behavior with no overlap with human traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] direct: A label applied to a verified bot or agent operated by a single, narrow operator, usually on the operator's own infrastructure. Replaces the standalone "verified bot" classification used before July 1, 2026. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] intermediary: A label applied to a verified agent that a wide range of end users can operate, such as a browser-use or agentic service. Replaces the "signed agent" classification used before July 1, 2026. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] JA3 fingerprint: JA3 and JA4 fingerprints profile specific SSL/TLS clients across different destination IPs, Ports, and X509 certificates. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] signed agent: A deprecated classification (retired July 1, 2026) for end-user-controlled agents that self-identify with Web Bot Auth. These agents are now verified bots labeled as intermediary. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] verified bot: A bot or agent that Cloudflare has confirmed is transparent about who it is and what it does: it represents itself honestly and does not abuse the access that honesty earns. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary
- [definition] Glossary — Last updated Apr 15, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/glossary/#glossary

- [change] 2026-07-01: **New options to manage AI traffic** All customers can now manage AI crawlers by behavior — [Search, Agent, and Training](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot/#ai-bots) — instead of a single Block AI bots toggle. Configure these options from [Block AI Bots](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/additional-configurations/block-ai-bots/). New defaults, in which Training… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/changelog/#2026-07-01
- [change] 2026-07-01: **BotBase and Attribution Business Insights for Enterprise Bot Management** Enterprise Bot Management customers can now use [BotBase](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/botbase/), a searchable directory of all tracked bots and agents with their behavior classification and detection IDs, and [Attribution Business… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/changelog/#2026-07-01
- [change] 2025-07-02: **Managed robots.txt will prepend existing files** Cloudflare will prepend our managed `robots.txt` before your existing `robots.txt`, combining both into a single response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/changelog/#2025-07-02
- [change] 2025-06-26: **Web Bot Auth is now available for bot verification** Web Bot Auth is an authentication method that leverages cryptographic signatures in HTTP messages to verify that a request comes from an automated bot. This provides a more robust way of verifying bots. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/changelog/#2025-06-26

Bot settings do not support compound conditions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/additional-configurations/custom-rules/#conditional-logic
- [definition] Custom actions — Bot settings offer **Block**, **Managed Challenge**, and **Allow** as actions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/additional-configurations/custom-rules/#custom-actions

- [definition] Forwarding bot data to origin — To send bot scores, verified bot status, or JA3/JA4 fingerprints to your origin server, use [Transform Rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/rules/transform/) (including [Managed Transforms](https://developers.cloudflare.com/rules/transform/managed-transforms/)) or… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/additional-configurations/custom-rules/#forwarding-bot-data-to-origin
- [definition] Execution order — Custom rules execute before Super Bot Fight Mode managed rules. If a custom rule takes a terminating action (such as _Block_ or _Managed Challenge_), the request does not reach bot settings. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/additional-configurations/custom-rules/#execution-order

- [definition] Heuristics — The **Heuristics** engine processes all requests. Cloudflare conducts a number of heuristic checks to identify automated traffic, and requests are matched against a growing database of malicious fingerprints. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-detection-engines/#heuristics
- [definition] JavaScript detections — The [**JavaScript Detections (JSD)**](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/additional-configurations/javascript-detections/) engine identifies headless browsers and other malicious fingerprints. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-detection-engines/#javascript-detections
- [definition] Machine Learning (Business and Enterprise) — The **Machine Learning (ML)** engine accounts for the majority of all detections, distinguishing between human and bot traffic. - [definition] Notes on detection — Cloudflare uses the `__cf_bm` cookie to smooth out the bot score and reduce false positives for actual user sessions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-detection-engines/#notes-on-detection

- [definition] Machine learning — Catches sophisticated bots by analyzing request features across billions of daily requests. Produces most scores between 2 and 99. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-score/#machine-learning
- [definition] Anomaly detection — Detects outlier requests by comparing traffic against a learned baseline for your specific site. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-score/#anomaly-detection
- [definition] JavaScript detections — Catches headless browsers (browsers controlled by software, with no visible window or human operator) and other automation tools. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-score/#javascript-detections
- [definition] Not computed — A bot score of 0 means Bot Management did not evaluate the request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-score/#not-computed
- [definition] Notes on detection — Cloudflare uses the `__cf_bm` cookie to smooth out the bot score and reduce false positives for actual user sessions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-score/#notes-on-detection

Create a content security rule with the Log action — When you create a content security rule with the [_Log_ action](https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/rules/#rule-actions), Cloudflare logs any resources not covered by the rule, without blocking any resources. Use this action to validate a new rule before deploying it. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/get-started/#41-create-a-content-security-rule-with-the-log-action
- [definition] 4.2\. Review rule violations — Resources not covered by the content security rule you created will be reported as [rule violations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/rules/violations/). After some time, review the list of rule violations to make sure the rule is correct. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/get-started/#42-review-rule-violations
- [definition] 4.3\. Change rule action to Allow — Once you have verified that your content security rule is correct, change the rule action from _Log_ to _Allow_. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/get-started/#43-change-rule-action-to-allow
- [definition] Footnotes — 1. A positive security model is one that defines what is allowed and rejects everything else. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/get-started/#footnotes

- [snippet] I get warnings in my browser's developer tools related to Content Security Policy (CSP): [Report Only] Refused to execute inline script because it violates — `[Report Only] Refused to execute inline script because it violates` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#i-get-warnings-in-my-browsers-developer-tools-related-to-content-security-policy-csp
- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/tro — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clie` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#on-this-page
- [parameter] Client-side security manages all CSP headers: Do not create Response Header Transform Rules for CSP headers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#recommended-patterns
- [parameter] Transform Rule manages all CSP headers: Use **Set static** or **Set dynamic** operations, and consider excluding the affected paths from your content security rule. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#recommended-patterns
- [parameter] Different CSP headers for different paths: Use content security rule conditions to target specific paths, and avoid overlapping Transform Rules. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#recommended-patterns
- [definition] Troubleshooting — Last updated Jul 2, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#troubleshooting
- [definition] Cloudflare does not show any client-side resources after activation — Cloudflare does not collect data on every single page view. Instead, it uses a sampling approach to gather information efficiently. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#cloudflare-does-not-show-any-client-side-resources-after-activation
- [definition] The dashboard shows scripts and connections that I do not recognize — Scripts often reference other scripts outside your application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#the-dashboard-shows-scripts-and-connections-that-i-do-not-recognize
- [definition] I get warnings in my browser's developer tools related to Content Security Policy (CSP) — Cloudflare uses a Content Security Policy (CSP) report-only directive to gather a list of all scripts running on your application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#i-get-warnings-in-my-browsers-developer-tools-related-to-content-security-policy-csp
- [definition] Redirects to other domains — Rule violations reported via CSP's [report-only directive](https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/reference/csp-header/) do not take into consideration any redirects or redirect HTTP status codes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#redirects-to-other-domains
- [definition] Ad-blocking browser extensions — If the violation reports reference domains that belong to user consent management or behavioral tracking services, an ad-blocking browser extension installed on the visitor's browser is a likely cause. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#ad-blocking-browser-extensions
- [definition] I get scoped alerts for hostnames I do not manage on a SaaS root zone — If you operate an [SSL for SaaS](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-for-platforms/cloudflare-for-saas/) root zone with custom hostnames, and you configured a [scoped alert](https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/alerts/#scoped-alerts) with a content security rule that… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#i-get-scoped-alerts-for-hostnames-i-do-not-manage-on-a-saas-root-zone
- [definition] My rule is not triggering (CSP header not added) — If you have configured a content security rule but the expected CSP header is not being added to responses, [Transform Rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/rules/transform/) may be rewriting the request path before the content security rule is evaluated. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#my-rule-is-not-triggering-csp-header-not-added
- [definition] Solution — To fix this issue, choose one of the following approaches: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#solution
- [definition] Responses contain duplicate CSP headers — If responses have duplicate `Content-Security-Policy` or `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` headers, this is likely caused by having both client-side security and a [response header transform rule](https://developers.cloudflare.com/rules/transform/response-header-modification/) adding the same… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#responses-contain-duplicate-csp-headers
- [definition] Solution — If you need to use Response Header Transform Rules alongside client-side security policies, use the **Set static** or **Set dynamic** operations. These operations replace any existing header value, including headers added by Cloudflare's client-side security. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/troubleshooting/#solution

This enhancement specifically helps reduce the false positive rate of our detection engines, focusing your attention on true… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2026-03-03

Scripts with false positive classification may have a different pattern than the previous model deployment. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2025-10-08

This allows you to simulate an end-to-end workflow before switching your policies to [allow mode](https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/rules/#rule-actions). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2025-09-12
- [change] 2025-05-20: **Updated machine learning (ML) model** The latest ML model has been deployed to all Page Shield add-on customers with better classification precision. Scripts with false positive classification may have a different pattern than the previous model deployment. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2025-05-20
- [change] 2025-05-09: **Reports from browser extension injected resources are filtered out** Script and connection reports caused by browser extension injections are now filtered out, helping you focus on managing application dependencies. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2025-05-09
- [change] 2024-12-02: **Alerts based on customer-defined policies** You can now scope all of Page Shield's alert types to selected zones and their associated policies, alerting only on the resources that have been explicitly allowed. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2024-12-02
- [change] 2024-09-30: **New machine learning (ML) scores for detected scripts** In addition to the global integrity score, Page Shield now provides individual script scores (from 1 to 99) for the following malicious code detections: Magecart, Crypto mining, and Malware. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2024-09-30
- [change] 2024-09-18: **Page Shield's script monitor now available in Free plan** The Page Shield's script monitor feature is now available to all users, including users in the Free plan. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2024-09-18
- [change] 2024-09-18: **Page Shield policy changes now available in audit logs** Cloudflare [Audit Logs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/account/account-security/review-audit-logs/) now include entries for any changes to Page Shield's policies. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2024-09-18
- [change] 2024-06-18: **Cookie Monitor now available** Page Shield now captures HTTP cookies set and used by your web application. The [list of detected cookies](https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/detection/monitor-connections-scripts/) in available in the Cloudflare dashboard or via API. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2024-06-18
- [change] 2024-06-14: **Added filter operators for scripts and connections** You can now filter scripts and connections in the Cloudflare dashboard using the `does not contain` operator. Pages associated with scripts and connections can be filtered by `includes`, `starts with`, and `ends with`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2024-06-14
- [change] 2024-04-26: **Suggestions for the default directive** When creating a policy in the dashboard, default directive aggregates suggestions of monitored scripts and connections data, enabling defining default directive easier. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2024-04-26
- [change] 2024-04-04: **Individual threat intelligence categories** Instead of aggregating categories of URL and domain data from threat intelligence, they are now listed per type. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/client-side-security/release-notes/#2024-04-04
- [change] 2024-03-21: **Increase allowed length per policy** Now each policy supports up to 6,000 characters. - [parameter] High threat score: IP addresses with a high-risk score trigger Challenges. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#challenges-on-cloudflare-protected-sites
- [parameter] IP reputation: If your IP has a history of suspicious activity, it may be flagged. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#challenges-on-cloudflare-protected-sites
- [parameter] Bot detection: Automated traffic resembling bots is filtered by Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#challenges-on-cloudflare-protected-sites
- [parameter] Web Application Firewall (WAF) custom rules: Site owners may set rules targeting specific regions or user agents. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#challenges-on-cloudflare-protected-sites
- [parameter] Browser Integrity Check: Cloudflare verifies that browsers meet certain standards. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#challenges-on-cloudflare-protected-sites

- [definition] Troubleshooting — Last updated May 5, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#troubleshooting
- [definition] Proxied hostnames — If your hostname is proxied through Cloudflare, visitors may experience challenges on your webpages. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#proxied-hostnames
- [definition] Deprecated browser support — Challenges are not supported by Microsoft Internet Explorer. If you are currently using Internet Explorer, try using another modern web browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#deprecated-browser-support
- [definition] Referer header — Your visitor's HTTP request contains a referer header set to the website that they came from. When they encounter and solve a Challenge Page, the request with the referer is sent to the origin, and the response to the request is served to the user. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#referer-header
- [definition] Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) preflight requests — Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) preflight requests, or `OPTIONS`, exclude user credentials that include cookies. As a result, the `cf_clearance` cookie will not be sent with the request, causing it to fail to bypass a Challenge Page (Non-interactive, Managed, or Interactive Challenge). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#cross-origin-resource-sharing-cors-preflight-requests
- [definition] Challenges on Cloudflare-protected sites — Cloudflare issues challenges to website visitors to protect against malicious activity, such as bot attacks and DDoS attempts. If a legitimate human visitor is unexpectedly challenged, the reason typically stems from a security feature flagging their request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#challenges-on-cloudflare-protected-sites
- [definition] Allowlist traffic from mitigation actions — If you need to prevent a **Block** or **Challenge** action from being applied to specific requests, such as known search engine crawlers, monitoring services, or internal APIs, you must configure an exclusion using [WAF custom rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/custom-rules/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/troubleshooting/#allowlist-traffic-from-mitigation-actions

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/ch — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/#on-this-page
- [definition] Interstitial Challenge Pages — Last updated Jul 6, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/#interstitial-challenge-pages
- [definition] Actions — The following challenge types are the available actions when you create a WAF rule for a Challenge Page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/#actions
- [definition] Non-Interactive Challenges — With a Non-Interactive Challenge, Cloudflare makes the determination on whether or not the visitor is automated based on the limited information attained from their browser signals via an injected JavaScript. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/#non-interactive-challenges
- [definition] Managed Challenges — Managed Challenges are where Cloudflare dynamically chooses the appropriate type of challenge served to the visitor based on the characteristics of a request from the signals indicated by their browser. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/#managed-challenges
- [definition] Interactive Challenges — Interactive Challenge Pages require a visitor to interact with the challenge to pass. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/#interactive-challenges
- [definition] Compatibility limitations — Challenge Pages interrupt the request flow by returning a full HTML page for the user's browser to render and solve. This mechanism fails when the browser expects a non-HTML response, such as an AJAX or XHR (fetch) request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/#compatibility-limitations

- [parameter] advanced: Rules related to features available to Enterprise customers, such as [Adaptive DDoS Protection](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/managed-rulesets/adaptive-protection/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/managed-rulesets/network/rule-categories/#rule-categories
- [parameter] generic: Rules for detecting and mitigating floods of packets. These rules rate-limit traffic by default, but you can override them to block… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/managed-rulesets/network/rule-categories/#rule-categories
- [parameter] read-only: Highly targeted rules for mitigating DDoS attacks with a high confidence rate. These rules are read-only — you cannot override their sensitivity level or action. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/managed-rulesets/network/rule-categories/#rule-categories
- [parameter] test: Rules used for testing the detection, mitigation, and alerting capabilities of Cloudflare's DDoS protection products. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/managed-rulesets/network/rule-categories/#rule-categories

## FAQ
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequent — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#on-this-page
- [definition] FAQ — Last updated Apr 15, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#faq
- [definition] What is a DDoS attack event? — When Cloudflare's DDoS systems detect and mitigate attacks, they drop, rate-limit, or challenge (as applicable) packets, DNS queries, or HTTP requests, based on the type of attack. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#what-is-a-ddos-attack-event
- [definition] How does Cloudflare protect against "low and slow" DDoS attacks? — A [low and slow DDoS attack ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/ddos/ddos-low-and-slow-attack/) is most commonly a non-volumetric attack. The attacker will send a low volume of HTTP requests, and do so slowly. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#how-does-cloudflare-protect-against-low-and-slow-ddos-attacks
- [definition] How does Cloudflare deal with SSL/TLS negotiation attacks or floods? — SSL/TLS based attacks such as BEAST, Poodle, and CRIME are mitigated by Cloudflare's TLS settings, configuration, and cipher limitations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#how-does-cloudflare-deal-with-ssltls-negotiation-attacks-or-floods
- [definition] Does Cloudflare use BGP Flowspec for upstream mitigation? — Yes. Using our anycast network, along with Traffic Manager, Unimog, and Plurimog, we conduct automated traffic engineering to spread the load of traffic (legitimate and attack) to ensure our network is performant, especially during mitigation of large attacks. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#does-cloudflare-use-bgp-flowspec-for-upstream-mitigation
- [definition] Where can I see latest DDoS trends? — Cloudflare publishes quarterly DDoS reports and coverage of significant DDoS attacks. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#where-can-i-see-latest-ddos-trends
- [definition] What is the Ping of Death DDoS attacks? — The Ping of Death (PoD) attack involves sending malformed or oversized packets to another computer or server, which can cause the system to freeze, crash, or reboot. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#what-is-the-ping-of-death-ddos-attacks
- [definition] What are LOIC and HOIC? — LOIC is a popular network stress testing and DoS attack application that is used to flood a server with TCP, UDP, or HTTP requests with the intention of disrupting the service. It is known for its simplicity and ability to be used by individuals with minimal hacking experience. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#what-are-loic-and-hoic
- [definition] Can I exclude specific user agents from HTTP DDoS protection? — Yes, you can create an [override](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/managed-rulesets/http/http-overrides/override-expressions/) and use the expression fields to match against HTTP requests with the user agent. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#can-i-exclude-specific-user-agents-from-http-ddos-protection
- [definition] Does Cloudflare charge for DDoS attack traffic? — No. Since 2017, Cloudflare offers [free, unmetered, and unlimited DDoS protection ↗](https://blog.cloudflare.com/unmetered-mitigation/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#does-cloudflare-charge-for-ddos-attack-traffic
- [definition] How does DDoS Protection determine whether a SYN flood attack is mitigated by `dosd` or Advanced TCP Protection? — DDoS [managed rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/managed-rulesets/) detect and mitigate attacks by finding commonality between attack packets and generating a real-time fingerprint to mitigate the attack. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#how-does-ddos-protection-determine-whether-a-syn-flood-attack-is-mitigated-by-dosd-or-advanced-tcp-protection
- [definition] How does Cloudflare handle hyper-localized DDoS attacks that may aim to overwhelm a specific Point of Presence (PoP)? — Hyper-localized DDoS attacks are attacks that target specific PoPs or data centers from botnet nodes that are close to those locations in an attempt to overwhelm them and cause an outage or service disruptions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#how-does-cloudflare-handle-hyper-localized-ddos-attacks-that-may-aim-to-overwhelm-a-specific-point-of-presence-pop
- [definition] Global Anycast Network — Anycast allows multiple servers (PoPs) to share the same IP address, and the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routing system ensures user traffic is routed to the nearest or lowest-cost node. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#global-anycast-network
- [definition] Intelligent Traffic Engineering — Cloudflare uses real-time data and intelligence systems to make decisions about traffic routing, load balancing, and congestion management. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#intelligent-traffic-engineering
- [definition] Real-Time DDoS Mitigation — DDoS managed rules and Advanced DDoS Protection are autonomous and run on every single server independently, while also coordinating locally and globally, contributing to the resilience of each server and PoP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#real-time-ddos-mitigation
- [definition] What is Advanced TCP Protection's Protected Learning functionality? — The Protected Learning functionality enables the [Advanced TCP Protection](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/advanced-ddos-systems/overview/advanced-tcp-protection/) system to overcome Internet routing chaos while allowing your legitimate traffic through and blocking DDoS attacks… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#what-is-advanced-tcp-protections-protected-learning-functionality
- [definition] Does DDoS Protection protect against email-based attacks? — No. Cloudflare DDoS Protection safeguards web and network infrastructure against DDoS attacks at layers 3, 4, and 7 of the OSI model. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ddos-protection/frequently-asked-questions/#does-ddos-protection-protect-against-email-based-attacks
