- [definition] Cloudflare Access policy actions — Actions let you grant or deny permission to a certain user or user group. You can set only one action per policy. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#cloudflare-access-policy-actions
- [definition] Allow — The Allow action in Cloudflare Access allows users that meet certain criteria to reach an application behind Access. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#allow
- [definition] Block — The Block action in Cloudflare Access prevents users who meet certain criteria from reaching an application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#block
- [definition] Bypass — The Bypass action in Cloudflare Access disables Access enforcement for specific traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#bypass
- [definition] Service Auth — Service Auth rules in Cloudflare Access enforce authentication flows that do not require an identity provider IdP login, such as service tokens and mutual TLS. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#service-auth
- [definition] Cloudflare Access rule types — Rule types work like logical operators and determine how your criteria are combined to evaluate a user. All Access policies must contain at least one Include rule. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#cloudflare-access-rule-types
- [definition] Include — The Include rule in Cloudflare Access is similar to an OR logical operator. In case more than one Include rule is specified, users need to meet only one of the criteria. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#include
- [definition] Exclude — The Exclude rule in Cloudflare Access works like a NOT logical operator. A user meeting any Exclusion criteria will not be allowed access to the application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#exclude
- [definition] Require — The Require rule in Cloudflare Access works like an AND logical operator. A user must meet all specified Require rules to be allowed access. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#require
- [definition] Cloudflare Access selectors — When you add a rule to your Cloudflare Access policy, you will be asked to specify the criteria, or attributes, you want users to meet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#cloudflare-access-selectors
- [definition] Connection context in Cloudflare Access — Connection context settings allow you to control how users interact with an application after they have been granted access. While [selectors](#selectors) determine who can access an application, connection context settings determine what actions users can take during their session. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#connection-context-in-cloudflare-access
- [definition] Cloudflare Access policy order of execution — Cloudflare Access policies are evaluated based on their action type and order you set. Bypass and Service Auth policies are evaluated first, from top to bottom as shown in the UI. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#cloudflare-access-policy-order-of-execution
- [definition] Common Cloudflare Access misconfigurations — If you add any of the following rules to an Allow policy, anyone will be able to access your application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#common-cloudflare-access-misconfigurations
- [definition] Include everyone — The following table shows a Cloudflare Access policy that includes everyone: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#include-everyone
- [definition] Include all valid emails — The following table shows a Cloudflare Access policy that includes all users with valid email login methods: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#include-all-valid-emails
- [definition] Additional Cloudflare Access resources — [API and Terraform](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/api-terraform/) provide programmatic ways to manage your Access policies and configurations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/#additional-cloudflare-access-resources

- [parameter] \*.example.com: Covers=alpha.example.com beta.example.com; Does not cover=example.com foo.bar.example.com — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#match-all-subdomains-of-an-apex-domain
- [parameter] example.com  or example.com/\*: Covers=example.com example.com/alpha example.com/beta; Does not cover=alpha.example.com — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#match-all-paths-of-an-apex-domain
- [parameter] \*.test.example.com: Covers=alpha.test.example.com beta.test.example.com; Does not cover=test.example.com example.com — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#match-multi-level-subdomains
- [parameter] \*test.example.com: Covers=test.example.com alphatest.example.com; Does not cover=beta.test.example.com — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#partially-match-subdomains
- [parameter] example.com/alpha/\*: Covers=example.com/alpha/one example.com/alpha/two; Does not cover=example.com/alpha example.com — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#match-multi-level-paths
- [parameter] example.com/foo\*/bar: example.com/foo/bar example.com/food/bar example.com/food/stuff/bar — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#partially-match-paths
- [definition] Application paths — Last updated Apr 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#application-paths
- [definition] Policy inheritance — Cloudflare Zero Trust allows you to create unique rules for parts of an application that share a root path. Imagine an example application is deployed at `dashboard.com/eng` that anyone on the engineering team should be able to access. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#policy-inheritance
- [definition] Wildcards — When you create an application for a specific subdomain or path, you can use asterisks (`*`) as wildcards. Wildcards allow you to extend the application you are creating to multiple subdomains or paths in a given apex domain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#wildcards
- [definition] Subdomain setups — [Subdomain setups](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/subdomain-setup/) allow you to manage a child domain separately from its parent domain. In Access application paths, your configured child domains will appear in the **Domain** dropdown menu. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#subdomain-setups
- [definition] Port numbers — Port numbers are not supported in Access application paths. If a request includes a port number in the URL, Access will strip the port number and redirect the request to the default HTTP/HTTPS port. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#port-numbers
- [definition] Query strings — Query strings (such as`?foo=bar`) are not supported in Access application paths. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#query-strings
- [definition] Anchor links — Since anchor links are processed by the browser and not the server, Access applications do not support `#` characters in the URL. For example, requests to `dashboard.com/#settings` will redirect to `dashboard.com`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/app-paths/#anchor-links

- [definition] Identity provider-based MFA — You can require that users log in with specific MFA methods provided by their identity provider. For example, you can create rules that only allow users to reach a given application if they authenticate with a security key through their IdP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/mfa-requirements/#identity-provider-based-mfa
- [definition] Authentication methods in the JWT — When users authenticate with their identity provider, the IdP shares their username with Cloudflare Access. - [definition] Independent MFA — Independent MFA prompts users for a second factor directly in Access. This allows you to enforce MFA requirements without relying on your IdP's MFA configuration. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/mfa-requirements/#independent-mfa
- [definition] Prerequisites — Before you configure independent MFA on applications or policies, you must [turn on independent MFA](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/access-settings/independent-mfa/) at the organization level. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/mfa-requirements/#prerequisites
- [definition] Configure independent MFA for a policy — Each policy has the same three MFA options described in [Configure independent MFA for an application](#configure-independent-mfa-for-an-application). Policy-level settings override application-level settings. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/mfa-requirements/#configure-independent-mfa-for-a-policy
- [definition] MFA session duration — The MFA session duration determines how long a successful MFA authentication remains valid. After the MFA session expires, the user must complete MFA again on their next Cloudflare Access login in addition to completing IdP authentication. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/mfa-requirements/#mfa-session-duration
- [definition] Infrastructure applications — Infrastructure applications that use SSH support two infrastructure-only MFA methods. `piv_key` uses an enrolled Personal Identity Verification (PIV) key. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/mfa-requirements/#infrastructure-applications
- [definition] Configure MFA for an infrastructure application — Select PIV key, FIDO2 key, or both when configuring custom MFA. - [definition] Configure MFA for an infrastructure policy — You can set different MFA requirements for different SSH usernames by configuring MFA at the policy level. Policy-level MFA settings override application-level settings. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/mfa-requirements/#configure-mfa-for-an-infrastructure-policy
- [definition] MFA session duration for SSH — The MFA session duration determines how long users can open new SSH connections without another MFA prompt. Set the duration to `0m` to require MFA for every new connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/mfa-requirements/#mfa-session-duration-for-ssh
- [definition] Precedence and conflict resolution — MFA configuration is evaluated from most specific to least specific: **policy** \> **application** \> **organization**. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/mfa-requirements/#precedence-and-conflict-resolution

## Troubleshoot Access
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-co — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#on-this-page
- [definition] Troubleshoot Access — Last updated Apr 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#troubleshoot-access
- [definition] AJAX/CORS errors — Cloudflare Access requires that the `credentials: same-origin` parameter be added to JavaScript when using the Fetch API to include cookies. AJAX requests fail if this parameter is missing, resulting in an error such as `No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is present on the requested resource`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#ajaxcors-errors
- [definition] SAML verification failure — The error `SAML Verify: Invalid SAML response, SAML Verify: No certificate selected to verify` occurs when the identity provider (IdP) does not include the signing public key in the SAML response. Cloudflare Access requires the public key to match the **Signing certificate** uploaded to Zero Trust. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#saml-verification-failure
- [definition] Identity provider user/group info error — The error `Failed to fetch user/group information from the identity provider` occurs when Cloudflare lacks the necessary API permissions to communicate with your IdP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#identity-provider-usergroup-info-error
- [definition] Google Workspace redirect loop — If you place your Google Workspace behind Access, you cannot use Google or Google Workspace as an identity provider for that application. This creates an infinite redirect cycle because both systems depend on each other to complete the login. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#google-workspace-redirect-loop
- [definition] Invalid session error — The error `Invalid session. Please try logging in again` indicates that Access was unable to validate your `CF_Session` cookie. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#invalid-session-error
- [definition] Firefox Private Window — Firefox's default tracking prevention in Private Windows may prevent the `CF_authorization` cookie from being sent, especially for XHR requests. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#firefox-private-window
- [definition] Workers routes on the login path — If you have a Cloudflare Worker route assigned to your application's login path, the Worker may overwrite the `cf-authorization` cookie. To prevent this, ensure your Worker script does not modify or strip the `Set-Cookie` header for Access cookies. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#workers-routes-on-the-login-path
- [definition] OTP email not received — If a user does not receive a one-time PIN (OTP) email: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#otp-email-not-received
- [definition] OTP code already used — The error `This One-Time PIN has already been used` occurs when the OTP code has already been redeemed before the user enters it. OTP codes are single-use and expire 10 minutes after the initial request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#otp-code-already-used
- [definition] Google Super Admin login — If you use Access as the SSO provider for your Google Workspace, Google Super Admins cannot sign in via Access when accessing `admin.google.com`. Google requires Super Admins to use their original Google password to ensure they can always access the admin console. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#google-super-admin-login
- [definition] Missing SAML attributes — If you receive a `Required attributes are missing` error during SAML authentication, verify that your IdP is sending the mandatory **email** attribute. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#missing-saml-attributes
- [definition] SSH short-lived certificates — The error `Error 0: Bad Request. Please create a ca for application` appears if a certificate has not been generated for the Access application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#ssh-short-lived-certificates
- [definition] SSH "Origin auth failed" — This error often indicates a configuration issue on the target server's SSH daemon (`sshd`): — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#ssh-origin-auth-failed
- [definition] Team domain change error — The error `Access api error auth_domain_cannot_be_updated_dash_sso` occurs if you try to change your team domain while [Cloudflare dashboard SSO](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/manage-members/dashboard-sso/) is enabled. Dashboard SSO does not currently support team domain changes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#team-domain-change-error
- [definition] Long-lived SSH sessions disconnect — All connections proxied through Cloudflare Gateway, including traffic to [Access for Infrastructure](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/use-cases/ssh/ssh-infrastructure-access/) SSH targets, have a maximum guaranteed duration of 10 hours. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#long-lived-ssh-sessions-disconnect
- [definition] How to contact Support — If you cannot resolve the issue, [open a support case](https://developers.cloudflare.com/support/contacting-cloudflare-support/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/troubleshooting/#how-to-contact-support

- [definition] Applications — When you choose the _Application_ selector in a Gateway policy builder, the **Value** field will include all supported applications and their respective app types. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/application-app-types/#applications
- [definition] App types — Gateway sorts applications into the following app type groups: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/application-app-types/#app-types
- [definition] Application hostnames — An application like Google Drive uses its own hostnames (for example, `drive.google.com`) and shared resources used by other applications (for example, `accounts.google.com` for login). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/application-app-types/#application-hostnames
- [definition] Hostnames — Hostnames are domains that are core to the application and not [used by other applications](#overlapping-hostnames). These are the domains that Gateway blocks when you block an application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/application-app-types/#hostnames
- [definition] Support hostnames — Support hostnames are shared resources that applications depend on for content delivery, authentication, or third-party integrations. Because multiple applications share these hostnames, blocking them can cause unexpected side effects. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/application-app-types/#support-hostnames
- [definition] Application controls — When you use the [_Application_ selector](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/#granular-controls) in an HTTP policy with the _is_ operator, you can choose specific actions and operations to match application traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/application-app-types/#application-controls
- [definition] Overlapping hostnames — Overlapping hostnames are most common for vendors with many applications, such as Google or Meta. When you use the Application selector in Gateway policies, actions taken by Gateway will be limited to the specific application defined. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/application-app-types/#overlapping-hostnames
- [definition] Do Not Inspect applications — Gateway automatically groups applications incompatible with TLS decryption into the _Do Not Inspect_ app type. As Cloudflare identifies incompatible applications, Gateway will periodically update this app type to add new applications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/application-app-types/#do-not-inspect-applications

- [definition] Actions — The action determines what Gateway does when a DNS query matches your policy conditions. You can assign one action per policy. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#actions
- [definition] Selectors — Gateway matches DNS queries against the following selectors, or criteria. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#selectors
- [definition] Application — You can apply DNS policies to a growing list of popular web applications. Refer to [Application and app types](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/application-app-types/) for more information. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#application
- [definition] Authoritative Nameserver IP — Use this selector to match against the IP address of the authoritative nameserver IP address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#authoritative-nameserver-ip
- [definition] Content Categories — Use this selector to filter domains belonging to specific [content categories](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#content-categories). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#content-categories
- [definition] DNS CNAME Record — Use this selector to filter DNS responses by their `CNAME` records. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#dns-cname-record
- [definition] DNS MX Record — Use this selector to filter DNS responses by their `MX` records. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#dns-mx-record
- [definition] DNS PTR Record — Use this selector to filter DNS responses by their `PTR` records. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#dns-ptr-record
- [definition] DNS Resolver IP — Use this selector to apply policies to DNS queries that arrived to your Gateway Resolver IP address aligned with a registered DNS location. For most Gateway customers, this is an IPv4 anycast address and policies created using this IPv4 address will apply to all DNS locations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#dns-resolver-ip
- [definition] DNS TXT Record — Use this selector to filter DNS responses by their `TXT` records. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#dns-txt-record
- [definition] DoH Subdomain (DNS over HTTPS) — Use this selector to match against DNS queries that arrive via DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) destined for the DoH endpoint configured for each DNS location. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#doh-subdomain-dns-over-https
- [definition] Domain — Use this selector to match against a domain and all subdomains. For example, you can match `example.com` and its subdomains, such as `www.example.com`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#domain
- [definition] Host — Use this selector to match against only the hostname specified. For example, you can match `test.example.com` but not `example.com` or `www.test.example.com`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#host
- [definition] Indicator Feeds — Use this selector to match against custom indicator feeds. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#indicator-feeds
- [definition] Location — Use this selector to apply policies to a specific [Gateway DNS location](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/dns/locations/) or set of locations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#location
- [definition] Query Record Type — Use this selector to choose the DNS resource record type that you would like to apply policies against. For example, you can match `A` records for a domain but not `MX` records. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#query-record-type
- [definition] Resolved Continent — Use this selector to filter based on the continent that the query resolves to. Geolocation is determined from the IP address in the response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#resolved-continent
- [definition] Resolved Country — Use this selector to filter based on the country that the query resolves to. Geolocation is determined from the IP address in the response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#resolved-country
- [definition] Resolved IP — Use this selector to filter based on the IP addresses that the query resolves to. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#resolved-ip
- [definition] Request Context Categories — Use this selector to match a dynamic list of [category IDs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#category-and-subcategory-ids) sent in the [EDNS (Extension Mechanisms for DNS) ↗](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6891) portion of a DNS query. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#request-context-categories
- [definition] Security Categories — Use this selector to match domains (and optionally, [IP addresses](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#filter-traffic-by-resolved-ip-category)) belonging to specific [security… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#security-categories
- [definition] Source Continent — Use this selector to filter based on the continent where the query arrived to Gateway from. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#source-continent
- [definition] Source Country — Use this selector to filter based on the country where the query arrived to Gateway from. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#source-country
- [definition] Source IP — Use this selector to apply policies to the source IP address of DNS queries. For example, this could be the WAN IP address of the stub resolver used by your organization to send queries to Gateway. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#source-ip
- [definition] Source Internal IP — Use this selector to apply policies to the source internal IP address of a DNS query. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#source-internal-ip
- [definition] Users — Use these selectors to match against identity attributes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#users
- [definition] Comparison operators — Comparison operators are the way Gateway matches traffic to a selector. When you choose a **Selector** in the dashboard policy builder, the **Operator** dropdown menu will display the available options for that selector. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#comparison-operators
- [definition] Value — In the **Value** field, you can input a single value when using an equality comparison operator (such as _is_) or multiple values when using a containment comparison operator (such as _in_). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#value
- [definition] Regular expressions — Regular expressions are evaluated using Rust. The Rust implementation is slightly different than regex libraries used elsewhere. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#regular-expressions
- [definition] Logical operators — To evaluate multiple conditions in an expression, select the **And** logical operator. These expressions can be compared further with the **Or** logical operator. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#logical-operators
- [definition] Third-party filtering conflict — Gateway will not properly filter traffic sent through third-party VPNs or other Internet filtering software, such as [iCloud Private Relay ↗](https://support.apple.com/102602) or [Google Chrome IP Protection ↗](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/ip-protection#ip-protection). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#third-party-filtering-conflict
- [definition] Cloudflare WAN forwarding — To apply DNS policies to queries forwarded through [Cloudflare WAN](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-gateway/), you can either point your organization's DNS resolver to an IPv6, DNS over HTTPS (DoH), or DNS over TLS (DoT) endpoint or request a dedicated… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#cloudflare-wan-forwarding
- [definition] Fallback DNS — Some applications (for example, WhatsApp and Android Studio) have backup DNS servers built into their code. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/dns-policies/#fallback-dns

## Domain categories
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/>

- [snippet] Terraform: data "cloudflare_zero_trust_gateway_categories_list" "categories" { — `data "cloudflare_zero_trust_gateway_categories_list" "categories" {` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#terraform
- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-p — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#on-this-page
- [parameter] Anonymizer: Sites that allow users to surf the Internet anonymously. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] Brand Embedding: Sites that imitate a verified brand, for example facobook.com. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] Command and Control & Botnet: Sites that are queried by compromised devices to exfiltrate information or potentially infect other devices in a network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] Compromised Domain: Sites where a legitimate domain has been compromised or taken over and had malicious content planted or injected. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] Cryptomining: Sites that mine cryptocurrency by taking over the user's computing resources. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] DGA Domains: Domains generated programmatically by Domain Generation Algorithms (DGA) associated with malware. These algorithmically created domain names change frequently, making them harder to block individually. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] DNS Tunneling: Domains with detected DNS tunneling activity, including attempts to encode or exfiltrate data in DNS queries and responses (for example, in TXT records) or to use DNS for command-and-control (C2) communications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] Malware: Sites hosting malicious content and other compromised websites. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] Phishing: Domains that are known for stealing personal information. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] Potentially Unwanted Software: Domains that distribute software that may come bundled with other less legitimate software or functionality, like toolbars, adware, and grayware. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] Private IP Address: Domains that resolve to private IP Addresses. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories
- [parameter] Scam: Fraudulent websites and schemes designed to trick victims into giving away money or personal information. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories

- [definition] Can I provision the same egress IP address to multiple data centers? — No, egress IPs are limited to a single data center. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/egress-policies/dedicated-egress-ips/#can-i-provision-the-same-egress-ip-address-to-multiple-data-centers
- [definition] Can my users in different locations egress from their closest data center via a single egress IP? — No, traffic exits from the data center where the egress IP is provisioned. - [definition] Can I use dedicated egress IPs with traffic proxied via [PAC files](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/)? — Yes, your users will egress via their provisioned IP address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/egress-policies/dedicated-egress-ips/#can-i-use-dedicated-egress-ips-with-traffic-proxied-via-pac-fileshttpsdeveloperscloudflarecomcloudflare-onenetworksresolvers-and-proxiesproxy-endpoints
- [definition] What happens when I use dedicated egress IPs with [Cloudflare Browser Isolation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/)? — Your users will connect to the nearest data center, where the remote browser session will load. The remote browser will then egress via the data center with their provisioned egress IP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/egress-policies/dedicated-egress-ips/#what-happens-when-i-use-dedicated-egress-ips-with-cloudflare-browser-isolationhttpsdeveloperscloudflarecomcloudflare-oneremote-browser-isolation
- [definition] Do dedicated egress IPs work on the [Cloudflare China Network](https://developers.cloudflare.com/china-network/)? — No, Gateway does not support dedicated egress IPs on the China Network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/egress-policies/dedicated-egress-ips/#do-dedicated-egress-ips-work-on-the-cloudflare-china-networkhttpsdeveloperscloudflarecomchina-network

- [definition] DNS resolution policies — Gateway enforces global DNS and resolver policies before any other policies. This ensures the traffic is not blocked by user policies and gets resolved with Cloudflare's public DNS resolver, [1.1.1.1](https://developers.cloudflare.com/1.1.1.1/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/global-policies/#dns-resolution-policies

- [definition] Block sites — Block attempts to reach sites by hostname or URL paths. Different approaches may be required based on how a site is organized. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/common-policies/#block-sites

- [definition] Skip inspection for groups of applications — Certain client applications, such as Zoom or Apple services, rely on certificate pinning. These applications verify they are connecting directly to their own servers and will reject Gateway's TLS inspection certificate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/common-policies/#skip-inspection-for-groups-of-applications

- [definition] Enforce a minimum OS version — Perform an [OS version check](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/posture-checks/client-checks/os-version/) to ensure users are running at least a minimum version. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/common-policies/#enforce-a-minimum-os-version
- [definition] Check for a specific file — Perform a [file check](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/posture-checks/client-checks/file-check/) to ensure users have a certain file on their device. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/common-policies/#check-for-a-specific-file
- [definition] Enforce session duration — [Require users to re-authenticate](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/configure/client-sessions/) after a certain amount of time has elapsed. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/common-policies/#enforce-session-duration

- [definition] Header operations — Gateway supports three header operations on HTTP policies. When a request matches an Allow policy with header operations configured, Gateway applies them in the following order: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#header-operations
- [definition] Add headers — Adding a header appends a value to the request. If the header already exists, the value is added alongside the existing value rather than replacing it. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#add-headers
- [definition] Overwrite headers — Overwriting a header overwrites any existing value. If the header does not already exist on the request, it is created. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#overwrite-headers
- [definition] Delete headers — Deleting a header removes it from the request entirely. If the header does not exist, the operation has no effect. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#delete-headers
- [definition] Dynamic header values — Header values can include dynamic variables that Gateway resolves at request time using identity, device, and network context from the current session. Dynamic variables use the `@{...}` syntax and can be mixed with static text in the same value. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#dynamic-header-values
- [definition] Dashboard — To create an HTTP policy with header operations: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#dashboard
- [definition] API — To create an HTTP policy with header operations via the API, include `add_headers`, `set_headers`, and `delete_headers` in the `rule_settings` object. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#api
- [definition] Verify custom headers — If you save a HAR (HTTP Archive) file from a browser to analyze your web traffic, custom headers defined with Gateway will not appear in the file. This is because Gateway injects the header after the request leaves the browser. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#verify-custom-headers
- [definition] SaaS tenant control — Tenant control allows your users to access corporate SaaS applications while blocking access to personal accounts on the same service. For example, you can allow access to your company's Google Workspace while blocking personal Gmail logins. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#saas-tenant-control
- [definition] Forward user identity to upstream services — You can use dynamic header values to forward user identity information to your upstream applications without requiring those applications to integrate with Cloudflare Access directly. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#forward-user-identity-to-upstream-services
- [definition] Strip internal headers — To prevent clients from spoofing internal headers, use the delete operation to remove headers before forwarding the request, then use the add or set operation to re-inject them with verified values. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#strip-internal-headers
- [definition] Exempt users in Cloudflare WAF — You can include custom headers in an HTTP policy to allow your users through [Cloudflare WAF](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/). This is useful for allowing only Cloudflare One Client users through your WAF. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#exempt-users-in-cloudflare-waf
- [definition] Use custom headers with Browser Isolation — You can configure [Browser Isolation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/) to send custom headers. This is useful for implementing tenant control for isolated SaaS applications or sending arbitrary custom request headers to isolated websites. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tenant-control/#use-custom-headers-with-browser-isolation

- [definition] TLS decryption — Last updated Jun 8, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#tls-decryption
- [definition] Inspection limitations — Gateway does not support TLS decryption for applications which use: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#inspection-limitations
- [definition] Inspect on all ports — By default, Gateway will only inspect HTTP traffic through port `80`. Additionally, if you [turn on TLS decryption](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#turn-on-tls-decryption), Gateway will inspect HTTPS traffic through port `443`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#inspect-on-all-ports
- [definition] Incompatible certificates — Applications that use certificate pinning and mTLS authentication do not trust Cloudflare certificates. For example, most mobile applications use [certificate pinning](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/reference/certificate-pinning/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#incompatible-certificates
- [definition] Google Chrome automatic HTTPS upgrades — Google Chrome can automatically upgrade HTTP requests to HTTPS requests, even when you select a link that explicitly declares `http://`. When you use Gateway to proxy and filter your traffic, this upgrade can interrupt the connection between your Zero Trust users and Gateway. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#google-chrome-automatic-https-upgrades
- [definition] Mutual TLS (mTLS) — In mutual TLS (mTLS), both the client and server present certificates to verify each other's identity. When Gateway decrypts TLS traffic, it terminates the connection from the client and creates a new connection to the origin server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#mutual-tls-mtls
- [definition] ESNI and ECH — Websites that adhere to [ESNI or Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) standards ↗](https://blog.cloudflare.com/encrypted-client-hello/) encrypt the Server Name Indication (SNI) during the TLS handshake and are therefore incompatible with HTTP inspection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#esni-and-ech
- [definition] Post-quantum support — Gateway supports post-quantum cryptography using a hybrid key exchange with X25519 and MLKEM768 over TLS 1.3\. Once the key exchange is complete, Gateway uses AES-128-GCM to encrypt traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#post-quantum-support
- [definition] FIPS compliance — By default, TLS decryption can use both TLS version 1.2 and 1.3\. However, some environments such as FedRAMP may require cipher suites and TLS versions compliant with FIPS 140-3\. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#fips-compliance
- [definition] Enable FIPS compliance — 1. In the [Cloudflare dashboard ↗](https://dash.cloudflare.com/), go to **Zero Trust** \> **Traffic policies** \> **Traffic settings**. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#enable-fips-compliance
- [definition] Limitations — When FIPS compliance is enabled, Gateway will only choose [FIPS-compliant cipher suites](#cipher-suites) when connecting to the origin. If the origin does not support FIPS-compliant ciphers, the request will fail. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#limitations
- [definition] FedRAMP compliance — When you use [Cloudflare Regional Services](https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/regional-services/) in the United States and the Cloudflare One Client to on-ramp TLS traffic to Gateway, traffic will egress from a Cloudflare data center within Cloudflare's FedRAMP boundary. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#fedramp-compliance
- [definition] Cipher suites — A cipher suite is a set of encryption algorithms for establishing a secure communications connection. There are several cipher suites in wide use, and a client and server agree on the cipher suite to use when establishing the TLS connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/#cipher-suites

- [definition] Selectors — Gateway matches network traffic against the following selectors, or criteria. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#selectors

- [definition] Access Private App — All destination IPs and hostnames secured by an [Access self-hosted private application](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/applications/non-http/self-hosted-private-app/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#access-private-app
- [definition] Application — You can apply network policies to a growing list of popular web applications. Refer to [Application and app types](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/application-app-types/) for more information. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#application
- [definition] Browser Isolation Beta — Whether the current session is running inside [Remote Browser Isolation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/). Use this selector to apply different policy behavior to isolated and non-isolated traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#browser-isolation-beta
- [definition] Content Categories — Applications within a specific [security category](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#content-categories) as categorized by [Cloudflare Radar](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/glossary/#content-categories). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#content-categories
- [definition] Destination Continent — The continent where the request is destined. Geolocation is determined from the target IP address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#destination-continent
- [definition] Destination Country — The country that the request is destined for. Geolocation is determined from the target IP address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#destination-country
- [definition] Destination Port — The port number of the request's target. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#destination-port
- [definition] Detected Protocol — The inferred network protocol based on Cloudflare's [protocol detection](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/protocol-detection/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#detected-protocol
- [definition] Device Posture — With the Device Posture selector, admins can use signals from end-user devices to secure access to their internal and external resources. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#device-posture
- [definition] Proxy Endpoint — The [proxy server](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/) where your browser forwards HTTP traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#proxy-endpoint
- [definition] Security Categories — Applications within a specific [security category](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#security-categories) as categorized by [Cloudflare Radar](https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/glossary/#content-categories). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#security-categories
- [definition] SNI — Server Name Indication (SNI) is the hostname a client sends during the TLS handshake, before encryption begins. Gateway reads the SNI to identify the destination of encrypted traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#sni
- [definition] SNI Domain — The domain whose Server Name Indication (SNI) header Gateway will filter traffic against. For example, a rule for `example.com` will match `example.com`, `www.example.com`, and `my.test.example.com`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#sni-domain
- [definition] Source Continent — The continent of the user making the request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#source-continent
- [definition] Source Country — The country of the user making the request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#source-country
- [definition] Source Internal IP — Use this selector to apply network policies to a private IP address, assigned by a user's local network, that requests arrive to Gateway from. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#source-internal-ip
- [definition] Source IP — The originating IP address or addresses of a device proxied by Gateway. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#source-ip
- [definition] Source Port — The originating port of a device proxied by Gateway. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#source-port
- [definition] Traffic Source Beta — The method used to on-ramp traffic to Cloudflare. Use this selector to apply policies based on how traffic reaches Gateway. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#traffic-source-beta
- [definition] Users — Use these selectors to match against identity attributes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#users
- [definition] Virtual Network — Use this selector to match all traffic routed through a specific [Virtual Network](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/private-net/cloudflared/tunnel-virtual-networks/) via the Cloudflare One Client. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#virtual-network
- [definition] Comparison operators — Comparison operators are the way Gateway matches traffic to a selector. When you choose a **Selector** in the dashboard policy builder, the **Operator** dropdown menu will display the available options for that selector. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#comparison-operators
- [definition] Value — In the **Value** field, you can input a single value when using an equality comparison operator (such as _is_) or multiple values when using a containment comparison operator (such as _in_). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#value
- [definition] Regular expressions — Regular expressions are evaluated using Rust. The Rust implementation is slightly different than regex libraries used elsewhere. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#regular-expressions
- [definition] Logical operators — To evaluate multiple conditions in an expression, select the **And** logical operator. These expressions can be compared further with the **Or** logical operator. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/network-policies/#logical-operators

- [definition] Proxy algorithm — Gateway uses the [Happy Eyeballs algorithm ↗](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6555), which tries IPv4 and IPv6 connections with a staggered fallback and uses whichever address family responds first, to proxy traffic in the following order: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/proxy/#proxy-algorithm

- [definition] UDP — The UDP proxy forwards UDP traffic such as VoIP, [internal DNS requests](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/private-net/cloudflared/private-dns/), and thick client applications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/proxy/#udp
- [definition] ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) — The ICMP proxy allows ICMP traffic to reach your private network through Gateway. For example, this would allow a Cloudflare One Client user to run diagnostic commands such as `ping` and `traceroute` to an internal server IP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/proxy/#icmp-internet-control-message-protocol
- [definition] Turn on the Gateway proxy — The Gateway proxy toggle only applies to traffic from Cloudflare One Client devices. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/proxy/#turn-on-the-gateway-proxy

- [definition] Use cases — You may use resolver policies if you require access to non-publicly routed domains, such as private network services or internal resources. You may also use resolver policies if you need to access a protected DNS service or want to simplify DNS management for multiple locations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#use-cases
- [definition] Internal DNS — [Cloudflare Internal DNS](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/internal-dns/) allows you to manage DNS records for internal resources on a private network. DNS zones configured in Internal DNS can only be queried by the Gateway resolver. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#internal-dns
- [definition] Local Domain Fallback — Use resolver policies when your DNS server is reachable from Cloudflare's network — for example, through a Cloudflare Tunnel, IPsec/GRE tunnel, or the public Internet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#local-domain-fallback
- [definition] Resolver connections — Resolver policies support TCP and UDP connections. - [definition] Cloudflare Tunnel — You can configure connections to a private resolver connected to Cloudflare with [Cloudflare Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#cloudflare-tunnel
- [definition] Cloudflare WAN — To enable connections to a private resolver connected to Cloudflare via [Cloudflare WAN](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/), contact your account team. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#cloudflare-wan

- [definition] DNS Resolver IP — Use this selector to apply policies to DNS queries that arrived to your Gateway Resolver IP address aligned with a registered DNS location. - [definition] Domain — Use this selector to match against a domain and all subdomains. For example, you can match `example.com` and its subdomains, such as `www.example.com`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#domain
- [definition] Host — Use this selector to match against only the hostname specified. For example, you can match `test.example.com` but not `example.com` or `www.test.example.com`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#host
- [definition] Location — Use this selector to apply policies to a specific [Gateway DNS location](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/dns/locations/) or set of locations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#location
- [definition] Query Record Type — Use this selector to choose the DNS resource record type that you would like to apply policies against. - [definition] Security Categories — Use this selector to match domains (and optionally, [IP addresses](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/domain-categories/#filter-traffic-by-resolved-ip-category)) belonging to specific [security… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#security-categories
- [definition] Source Continent — Use this selector to filter based on the continent where the query arrived to Gateway from. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#source-continent
- [definition] Source Country — Use this selector to filter based on the country where the query arrived to Gateway from. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#source-country
- [definition] Source IP — Use this selector to apply policies to the source IP address of DNS queries. For example, this could be the WAN IP address of the stub resolver used by your organization to send queries to Gateway. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#source-ip
- [definition] Users — Use these selectors to match against identity attributes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#users
- [definition] Comparison operators — Comparison operators are the way Gateway matches traffic to a selector. When you choose a **Selector** in the dashboard policy builder, the **Operator** dropdown menu will display the available options for that selector. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#comparison-operators
- [definition] Value — In the **Value** field, you can input a single value when using an equality comparison operator (such as _is_) or multiple values when using a containment comparison operator (such as _in_). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#value
- [definition] Regular expressions — Regular expressions are evaluated using Rust. The Rust implementation is slightly different than regex libraries used elsewhere. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/resolver-policies/#regular-expressions
- [definition] Logical operators — To evaluate multiple conditions in an expression, select the **And** logical operator. - [definition] Egress policies do not work as expected — Egress policies are the most common category of issues for Gateway. - [definition] Private DNS and internal resources are not working — You have configured Gateway to resolve internal hostnames, but users are unable to access them. For example, a user connected to the Cloudflare One Client tries to access an internal service like `jira.mycompany.local`, but the DNS query fails. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshoot-gateway/#private-dns-and-internal-resources-are-not-working

- [parameter] Routing or configuration issue on the Cloudflare side: Document the time of the incident and collect Request IDs from Gateway HTTP or DNS logs for affected users. Open a support ticket and provide this information. Temporarily, you can edit the egress policy to set your secondary IP as the primary to restore service. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#symptom-failover-is-not-working-or-is-using-the-wrong-ip
- [parameter] Single egress policy: You may have one broad egress policy that applies to all users regardless of their location. Create location-aware egress policies. Use the _User Location_ selector in your policy to tie specific user locations to their nearest dedicated egress IP. For example, create one policy for when _User Location_ is United Kingdom, egress via London IP; create a second policy for… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#symptom-users-are-egressing-from-a-geographically-distant-location
- [parameter] Incorrect geolocation data: The IP address of the user's ISP may not be correctly geolocated. Check the user's location as seen by Cloudflare in the Gateway logs. If it appears incorrect, you can report it to Cloudflare Support. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#symptom-users-are-egressing-from-a-geographically-distant-location
- [parameter] Domain: Operator=in list; Value=_CLI Tool Domains_; Action=Do Not Inspect — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#symptom-command-line-tools-cli-tools-or-native-applications-fail-with-certificate-errors
- [parameter] Missing or incorrect resolver policy: Go to **Traffic policies** \> **Resolver policies**. Create a policy that matches your internal domain suffix and forwards queries to your internal DNS servers' IP addresses. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#private-dns-and-internal-resources-are-not-working
- [parameter] Split Tunnel excludes the private IP range: If your internal resources are in a private IP range (such as 10.0.0.0/8), that range must be included in the tunnel. If it is in the Exclude list of your Split Tunnel configuration, the Cloudflare One Client will not proxy the traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#private-dns-and-internal-resources-are-not-working
- [parameter] Local Domain Fallback misconfiguration: Use resolver policies for corporate DNS. Only use Local Domain Fallback for domains specific to a user's immediate physical network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#private-dns-and-internal-resources-are-not-working

- [definition] A website is blocked incorrectly — If you believe a domain has been incorrectly blocked by Gateway's security categories or threat intelligence, you can use the [Cloudflare Radar categorization feedback form ↗](https://radar.cloudflare.com/categorization-feedback/) to request a review. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#a-website-is-blocked-incorrectly
- [definition] Error 526: Invalid SSL certificate — Gateway presents a **526** error page when it cannot establish a secure connection to the origin. - [definition] Gateway analytics not displayed — If you do not see analytics on the Gateway Overview page: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#gateway-analytics-not-displayed
- [definition] Egress policies — Egress policies symptoms include traffic not using your dedicated egress IP, incorrect failover behavior, or high latency due to Gateway routing traffic through a distant data center. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#egress-policies
- [definition] Symptom: traffic is not using your dedicated egress IP — Even with an active egress policy, you may find that traffic is egressing from a default Cloudflare IP address instead of your dedicated egress IP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#symptom-traffic-is-not-using-your-dedicated-egress-ip
- [definition] Symptom: failover is not working or is using the wrong IP — Your primary dedicated egress IP becomes unavailable, but instead of using your configured secondary dedicated IP, traffic fails over to a default Cloudflare shared IP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#symptom-failover-is-not-working-or-is-using-the-wrong-ip
- [definition] Symptom: users are egressing from a geographically distant location — Gateway routes your users in one country (such as Australia) through a dedicated egress IP located in another region (such as Germany), causing high latency and breaking access to geo-restricted content. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#symptom-users-are-egressing-from-a-geographically-distant-location
- [definition] Policy precedence — A common point of confusion is how Gateway evaluates its different policy types and the rules within them. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#policy-precedence
- [definition] Symptom: a Block policy is overriding a more specific Allow or Do Not Scan policy — You have a high-precedence Allow or Do Not Scan policy for a specific application (such as Allow finance.example.com), but Gateway still block traffic with a low-precedence Block policy (such as Block All High-Risk Sites). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#symptom-a-block-policy-is-overriding-a-more-specific-allow-or-do-not-scan-policy
- [definition] TLS decryption breaks applications — Turning on [TLS decryption](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/) is required for Gateway features such as Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Browser Isolation, and application-aware HTTP policies. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#tls-decryption-breaks-applications
- [definition] Symptom: command-line tools (CLI tools) or native applications fail with certificate errors — If after turning on TLS decryption, command-line tools (such as `git`, `aws`, `kubectl`, and `terraform`) or desktop applications (such as ChatGPT or Docker) stop working, this may be due to certificate errors. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#symptom-command-line-tools-cli-tools-or-native-applications-fail-with-certificate-errors
- [definition] Symptom: the custom block page is not displayed — When an HTTP policy blocks a user's request, their browser will return a generic error (`ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR`) instead of your configured Gateway block page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#symptom-the-custom-block-page-is-not-displayed
- [definition] Private DNS and internal resources are not working — You have configured Gateway to resolve internal hostnames, but users are unable to access them. For example, a user connected to the Cloudflare One Client tries to access an internal service like `jira.mycompany.local`, but the DNS query fails. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/troubleshooting/#private-dns-and-internal-resources-are-not-working

- [definition] Understand scan frequency — CASB integrations do not provide real-time updates. Scans are performed periodically to discover new findings and validate the status of existing ones. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#understand-scan-frequency
- [definition] Remediation action fails in the dashboard — If you attempt to use a one-click remediation action (such as "Make private") on a finding, it may result in a **Failed** status, often with a timeout error. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#remediation-action-fails-in-the-dashboard
- [definition] Verify permissions — The remediation failure may be due to the permissions for the Cloudflare app being changed or revoked in the SaaS application after the initial setup. Re-validate the integration to ensure all required permissions are still granted. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#verify-permissions
- [definition] Remediate manually — As a workaround, remediate the finding directly within the SaaS application (for example, change the file's sharing settings in Google Drive). CASB will clear the finding from the dashboard after the next successful scan. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#remediate-manually
- [definition] Webhook test or delivery fails — If Cloudflare cannot deliver a test request or a posture finding instance to your destination, follow these steps. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#webhook-test-or-delivery-fails
- [definition] Check destination requirements — Verify that the destination URL uses `https://` and is publicly reachable. Cloudflare rejects destinations that resolve to localhost, loopback, private, or other reserved addresses. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#check-destination-requirements
- [definition] Check authentication settings — Ensure that the webhook's authentication method matches what your receiver expects. Re-enter any bearer token, Basic auth credentials, static headers, or signing secret if needed. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#check-authentication-settings
- [definition] Understand delivery timing — Test delivery sends a test request immediately, but posture finding instance sends are queued in the background. A success message means that Cloudflare accepted the request for delivery. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#understand-delivery-timing
- [definition] CASB is generating false positives — CASB may incorrectly flag items, such as flagging internally-shared files as public or archived Google Workspace users as inactive. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#casb-is-generating-false-positives
- [definition] Review finding details — Carefully examine the evidence provided in the finding. An object's status in the SaaS platform may not be accurate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#review-finding-details
- [definition] Report the issue — If you confirm the finding is a false positive, report the behavior to Cloudflare Support. Provide the finding ID (visible in the finding's detail view) and as much detail as possible. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#report-the-issue
- [definition] Hide the finding — While Cloudflare investigates the issue, you can [ignore the finding or hide individual instances](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/manage-findings/#hide-findings) to remove it from your active list and reduce noise. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/troubleshoot-casb/#hide-the-finding

<https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/ — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-g` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/#on-this-page
- [parameter] Pass (no findings): Response cached=Yes; Behavior=The response is cached normally according to your gateway cache settings. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/#interaction-with-caching
- [parameter] Flag: Response cached=Yes; Behavior=The response is cached normally. - [parameter] Block: Response cached=No; Behavior=The provider response is discarded and replaced with a DLP error response (status 400). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/#interaction-with-caching

- [definition] How it works — AI Gateway DLP leverages the same powerful detection engines used in [Cloudflare's Data Loss Prevention](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/data-loss-prevention/) solution to scan AI traffic in real-time. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/#how-it-works
- [definition] Inspection scope — DLP inspects the text content of request and response bodies as they pass through AI Gateway. The following details apply: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/#inspection-scope
- [definition] Streaming behavior — When DLP response scanning is enabled and a client sends a streaming request (`"stream": true`), AI Gateway buffers the complete provider response before running DLP inspection. This differs from requests without DLP, where streamed chunks are forwarded to the client as they arrive. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/#streaming-behavior
- [definition] Interaction with caching — DLP scanning runs after a cache miss, when AI Gateway forwards the request to the provider and receives a response. The following table describes how each DLP outcome affects caching: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/#interaction-with-caching
- [definition] Per-request DLP controls — DLP policies are configured at the gateway level and apply uniformly to all requests passing through that gateway. There is no per-request header to select specific DLP profiles or to bypass DLP scanning for individual requests. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/#per-request-dlp-controls
- [definition] Integration with Cloudflare DLP — AI Gateway DLP uses the same [detection profiles](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/data-loss-prevention/dlp-profiles/) as Cloudflare One's DLP solution. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dlp/#integration-with-cloudflare-dlp

- [definition] 1\. Configure a DLP profile — A DLP profile defines the sensitive data patterns you want to detect — for example, social security number formats, credit card numbers, or custom patterns specific to your organization. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/data-loss-prevention/dlp-policies/#1-configure-a-dlp-profile
- [definition] 2\. Create a DLP policy — DLP Profiles may be used alongside other Cloudflare One rules in a [Gateway HTTP policy](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/). To start logging or blocking traffic, create a policy for DLP: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/data-loss-prevention/dlp-policies/#2-create-a-dlp-policy
