- [definition] Website compatibility — Our Network Vector Rendering (NVR) technology sends drawing instructions to the user's browser instead of streaming video of the page. This allows us to deliver a secure remote computing experience without the bandwidth limitations of video streams. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/known-limitations/#website-compatibility
- [definition] Brave — Browser Isolation uses [WebRTC](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/network-dependencies/#webrtc-channel) for low-latency communication between the local and remote browser. Brave's WebRTC IP Handling Policy can impact how Cloudflare RBI loads and functions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/known-limitations/#brave
- [definition] Protocol support — Browser Isolation requires HTTPS. Websites served over unencrypted HTTP cannot be isolated. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/known-limitations/#protocol-support
- [definition] Virtual machines — Browser Isolation is not supported in virtualized environments (VMs). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/known-limitations/#virtual-machines
- [definition] Gateway selectors — Certain selectors for Gateway HTTP policies bypass Browser Isolation, including: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/known-limitations/#gateway-selectors
- [definition] File download size — When a user downloads a file within the remote browser, the file is held in memory and destroyed at the end of the remote browser session. Therefore, the total size of files downloaded per session is shared with the amount of memory available to the remote browser. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/known-limitations/#file-download-size
- [definition] Multifactor authentication — [Clientless Web Isolation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/setup/clientless-browser-isolation/) does not support Yubikey or WebAuthN (hardware security key authentication). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/known-limitations/#multifactor-authentication
- [definition] SAML applications — Cloudflare Remote Browser Isolation now [supports SAML applications that use HTTP-POST bindings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/changelog/browser-isolation/#2025-05-13). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/known-limitations/#saml-applications
- [definition] Browser Isolation is not compatible with private apps on non-`443` ports — Browser Isolation is not compatible with [self-hosted private applications](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/applications/non-http/self-hosted-private-app/) that use private IPs or hostnames on ports other than `443`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/remote-browser-isolation/known-limitations/#browser-isolation-is-not-compatible-with-private-apps-on-non-443-ports

## Policies FAQ
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/polic — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/#on-this-page
- [definition] Policies FAQ — Last updated Apr 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/#policies-faq
- [definition] What is the order of policy enforcement? — Gateway and Access policies generally trigger from top to bottom based on their position in the policy table in the UI. Exceptions include Bypass and Service Auth policies, which Access evaluates first. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/#what-is-the-order-of-policy-enforcement
- [definition] **How can I bypass the L7 firewall for a website?** — Cloudflare Gateway uses the hostname in the HTTP `CONNECT` header to identify the destination of the request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/#how-can-i-bypass-the-l7-firewall-for-a-website
- [definition] Can I secure applications with a second-level subdomain URL? — Yes. Ensure that your SSL certificates cover the first- and second-level subdomain. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/#can-i-secure-applications-with-a-second-level-subdomain-url
- [definition] How do isolation policies work together with HTTP policies? — Isolation policies, like all HTTP policies, are evaluated in stages. When a user makes a request which evaluates an Isolation policy, the request will be rerouted to an isolated browser and re-evaluated for HTTP policies. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/#how-do-isolation-policies-work-together-with-http-policies
- [definition] Why is API or CLI traffic not isolated? — Isolation policies are applied to requests that include `Accept: text/html*`. This allows Browser Isolation policies to co-exist with API and command line requests. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/#why-is-api-or-cli-traffic-not-isolated
- [definition] Can Access enforce policies on a specific nonstandard port? — No. Cloudflare Access cannot enforce a policy that would contain a port appended to the URL. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/#can-access-enforce-policies-on-a-specific-nonstandard-port
- [definition] Why can I still reach domains blocked by a Gateway policy? — If the domain is blocked by a DNS, network, or HTTP policy, it may be because: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/#why-can-i-still-reach-domains-blocked-by-a-gateway-policy
- [definition] When does Access return a Forbidden status page versus a login page? — Access returns a Forbidden page with status codes `401`/`403` when it determines there is no way a user can pass a [policy](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/faq/policies-faq/#when-does-access-return-a-forbidden-status-page-versus-a-login-page

<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"WebPage","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooti — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"WebPage","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudfla` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#on-this-page

- [definition] AJAX/CORS errors — Cloudflare Access requires that the `credentials: same-origin` parameter be added to JavaScript when using the Fetch API to include cookies. AJAX requests fail if this parameter is missing, resulting in an error such as `No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is present on the requested resource`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#ajaxcors-errors
- [definition] SAML verification failure — The error `SAML Verify: Invalid SAML response, SAML Verify: No certificate selected to verify` occurs when the identity provider (IdP) does not include the signing public key in the SAML response. Cloudflare Access requires the public key to match the **Signing certificate** uploaded to Zero Trust. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#saml-verification-failure
- [definition] Identity provider user/group info error — The error `Failed to fetch user/group information from the identity provider` occurs when Cloudflare lacks the necessary API permissions to communicate with your IdP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#identity-provider-usergroup-info-error
- [definition] Google Workspace redirect loop — If you place your Google Workspace behind Access, you cannot use Google or Google Workspace as an identity provider for that application. This creates an infinite redirect cycle because both systems depend on each other to complete the login. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#google-workspace-redirect-loop
- [definition] Invalid session error — The error `Invalid session. Please try logging in again` indicates that Access was unable to validate your `CF_Session` cookie. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#invalid-session-error
- [definition] Firefox Private Window — Firefox's default tracking prevention in Private Windows may prevent the `CF_authorization` cookie from being sent, especially for XHR requests. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#firefox-private-window
- [definition] Workers routes on the login path — If you have a Cloudflare Worker route assigned to your application's login path, the Worker may overwrite the `cf-authorization` cookie. To prevent this, ensure your Worker script does not modify or strip the `Set-Cookie` header for Access cookies. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#workers-routes-on-the-login-path
- [definition] OTP email not received — If a user does not receive a one-time PIN (OTP) email: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#otp-email-not-received
- [definition] OTP code already used — The error `This One-Time PIN has already been used` occurs when the OTP code has already been redeemed before the user enters it. OTP codes are single-use and expire 10 minutes after the initial request. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#otp-code-already-used
- [definition] Google Super Admin login — If you use Access as the SSO provider for your Google Workspace, Google Super Admins cannot sign in via Access when accessing `admin.google.com`. Google requires Super Admins to use their original Google password to ensure they can always access the admin console. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#google-super-admin-login
- [definition] Missing SAML attributes — If you receive a `Required attributes are missing` error during SAML authentication, verify that your IdP is sending the mandatory **email** attribute. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#missing-saml-attributes
- [definition] SSH short-lived certificates — The error `Error 0: Bad Request. Please create a ca for application` appears if a certificate has not been generated for the Access application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#ssh-short-lived-certificates
- [definition] SSH "Origin auth failed" — This error often indicates a configuration issue on the target server's SSH daemon (`sshd`): — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#ssh-origin-auth-failed
- [definition] Team domain change error — The error `Access api error auth_domain_cannot_be_updated_dash_sso` occurs if you try to change your team domain while [Cloudflare dashboard SSO](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/manage-members/dashboard-sso/) is enabled. Dashboard SSO does not currently support team domain changes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#team-domain-change-error
- [definition] Long-lived SSH sessions disconnect — All connections proxied through Cloudflare Gateway, including traffic to [Access for Infrastructure](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/use-cases/ssh/ssh-infrastructure-access/) SSH targets, have a maximum guaranteed duration of 10 hours. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#long-lived-ssh-sessions-disconnect
- [definition] More Access resources — For more information, refer to the full Access troubleshooting guide. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/access/#more-access-resources

## Gateway
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/gateway/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"WebPage","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooti — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"WebPage","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudfla` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/gateway/#on-this-page
- [parameter] DNS resolution to an initial resolved IP: When an egress policy uses a _Domain_ or _Host_ selector, Gateway must first resolve that domain to an [initial resolved IP](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/routes/reserved-ips/#gateway-initial-resolved-ips). If your account still uses a legacy range within CGNAT (carrier-grade NAT) address space, this IP may be treated as… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/gateway/#symptom-traffic-is-not-using-your-dedicated-egress-ip
- [parameter] Policy precedence: A different egress policy with a higher precedence (a lower number) is matching the traffic first. Remember that egress policies follow the same first-match-wins logic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/gateway/#symptom-traffic-is-not-using-your-dedicated-egress-ip
- [parameter] Split Tunnel configuration: The destination IP or domain is excluded from the WARP tunnel via your Split Tunnel configuration. Traffic that is excluded from the tunnel will not be subject to any Gateway policies, including egress. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/gateway/#symptom-traffic-is-not-using-your-dedicated-egress-ip
- [parameter] No egress logs: Egress logging is available via Logpush with the Gateway Egress dataset. This is essential for troubleshooting. You can also use a third-party IP check service to verify the egress IP from a test device. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/gateway/#symptom-traffic-is-not-using-your-dedicated-egress-ip
- [parameter] Routing or configuration issue on the Cloudflare side: Document the time of the incident and collect Request IDs from Gateway HTTP or DNS logs for affected users. Open a support ticket and provide this information. Temporarily, you can edit the egress policy to set your secondary IP as the primary to restore service. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/troubleshooting/gateway/#symptom-failover-is-not-working-or-is-using-the-wrong-ip

- [parameter] App Launcher: The App Launcher portal provides end users with a single dashboard to open applications secured by Cloudflare One. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] application: The resource protected by Cloudflare One, which can be a subdomain, a path, or a SaaS application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] application token: A piece of data that grants a user access to a specific Access application for a period of time. Can be stored in a browser cookie or passed to the application in place of a normal password. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] captive portal: A login screen shown to users when they connect to a public Wi-Fi. Captive portals typically occur in places such as airports, cafes, and hotels. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare Access: Cloudflare Access replaces corporate VPNs with Cloudflare's network. It verifies attributes such as identity and device posture to grant users secure access to internal tools. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare Browser Isolation: Cloudflare Browser Isolation seamlessly executes active webpage content in a secure isolated browser to protect users from zero-day attacks, malware, and phishing. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare CASB: Cloudflare CASB provides comprehensive visibility and control over SaaS apps to prevent data leaks and compliance violations. It helps detect insider threats, shadow IT, risky data sharing, and bad actors. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare Data Loss Prevention (DLP): Cloudflare [Data Loss Prevention](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/access-management/what-is-dlp/) (DLP) allows you to scan your web traffic and SaaS applications for the presence of sensitive data such as social security numbers, financial information, secret keys, and source code. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare DEX: Cloudflare Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) provides visibility into device, network, and application performance across your Zero Trust Organization. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare Gateway: Cloudflare Gateway is a modern next-generation firewall between your user, device, or network and the public Internet. It includes DNS filtering to inspect and apply policies to all Internet-bound DNS queries. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare Mesh: Connects private networks, servers, and devices through Cloudflare for bidirectional, site-to-site, and mesh connectivity. Every participant receives a private Mesh IP address and can reach any other participant directly. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare One: The name for Cloudflare's Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) platform, which includes Zero Trust and network services. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare One Agent: The name of the Cloudflare One Client app on iOS and Android devices. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare One Client: An application that connects corporate devices to Cloudflare for private network access, advanced web filtering, and other security functions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare Tunnel: Cloudflare Tunnel uses a software agent (cloudflared) to establish a secure connection between a private network and Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Cloudflare Zero Trust: Cloudflare Zero Trust provides the power of Cloudflare's global network to your internal teams and infrastructure. It empowers users with secure, fast, and seamless access to any device on the Internet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] cloudflared: The software powering Cloudflare Tunnel. It runs on origin servers to connect applications or private networks to Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] cloudflared replica: An additional instance of cloudflared that points to the same Cloudflare Tunnel. It ensures that your network remains online in case a single host running cloudflared goes down. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] daemon: A program that performs tasks without active management or maintenance. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] device posture: A way to evaluate the security of a user's device, for example by verifying its serial number or checking if it has the latest software updates. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] device profile: A collection of Cloudflare One Client settings applied to a specific set of devices in your organization. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] device registration: An individual session of the Cloudflare One Client on a physical device, with associated configuration including a unique public key, device profile, and virtual IP addresses (one IPv4 and one IPv6). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] DNS filtering: DNS filtering uses the Domain Name System to block malicious websites and filter out harmful content, enhancing security and access control. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] DNS location: DNS locations are a collection of DNS endpoints which can be mapped to physical entities such as offices, homes, or data centers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] DoH subdomain: A unique DoH subdomain for each DNS location in Cloudflare One used in Cloudflare One Client settings. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] fleet: A fleet is a collection of user devices. All devices in a fleet have the Cloudflare One Client installed and are connected to a [Zero Trust Organization](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/setup/#create-a-zero-trust-organization). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Hops: Hops refer to the stops an email makes as it travels from the sender to the recipient. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] identity provider: An identity provider (IdP) stores and manages users' digital identities, enabling single sign-on and authentication for multiple applications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] initial resolved IP: A unique, ephemeral IP address that Gateway assigns to DNS queries when filtering network traffic by hostname. The IP is randomly selected from an IPv4 range (172.64.128.0/20 by default, configurable per account) or an IPv6 range (2606:4700:0cf1:4000::/64, not configurable). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] JSON web token: A compact way to securely transmit information between parties as a JSON object, often used for authentication. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] locally-managed tunnel: A Cloudflare Tunnel that was created by running cloudflared tunnel create <NAME> on the command line. Tunnel configuration is stored in your local cloudflared directory. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] managed network: A network location, such as an office, that is associated with a specific Cloudflare One Client device profile. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] MCP client: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) client is an AI program that can request information and receive responses from an MCP server. Examples of MCP clients include Claude Desktop, Cursor AI, and Windsurf. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] MCP server: A web application that allows AI agents to access third-party data sources and APIs using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). For example, you can use an MCP server to connect an AI assistant to your Google Drive account. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] MCP server portal: A web application in Cloudflare One that serves as a gateway to multiple MCP servers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] MCP server tool: An integration provided by an MCP server which allows an AI agent to perform a limited set of actions on a third-party system. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] MDM file: A Mobile Device Management (MDM) file is a configuration file that allows organizations to manage the software, settings, and certificates installed on their devices. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Mesh IP: A private IP address assigned to each device and node enrolled in Cloudflare Mesh from the 100.96.0.0/12 CGNAT range. Mesh IPs are the same as Cloudflare One Client device IPs. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] MFA: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) checks multiple aspects of a user's identity, not only their username and password, before allowing them access to an application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] OAuth: A protocol for authorizing users, allowing them to perform actions and view data on different platforms without sharing credentials. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] OIDC: OpenID Connect (OIDC) is an identity authentication protocol built on top of OAuth 2.0\. It is used verifying user identity and obtaining basic profile information. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] on-ramp: Refers to a way of connecting a business network to Cloudflare. Examples of on-ramps, or ways to connect to Cloudflare, are Anycast GRE tunnels, Anycast IPsec tunnels, Cloudflare Network Interconnect (CNI), Cloudflare Tunnel, and the Cloudflare One Client. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] PAC file: A file containing a JavaScript function which can instruct a browser to forward traffic to a proxy server instead of directly to the destination server. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] policy: A set of rules that regulate network activity, such as login access and website reachability. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Quarantine policies: Policies that block specific types of emails (usually malicious and suspicious emails), preventing emails from reaching the end-user or the next mail service provider. Emails that are quarantined are reviewed by administrators and potentially released if falsely flagged. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] RDP: Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) allows remote desktop connections to a computer, often used on Windows and Mac operating systems. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] remotely-managed tunnel: A Cloudflare Tunnel whose configuration is stored on Cloudflare rather than on your local machine. You can manage the tunnel in the dashboard or by using the API. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Rule group: A set of Access rules that can be configured once and then quickly applied across many Access policies. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SafeSearch: SafeSearch is a feature of search engines that filters explicit or offensive content from search results. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SAML: Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) enables single sign-on and authentication for multiple applications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SASE: Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) is a cloud-based security model bundling networking and security functions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SCIM: System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) is an open standard protocol that allows identity providers (such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID) to synchronize user identity information with cloud applications and services. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] seat: A unique, billable user within your Zero Trust organization who has performed [an authentication event](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/users/seat-management/#authentication-events). Service tokens do not consume seats. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] service provider (SP): A service provider (SP) provides federated access to an application for a user from an identity provider (IdP). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] service token: Authentication credentials generated by Cloudflare Access which enable automated systems to access protected applications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] session: An event generated when a user logs in to an Access application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] shadow IT: Shadow IT is the unsanctioned use of software, hardware, or other systems and services within an organization, often without the knowledge of that organization's information technology (IT) department. For more information, refer to the [Cloudflare Learning Center](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/access-management/what-is-shadow-it/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SMB: Secure Messaging Block (SMB) is a network file sharing protocol used for accessing files and services on a network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SSH: Secure Shell (SSH) protocol allows users to connect to infrastructure remotely and execute commands. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] SSO: Single Sign-On (SSO) is a technology that combines multiple application logins into one, requiring users to enter credentials only once. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] target: A resource with an IP address or hostname that is reachable by Cloudflare, such as a server or web application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] target hostname: A label used to identify a set of targets in an Access for Infrastructure application. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] team domain: A unique subdomain assigned to your Cloudflare account (for example, <your-team-name>.cloudflareaccess.com), where users will find the apps you have secured behind Cloudflare One. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] team name: The customizable portion of your team domain (<your-team-name>.cloudflareaccess.com). You can view your team name in Cloudflare One under **Settings**. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Terraform: An infrastructure as code software tool that allows you to deploy services from different providers using a standardized configuration syntax. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] tunnel: A secure pathway for network traffic to flow between a device and Cloudflare's global network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] User risk score: Ranks the likelihood of a user to introduce risk to your organization's systems and data based on the detection of security risk behaviors. Risk scores add user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) to the Cloudflare One platform. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] User risk score level: Cloudflare One assigns a risk score of Low, Medium or High based on detections of users' activities, posture, and settings. A user's risk score is equal to the highest-level risk behavior they trigger. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Virtual network: A software abstraction that allows you to logically segregate resources on a private network. Virtual networks are especially useful for exposing resources which have overlapping IP routes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Virtual Private Cloud (VPC): A secure, isolated private network hosted on public cloud infrastructure. Examples of public cloud providers include Google Cloud, AWS, and Microsoft Azure. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Virtual Private Network (VPN): A tool that allows users to send and receive data across shared or public networks as if their devices were directly connected to the private network. For example, employees working from home can use a VPN to access files on the corporate network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] WARP CGNAT IP: A unique, virtual IP address assigned to each Cloudflare One Client device from the 100.96.0.0/12 range. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] WARP client: The previous name for the Cloudflare One Client, an application that connects corporate devices to Cloudflare for private network access, advanced web filtering, and other security functions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] WARP Connector: The previous name for Cloudflare Mesh, a networking product that connects private networks, servers, and devices through Cloudflare for bidirectional, site-to-site, and mesh connectivity. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Zero Trust Security: Zero Trust Security is an IT security model that requires strict identity verification for every person and device accessing resources on a network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/glossary/#glossary

- [definition] Check permissions in the third-party application — Ensure the account you are using to authorize the integration has the necessary administrative privileges in the third-party application (for example, **Global Administrator** for Microsoft 365, **Super Admin** for Google Workspace, or **Organization Owner** for GitHub). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#check-permissions-in-the-third-party-application
- [definition] Clear previous installations — If the SaaS application was previously integrated with a different Cloudflare account, you must manually revoke the old Cloudflare application from within the SaaS provider's admin console. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#clear-previous-installations
- [definition] Verify OAuth permissions — During setup, CASB will ask you to approve a set of permissions. The permissions requested are required for the CASB service to scan for misconfigurations and, if you choose, to take remediation actions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#verify-oauth-permissions
- [definition] Findings are stale or not updating after remediation — A common point of confusion is when a resolved issue (for example, when a file is made private, or when a user is suspended) continues to appear as an active finding in the CASB dashboard. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#findings-are-stale-or-not-updating-after-remediation
- [definition] Understand scan frequency — CASB integrations do not provide real-time updates. Scans are performed periodically to discover new findings and validate the status of existing ones. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#understand-scan-frequency
- [definition] Remediation action fails in the dashboard — If you attempt to use a one-click remediation action (such as "Make private") on a finding, it may result in a **Failed** status, often with a timeout error. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#remediation-action-fails-in-the-dashboard
- [definition] Verify permissions — The remediation failure may be due to the permissions for the Cloudflare app being changed or revoked in the SaaS application after the initial setup. Re-validate the integration to ensure all required permissions are still granted. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#verify-permissions
- [definition] Remediate manually — As a workaround, remediate the finding directly within the SaaS application (for example, change the file's sharing settings in Google Drive). CASB will clear the finding from the dashboard after the next successful scan. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#remediate-manually
- [definition] Webhook test or delivery fails — If Cloudflare cannot deliver a test request or a posture finding instance to your destination, follow these steps. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#webhook-test-or-delivery-fails
- [definition] Check destination requirements — Verify that the destination URL uses `https://` and is publicly reachable. Cloudflare rejects destinations that resolve to localhost, loopback, private, or other reserved addresses. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#check-destination-requirements
- [definition] Check authentication settings — Ensure that the webhook's authentication method matches what your receiver expects. Re-enter any bearer token, Basic auth credentials, static headers, or signing secret if needed. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#check-authentication-settings
- [definition] Understand delivery timing — Test delivery sends a test request immediately, but posture finding instance sends are queued in the background. A success message means that Cloudflare accepted the request for delivery. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#understand-delivery-timing
- [definition] CASB is generating false positives — CASB may incorrectly flag items, such as flagging internally-shared files as public or archived Google Workspace users as inactive. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#casb-is-generating-false-positives
- [definition] Review finding details — Carefully examine the evidence provided in the finding. An object's status in the SaaS platform may not be accurate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#review-finding-details
- [definition] Report the issue — If you confirm the finding is a false positive, report the behavior to Cloudflare Support. Provide the finding ID and as much detail as possible. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#report-the-issue
- [definition] Hide the finding — While Cloudflare investigates the issue, you can [ignore the finding or hide individual instances](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/cloud-and-saas-findings/manage-findings/#hide-findings) to remove it from your active list and reduce noise. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/integrations/cloud-and-saas/troubleshooting/casb/#hide-the-finding

- [parameter] Zero-touch branch office deployment: [Cloudflare One Appliance](#cloudflare-one-appliance) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectivity-options/#choose-the-right-cloudflare-one-connectivity-option
- [parameter] Connect cloud VPCs (AWS, Azure, GCP) with minimal configuration: [Multi-Cloud Networking](#multi-cloud-networking) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectivity-options/#choose-the-right-cloudflare-one-connectivity-option

- [parameter] High-throughput enterprise connectivity: [Cloudflare One Appliance](#cloudflare-one-appliance) or [CNI](#cloudflare-network-interconnect-cni) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectivity-options/#choose-the-right-cloudflare-one-connectivity-option
- [parameter] Security / InfoSec: Recommended starting point=[Cloudflare Tunnel](#cloudflare-tunnel) \+ [Cloudflare One Client](#cloudflare-one-client); Rationale=Minimal network infrastructure changes required. - [parameter] **Deployment model**: Cloudflare Mesh=Software on Linux host (can run alongside other workloads); Cloudflare One Appliance=Dedicated hardware appliance or virtual machine — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectivity-options/#cloudflare-mesh-and-cloudflare-one-appliance-comparison
- [parameter] **Best for**: Cloudflare Mesh=Cloud VPCs, development environments, smaller deployments with an available Linux host; Cloudflare One Appliance=Enterprise branch offices, data centers, sites requiring high throughput (1 Gbps+) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectivity-options/#cloudflare-mesh-and-cloudflare-one-appliance-comparison
- [parameter] **Platform support**: Cloudflare Mesh=Linux only (x86\_64, ARM64). - [parameter] **High availability**: Cloudflare Mesh=[Active-passive replicas](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/high-availability/) for nodes with routes; Cloudflare One Appliance=Supported through multiple connectors per site — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectivity-options/#cloudflare-mesh-and-cloudflare-one-appliance-comparison
- [parameter] **Management**: Cloudflare Mesh=Configured as a device in the Cloudflare One Client settings; Cloudflare One Appliance=Centralized through the Cloudflare WAN dashboard with zero-touch provisioning — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectivity-options/#cloudflare-mesh-and-cloudflare-one-appliance-comparison
- [parameter] Cloudflare Mesh + Cloudflare WAN: Compatible=Conditional; Notes=Requires [Cloudflare One Unified Routing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/traffic-steering/#unified-routing-mode-beta). - [parameter] Cloudflare One Client + Cloudflare WAN: Compatible=Yes; Notes=Cloudflare One Client users can access Cloudflare WAN-connected sites. - [parameter] SRCNAT\_ENABLED: Controls [source NAT](#source-nat). Defaults to true. Accepts true, false, 1, or 0. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#runtime-configuration
- [parameter] /var/lib/cloudflare-warp: Stores registration state. Persist this path with a volume to maintain a stable Mesh identity across container recreation. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#runtime-configuration
- [parameter] NET\_ADMIN: Creates and configures the tunnel interface, routing, and nftables rules. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#runtime-configuration
- [parameter] NET\_RAW: Enables raw-socket operations such as ICMP. Docker normally grants this capability by default, but it is declared explicitly here. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#runtime-configuration
- [parameter] /dev/net/tun: Creates the WARP TUN interface. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#runtime-configuration
- [parameter] IP-forwarding sysctls: Required when the node forwards traffic for routed subnets. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#runtime-configuration

- [definition] Supported architectures — The `latest` tag is a multi-platform manifest. Docker automatically selects the appropriate image for the host architecture. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#supported-architectures
- [definition] Prerequisites — Before starting the container, create a Mesh node and copy its token. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#prerequisites
- [definition] Deploy with Docker Compose — Docker Compose is the recommended way to run a Mesh node alongside your application services. Add a `cloudflare-mesh` service to your `compose.yaml`: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#deploy-with-docker-compose
- [definition] Deploy with Docker CLI — For a standalone container without Compose: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#deploy-with-docker-cli
- [definition] Deploy on Kubernetes — This example creates a one-replica `StatefulSet` with persistent registration state. It requires a Kubernetes cluster that permits `NET_ADMIN`, `NET_RAW`, and `/dev/net/tun` host access (for example, GKE Standard). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#deploy-on-kubernetes
- [definition] 2\. Apply the manifest — Save the following as `cloudflare-mesh.yaml`: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#2-apply-the-manifest
- [definition] Kubernetes sidecar — To connect an application container to Mesh, add the Mesh image as a sidecar in the same Pod. Containers in a Pod share the network namespace, so the Mesh sidecar connects the application to Cloudflare without any application changes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#kubernetes-sidecar
- [definition] 1\. Create the token Secret — Create a separate Mesh node and Kubernetes Secret for the sidecar: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#1-create-the-token-secret
- [definition] 2\. Apply the manifest — Save the following as `cloudflare-mesh-sidecar.yaml`: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#2-apply-the-manifest
- [definition] Source NAT — Source NAT (masquerading) is enabled by default (`SRCNAT_ENABLED=true`). When a Mesh node receives traffic from the Cloudflare edge and forwards it to a destination on the local network, it translates the source IP from the Mesh CGNAT address (`100.96.x.x`) to the node's own local interface IP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#source-nat
- [definition] Hostname routes — Containers support [hostname routing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/routes/#hostname-routes). To resolve Kubernetes Services through a hostname route, make sure the hostname matches the cluster's actual DNS suffix. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#hostname-routes
- [definition] Site-to-site networking — Deploy a separate Mesh node container at each site with a separate node token for each node identity. Each node should advertise its locally reachable subnet as a [CIDR route](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/routes/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#site-to-site-networking
- [definition] Node registers as a regular Cloudflare One Client device — Confirm that the correct Mesh node token is set in `MESH_NODE_TOKEN`. Existing registration state in the persistent volume takes precedence — remove the volume only when you intentionally want to discard that registration and create a new identity. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#node-registers-as-a-regular-cloudflare-one-client-device
- [definition] `warp-cli status` remains Connecting — Check the token, device profile, Gateway proxy, Split Tunnel configuration, outbound firewall connectivity, and container logs: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#warp-cli-status-remains-connecting
- [definition] A Kubernetes Service cannot be resolved — Confirm that the [hostname route](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/routes/#hostname-routes) matches the cluster's actual DNS suffix. The usual default is `cluster.local`, producing Service names such as `service.namespace.svc.cluster.local`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#a-kubernetes-service-cannot-be-resolved
- [definition] A hostname request arrives but no response returns — Check source NAT and return routing first. Verify `SRCNAT_ENABLED` is set to `true` or that your network has return routes to the Mesh IP range. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/containers/#a-hostname-request-arrives-but-no-response-returns

- [definition] Cloud VPC deployments — When deploying Mesh nodes in a cloud VPC, you may need to configure additional provider settings so the node can forward traffic for other devices on the subnet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/tips/#cloud-vpc-deployments

- [definition] Running Mesh alongside other VPN or mesh software — The Cloudflare One Client creates a virtual network interface and manages the system routing table. Other software that does the same — Tailscale, WireGuard, OpenVPN, Cisco AnyConnect, GlobalProtect, ZScaler, Netskope, or any traditional VPN client — will compete for control of routing. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/tips/#running-mesh-alongside-other-vpn-or-mesh-software
- [definition] Running Mesh with Cloudflare Tunnel — A Mesh node (`warp-cli`) and [Cloudflare Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/) (`cloudflared`) can run on the same Linux host. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/tips/#running-mesh-with-cloudflare-tunnel
- [definition] Routing between Mesh and Cloudflare WAN — To route traffic between Cloudflare Mesh and [Cloudflare WAN](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/) (for example, reaching a Mesh node from a WAN-connected site or vice versa), your account must be on [Unified Routing mode… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/tips/#routing-between-mesh-and-cloudflare-wan
- [definition] Connect Workers to Mesh — Cloudflare Workers can connect to your Mesh network using [VPC Network bindings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/configuration/vpc-networks/). Bind to `cf1:network` to reach any Mesh node, client device, or subnet route in your account — without specifying a particular tunnel UUID. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/tips/#connect-workers-to-mesh
- [definition] Source IPs for Cloudflare services — When Cloudflare services (such as [Load Balancing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/) health checks or [Workers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/)) send traffic to your private network through a Mesh node, the traffic originates from the Cloudflare source IP range… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/tips/#source-ips-for-cloudflare-services
- [definition] MTU and packet fragmentation — Mesh nodes use encapsulation to route traffic, which adds overhead to each packet. This is especially relevant for traffic between two Mesh participants, where the packet may be encapsulated twice (once by the sending node, and again by Cloudflare before delivery to the receiving side). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/tips/#mtu-and-packet-fragmentation

- [definition] Required for tunnel operation — `cloudflared` connects to Cloudflare's global network on port `7844`. To use Cloudflare Tunnel, your firewall must allow outbound connections to the following destinations on port `7844` (via UDP if using the `quic` protocol or TCP if using the `http2` protocol). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-with-firewall/#required-for-tunnel-operation
- [definition] Region US — When using the [\--region us](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/run-parameters/#region) flag, ensure your firewall allows outbound connections to these US-region destinations on port `7844` (TCP/UDP). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-with-firewall/#region-us
- [definition] Region FedRAMP High — When deploying `cloudflared` in a [FedRAMP High ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-for-government/) environment, `cloudflared` automatically routes to FedRAMP data centers based on the [tunnel… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-with-firewall/#region-fedramp-high
- [definition] Optional — Opening port `443` enables some optional features. Failure to allow these connections may prompt a log error, but `cloudflared` will still run correctly. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-with-firewall/#optional
- [definition] Cloud VM firewall — If you host your services on a virtual machine (VM) instance in a cloud provider, you may set up instance-level firewall rules to block all ingress traffic and allow only egress traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-with-firewall/#cloud-vm-firewall
- [definition] OS firewall — Alternatively, you may use operating system (OS)-level firewall rules to block all ingress traffic and allow only egress traffic. For example, if your server runs on Linux, you may use `iptables` to set up firewall rules: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-with-firewall/#os-firewall
- [definition] Test with dig — To test your connectivity to Cloudflare, you can use the `dig` command to query the hostnames listed above. - [parameter] cloudflared tunnel create <NAME or UUID>: Creates a tunnel, registers it with the Cloudflare edge and generates a credential file to run this tunnel. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-tunnels
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel --config path/config.yaml run <NAME or UUID>: Runs a tunnel, creating highly available connections between your server and the Cloudflare edge. You can provide name or UUID of the tunnel to run either as the last command line argument or in the configuration file using tunnel: <NAME>. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-tunnels
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel info <NAME or UUID>: Displays details about the active connectors for a given tunnel identified by name of UUID. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-tunnels
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel cleanup <NAME or UUID>: Deletes connections for tunnels with the given UUIDs or names. This is useful if you get an error trying to delete or run a tunnel after cloudflared is not shut down gracefully (for example, if a kill command is issued). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-tunnels
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel cleanup --connector-id <CONNECTOR-ID> <NAME or UUID>: Disconnects and deletes a [cloudflared replica](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-availability/) with the given connector ID. You can view all replicas for a tunnel by running cloudflared tunnel info <NAME or UUID>. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-tunnels
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel delete <NAME or UUID>: Deletes tunnels with the given name or UUID. A tunnel cannot be deleted if it has active connections. To delete the tunnel unconditionally, use the \-f flag. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-tunnels
- [parameter] cloudflared tail <UUID>: Start a session to livestream logs from a specific tunnel. For more information, refer to [Tunnel logs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/monitor-tunnels/logs/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-tunnels
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel route dns: Creates a DNS CNAME record hostname that points to the tunnel. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-published-applications
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel route lb <NAME or UUID> <hostname> <load balancer pool>: Adds a tunnel as an endpoint in a [load balancer pool](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/routing-to-tunnel/public-load-balancers/). A new load balancer and pool will be created if necessary. <hostname>: the public-facing hostname of the load balancer, for example… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-published-applications
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel route ip add <IP/CIDR> <NAME or UUID>: Adds any network route space (represented as a CIDR) to your routing table. That network space becomes reachable for requests egressing from a user's machine as long as it is using the Cloudflare One Client and is enrolled in the same account that is running the tunnel chosen here. Further, those requests will be proxied to the specified… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-private-networks
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel route ip show (or list): Shows your organization's private routing table. You can use additional flags to filter the results. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-private-networks
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel route ip delete: Deletes the row for a given CIDR from your routing table. That portion of your network will no longer be reachable by the Cloudflare One Client. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-private-networks
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel route ip get <IP/CIDR>: Checks which row of the routing table will be used to proxy a given IP. This helps check and validate your configuration. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-private-networks
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel vnet add <NAME or UUID>: Creates a Virtual Network to which IP routes can be assigned. To make this Virtual Network the default for your Zero Trust organization, use the \-d flag. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-private-networks
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel vnet delete <NAME or UUID>: Deletes the Virtual Network with the given name or UUID. Before you can delete a Virtual Network, you must first delete all IP routes assigned to the Virtual Network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-private-networks
- [parameter] cloudflared tunnel vnet list: Displays all active Virtual Networks, the default Virtual Network, and their creation times. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/local-management/tunnel-useful-commands/#manage-private-networks

## Useful terms
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/ — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#on-this-page
- [definition] Useful terms — Last updated Jun 23, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#useful-terms
- [definition] Tunnel — A tunnel is a secure, outbound-only pathway you can establish between your origin and Cloudflare's global network. Each tunnel you create will be assigned a [name](#tunnel-name) and a [UUID](#tunnel-uuid). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#tunnel
- [definition] Tunnel UUID — A tunnel UUID is an alphanumeric, unique ID assigned to a tunnel. The tunnel UUID can be used whenever you need to reference a specific tunnel. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#tunnel-uuid
- [definition] Tunnel name — A tunnel name is a unique, user-friendly identifier that you choose for a tunnel. Since a tunnel can proxy traffic to multiple services, tunnel names do not need to be hostnames. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#tunnel-name
- [definition] Connector — The connector, referred to as `cloudflared`, establishes connectivity from your origin server to the Cloudflare global network. Each `cloudflared` instance creates four long-lived connections to at least two distinct data centers within Cloudflare's global network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#connector
- [definition] Replica — A replica is an additional instance of `cloudflared` running the same tunnel on a different host. You can create and configure a tunnel once, then run it through multiple replicas for redundancy. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#replica
- [definition] Remotely-managed tunnel — A remotely-managed tunnel is a [tunnel](#tunnel) that was created in the Cloudflare dashboard under **Networking** \> **Tunnels**. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#remotely-managed-tunnel
- [definition] Locally-managed tunnel — A locally-managed tunnel is a [tunnel](#tunnel) that was created by running `cloudflared tunnel create <NAME>` on the command line. Tunnel configuration is stored in your local [cloudflared directory](#default-cloudflared-directory). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#locally-managed-tunnel
- [definition] Quick tunnels — Quick tunnels, when run, will generate a URL that consists of a random subdomain of the website `trycloudflare.com`, and point traffic to localhost on port `8080`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#quick-tunnels
- [definition] Virtual networks — A [virtual network](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/private-net/cloudflared/tunnel-virtual-networks/) is a software abstraction that allows you to logically segregate resources on your private network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/get-started/tunnel-useful-terms/#virtual-networks

- [definition] I see `cloudflared service is already installed`. — If you see this error when installing a remotely-managed tunnel, ensure that no other `cloudflared` instances are running as a service on this machine. Only a single instance of `cloudflared` may run as a service on any given machine. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#i-see-cloudflared-service-is-already-installed
- [definition] I see `An A, AAAA, or CNAME record with that host already exists`. — If you are unable to save your tunnel's public hostname, choose a different hostname or delete the existing DNS record. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#i-see-an-a-aaaa-or-cname-record-with-that-host-already-exists
- [definition] Tunnel credentials file does not exist or is not a file. — If you encounter the following error when running a tunnel, double check your `config.yml` file and ensure that the `credentials-file` points to the correct location. You may need to change `/root/` to your home directory. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#tunnel-credentials-file-does-not-exist-or-is-not-a-file
- [definition] My tunnel fails to authenticate. — To start using Cloudflare Tunnel, a super administrator in the Cloudflare account must first log in through `cloudflared login`. The client will launch a browser window and prompt the user to select a hostname in their Cloudflare account. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#my-tunnel-fails-to-authenticate
- [definition] I see an error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority. — This means the origin is using a certificate that `cloudflared` does not trust. For example, you may get this error if you are using SSL/TLS inspection in a proxy between your server and Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#i-see-an-error-x509-certificate-signed-by-unknown-authority
- [definition] I see an error 1033 when attempting to run a tunnel. — A `1033` error indicates your tunnel is not connected to Cloudflare's network because Cloudflare's network cannot find a healthy `cloudflared` instance to receive the traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#i-see-an-error-1033-when-attempting-to-run-a-tunnel
- [definition] I see a 502 Bad Gateway error when connecting to an HTTP or HTTPS application through tunnel. — A `502 Bad Gateway` error with `Unable to reach the origin service. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#i-see-a-502-bad-gateway-error-when-connecting-to-an-http-or-https-application-through-tunnel
- [definition] I see `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS` when attempting to connect to an Access self-hosted app. — This error occurs when `cloudflared` does not recognize the SSL/TLS certificate presented by your origin. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#i-see-err-too-many-redirects-when-attempting-to-connect-to-an-access-self-hosted-app
- [definition] `cloudflared access` shows an error `websocket: bad handshake`. — This means that your `cloudflared access` client is unable to reach your `cloudflared tunnel` origin. To diagnose this, look at the `cloudflared tunnel` logs. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#cloudflared-access-shows-an-error-websocket-bad-handshake
- [definition] Tunnel connections fail with SSL error. — If `cloudflared` returns error `error="remote error: tls: handshake failure"`, check to make sure the hostname in question is covered by a SSL certificate. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#tunnel-connections-fail-with-ssl-error
- [definition] Tunnel connections fail with `Too many open files` error. — If your [Cloudflare Tunnel logs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/monitor-tunnels/logs/) return a `socket: too many open files` error, it means that `cloudflared` has exhausted the open files limit on your machine. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#tunnel-connections-fail-with-too-many-open-files-error
- [definition] I see `failed to sufficiently increase receive buffer size` in my cloudflared logs. — This buffer size increase is reported by the [quic-go library ↗](https://github.com/quic-go/quic-go) leveraged by [cloudflared ↗](https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#i-see-failed-to-sufficiently-increase-receive-buffer-size-in-my-cloudflared-logs
- [definition] Cloudflare Tunnel is buffering my streaming response instead of streaming it live. — Proxied traffic through Cloudflare Tunnel is buffered by default unless the origin server includes the `Content-Type: text/event-stream` response header. This header tells `cloudflared` to stream data as it arrives instead of buffering the entire response. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#cloudflare-tunnel-is-buffering-my-streaming-response-instead-of-streaming-it-live
- [definition] My tunnel randomly disconnects. — Long-lived connections initiated through Cloudflare One, such as SSH sessions, can last up to eight hours. However, disruptions along the service path may result in more frequent disconnects. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#my-tunnel-randomly-disconnects
- [definition] `ping` and `traceroute` commands do not work. — To ping an IP address behind Cloudflare Tunnel, your system must allow ICMP traffic through `cloudflared`. For configuration instructions, refer to the [ICMP proxy documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/proxy/#icmp). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#ping-and-traceroute-commands-do-not-work
- [definition] I see `Error: This route's network is inside an existing subnet's network at "100.96.0.0/12"`. — This error occurs when you try to add a CIDR route that falls within the Cloudflare One Client's CGNAT IP range. The `100.96.0.0/12` range, which covers addresses from `100.96.0.1` to `100.111.255.254`, is reserved for internal WARP routing and cannot be added as a Cloudflare Tunnel route. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors/#i-see-error-this-routes-network-is-inside-an-existing-subnets-network-at-100960012

- [definition] Prerequisites — You need to purchase [Cloudflare WAN ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/magic-wan/) before you can purchase and use Cloudflare One Appliance. - [definition] Before you begin — There are a couple of decisions you need to make when installing your Cloudflare One Appliance. - [definition] Port speeds — The hardware version of the Cloudflare One Appliance includes two [SFP+ ports ↗](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small%5FForm-factor%5FPluggable) that support 10G throughput, as well as six RJ45 ports that support 1G throughput. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#port-speeds

- [definition] Create a new profile — You need to create a profile for your appliance before connecting it to the Internet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#create-a-new-profile
- [definition] Create a WAN — When you have more than one anycast IP configured in your account (set up during your Cloudflare WAN (formerly Magic WAN) onboarding), Cloudflare One Appliance will automatically create at most two tunnels per WAN port. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#create-a-wan

- [definition] Add your Cloudflare One Appliance to a site — After finishing your Cloudflare One Appliance configuration, you need to add it to a site. Sites represent the local network of a data center, office, or other physical location, and combine all on-ramps available there. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#add-your-cloudflare-one-appliance-to-a-site
- [definition] Device installation — There are several deployment options for Cloudflare One Appliance. - [definition] Activate appliance — The Connector is shipped to you deactivated, and will only establish a connection to the Cloudflare network when it is activated. Cloudflare recommends leaving it deactivated until you finish [setting it up in the dashboard](#set-up-cloudflare-dashboard). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#activate-appliance
- [definition] WAN with a static IP address — After activating your device, you can use it in a network configuration with the WAN interface set to a static IP address — that is, an Internet configuration that is not automatically set by DHCP. - [definition] About high availability configurations — You need to deploy two Connectors in your premises before you can set up a site in high availability. When you set up a site in high availability, the WANs and LANs in your Cloudflare One Appliance have the same configuration but are replicated on two nodes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#about-high-availability-configurations
- [definition] Create a high availability configuration — You cannot enable high availability for an existing site. Follow the [Add tunnels](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/configuration/how-to/configure-tunnel-endpoints/#add-tunnels) instructions to create the required IPsec tunnel. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/configuration/third-party/yamaha/#ipsec-tunnels
- [definition] Static routes — Static routes are required for any networks that will be reached via the IPsec tunnel. In our example, there is one network: `172.16.2.0/24`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/configuration/third-party/yamaha/#static-routes
- [definition] RTX router configuration — Use the CLI to configure these settings. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/configuration/third-party/yamaha/#rtx-router-configuration
