## Anti-replay protection
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/ — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#on-this-page
- [definition] Anti-replay protection — Last updated Aug 24, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#anti-replay-protection
- [definition] Replay attacks — Replay attacks occur when a malicious actor intercepts and records a [packet ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/network-layer/what-is-a-packet/), and later sends the recorded packet to the target network again with an intent that benefits the attacker. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#replay-attacks
- [definition] Example — Consider a poorly designed Internet of Things (IoT) garage door opener. The device has a simple protocol for operation: A User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packet contains the garage door password and either `open` or `shut` in its data segment. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#example
- [definition] IPsec anti-replay protection — IPsec anti-replay protection works similarly to the prevention example in the scenario above. The sender assigns each IPsec packet a sequence number. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#ipsec-anti-replay-protection
- [definition] Cloudflare WAN and anti-replay protection — Standard IPsec anti-replay protection assumes a single sender and a single receiver. The sender stores a sequence number in memory and increments it for every packet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#cloudflare-wan-and-anti-replay-protection
- [definition] Additional considerations — IPsec anti-replay protection is extremely important for transport mode - host-to-host or even app-to-app IPsec. In transport mode, an attacker has a relatively easy time identifying the encrypted protocol and identifying which packets to replay if the protocol is even subject to replay attacks. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#additional-considerations
- [definition] Troubleshooting — If you're experiencing tunnel instability or packet drops related to anti-replay protection, refer to [Troubleshoot tunnel health](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/troubleshooting/tunnel-health/#ipsec-tunnel-instability-or-packet-drops). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#troubleshooting

## How Cloudflare calculates tunnel health alerts
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/>

- [snippet] Error budget: number of events x (1 - SLO) = 1,000,000 x (1-0.999) = 1,000 — `number of events x (1 - SLO) = 1,000,000 x (1-0.999) = 1,000` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#error-budget

- [definition] How Cloudflare calculates tunnel health alerts — Last updated Aug 24, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts
- [definition] Service-level indicator (SLI) — SLI is the ratio of positive events to total events. An SLI of 0% means the feature is not working at all, and an SLI of 100% means the feature is fully working as expected. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#service-level-indicator-sli
- [definition] Service-level objectives (SLOs) — SLOs are the threshold for the SLI and set a target level of reliability for IPsec/GRE tunnels. For example, an SLO could be 99.9% of tunnel states being healthy over the past 30 days. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#service-level-objectives-slos
- [definition] Error budget — The error budget is the amount of unsuccessful events that can happen over the course of the SLO time window while maintaining the service at the level of availability the SLO defines. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#error-budget
- [definition] Burn rate — The burn rate measures how fast you expend the error budget over a given time window relative to the SLO window. In the example, an SLO of 99.9% means you can observe 1,000 tunnel health check failures over the course of 30 days. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#burn-rate
- [definition] When Cloudflare alerts you — To determine when to send Tunnel health alerts, Cloudflare relies on a multi-window, multi-burn rate approach. Every five minutes, Cloudflare analyzes the last hour and the last five minutes of data. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#when-cloudflare-alerts-you

- [definition] MTU and MSS — The [maximum transmission unit (MTU) ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/network-layer/what-is-mtu/) is a measurement representing the largest data packet that a network-connected device will accept. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#mtu-and-mss
- [definition] Encapsulation — Since Cloudflare WAN uses encapsulation to deliver its services, it is also important to understand why MTU and MSS matter in this case. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#encapsulation
- [definition] Fragmentation — If the data packet is larger than what the network interface can accept, the network must either drop or fragment it into smaller packets. When fragmentation occurs, Cloudflare only accepts data packets that it can completely reassemble. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#fragmentation
- [definition] Fragmentation in Cloudflare WAN — Consider a UDP datagram of size 3,000 bytes (8 bytes for the UDP header + 2,992 bytes for the UDP data). - [definition] How Cloudflare handles fragments — The following diagram shows how the three UDP fragments in the preceding example flow through Cloudflare and Cloudflare WAN. - [definition] MSS clamping — Maximum segment size (MSS) is a TCP setting that limits the size of TCP segments. The SYN packets set this option during the three-way handshake. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#mss-clamping
- [definition] GRE tunnels as off-ramp — The MSS value depends on how your network is set up. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#gre-tunnels-as-off-ramp
- [definition] IPsec tunnels — For IPsec tunnels, the value you need to specify depends on how your network is set up. The MSS clamping value is lower than for GRE tunnels because the physical interface sees IPsec-encrypted packets, not TCP packets, and MSS clamping does not apply to those. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#ipsec-tunnels

If you are using the Cloudflare WAN Connector, you can also steer traffic based on well-known applications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/traffic-steering/#application-aware-policies

- [definition] Tunnel health checks — Last updated Aug 24, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#tunnel-health-checks
- [definition] Types of health checks — Cloudflare WAN uses two types of health checks: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#types-of-health-checks
- [definition] Tunnel health checks — Tunnel health checks monitor the status of the tunnels that route traffic from Cloudflare to your origin network. Cloudflare WAN relies on these checks to steer traffic to the best available routes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#tunnel-health-checks
- [definition] Endpoint health checks — Endpoint health checks evaluate connectivity from Cloudflare distributed data centers to your origin network. Unlike tunnel health checks, endpoint probes are designed to provide a broad picture of Internet health between Cloudflare and your network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#endpoint-health-checks
- [definition] Tunnel health check attributes — A tunnel health check probe has the following attributes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#tunnel-health-check-attributes
- [definition] Target — A tunnel health check probe tests whether Cloudflare can successfully connect to a specific address or endpoint through the tunnel. The target is the address you want to verify is reachable. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#target
- [definition] Direction — A tunnel health check probe can have two possible directions — unidirectional and bidirectional. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#direction
- [definition] Type — A tunnel health check probe can have two possible types: request and reply. For each type, the source and destination address depends on the direction. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#type
- [definition] Health state and prioritization — There are three tunnel health states: healthy, degraded, and down. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#health-state-and-prioritization
- [definition] Cloudflare data centers and tunnels — In the event a Cloudflare data center is down, Cloudflare's global network does not advertise your prefixes, and Cloudflare routes your packets to the next closest data center. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#cloudflare-data-centers-and-tunnels
- [definition] Recovery — Once a tunnel is in the down state, global network servers continue to emit probes according to the cadence described earlier. When a probe returns healthy, the global network server that received the healthy packet immediately sends two more probes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#recovery
- [definition] Example — Consider two tunnels and their associated routing priorities. Remember that lower route values have priority. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#example
- [definition] Failure response — If the link between Tunnel 1 and Cloudflare becomes unusable, Cloudflare global network servers discover the failure on their next health check probe, and immediately issue two more probes (assuming the tunnel was initially healthy). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#failure-response
- [definition] Recovery response — Suppose the connectivity issue that set Tunnel 1 health to down becomes resolved. At the next health check interval, the issuing global network server receives a successful probe and immediately sends two more probes to validate tunnel health. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#recovery-response
- [definition] Troubleshooting — For help resolving tunnel health issues, refer to [Troubleshoot tunnel health](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/troubleshooting/tunnel-health/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#troubleshooting

- [snippet] Solution: configure terminal — `configure terminal` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/troubleshooting/tunnel-health/#solution
- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/ — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/troubleshooting/tunnel-health/#on-this-page

## WAN transformation
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/ — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#on-this-page
- [parameter] **Performance**: Traditional WAN (MPLS)=Predictable but limited to circuit capacity. High latency for cloud-bound traffic due to backhauling.; SD-WAN=Improved path selection across multiple links. Still relies on branch appliances for processing.; Cloudflare One=Traffic routed to the nearest Cloudflare data center. Cloud-bound traffic egresses locally without backhauling. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#compare-wan-approaches
- [parameter] **Cost model**: Traditional WAN (MPLS)=High fixed costs. Multi-year contracts for private circuits. Per-site hardware investment.; SD-WAN=Lower circuit costs (uses Internet links). Per-site appliance licensing and hardware costs remain.; Cloudflare One=Internet circuit costs only. No per-site hardware required (optional). Pay-as-you-grow model. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#compare-wan-approaches
- [parameter] **Agility**: Traditional WAN (MPLS)=Weeks to months to provision new circuits. Rigid topology changes.; SD-WAN=Faster site deployment over Internet circuits. Still requires appliance staging and configuration.; Cloudflare One=Connect a new site in minutes. Tunnels auto-establish from any Internet connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#compare-wan-approaches
- [parameter] **Security**: Traditional WAN (MPLS)=Security applied at central data center or per-site firewalls.; SD-WAN=Varies by vendor. Some offer integrated security, others require separate appliances.; Cloudflare One=Integrated security at every data center — firewall, secure web gateway, and Zero Trust policies applied inline. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#compare-wan-approaches
- [parameter] **Management**: Traditional WAN (MPLS)=Separate management for WAN circuits, routers, and security appliances.; SD-WAN=Single console for WAN, but security often managed separately.; Cloudflare One=Single dashboard for network connectivity, routing, firewall rules, and security policies. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#compare-wan-approaches
- [definition] WAN transformation — Last updated Aug 24, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#wan-transformation
- [definition] Reduce cost and rigidity — MPLS circuits require multi-year contracts and take weeks or months to provision. Adding a new site means ordering a new circuit. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#reduce-cost-and-rigidity
- [definition] Eliminate Internet breakout tradeoffs — With traditional WANs, you have two options for Internet-bound traffic: backhaul it to a central data center for security inspection (adding latency), or break out directly at the branch (bypassing security controls). Cloudflare One eliminates this tradeoff. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#eliminate-internet-breakout-tradeoffs
- [definition] Avoid vendor lock-in — Proprietary SD-WAN appliances create dependency on a single vendor's hardware and software ecosystem. Cloudflare One uses open standards — IPsec, GRE, and BGP — and works with your existing third-party routers and firewalls. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#avoid-vendor-lock-in
- [definition] Simplify operations — On-premises network and security appliances require manual firmware updates, patching, and capacity planning at every location. With Cloudflare One, networking and security services run in the cloud. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#simplify-operations
- [definition] Plan your migration — WAN transformation is not an all-or-nothing change. Most organizations follow an incremental approach, adding capabilities over time while decommissioning legacy infrastructure as each phase proves out. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#plan-your-migration
- [definition] 1\. Secure user access — Start by replacing VPN concentrators with Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA). Deploy the Cloudflare One Client on user devices and use Cloudflare Access to enforce identity-based policies for application access. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#1-secure-user-access
- [definition] 2\. Connect your networks — Set up site-to-site connectivity by establishing IPsec or GRE tunnels from your existing routers, deploying the Cloudflare One Appliance at branch locations, or using Cloudflare Network Interconnect for private connectivity. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#2-connect-your-networks
- [definition] 3\. Secure Internet egress — Enable Cloudflare Gateway to apply secure web gateway (SWG) policies to Internet-bound traffic from your sites. Add Cloudflare Network Firewall rules to enforce packet-level filtering. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#3-secure-internet-egress
- [definition] 4\. Reduce infrastructure — As Cloudflare handles routing and security in the cloud, you can begin decommissioning branch firewalls, VPN concentrators, and MPLS circuits. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#4-reduce-infrastructure

- [definition] Send specific queries to Gateway — By default, all queries from a configured DNS location will be sent to its DNS resolver IP address to be inspected by Gateway. - [definition] PAC file format — The default Cloudflare PAC file follows a standard format: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#pac-file-format
- [definition] PAC file template with identity provider bypass — When using [authorization endpoints](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/#authorization-endpoint), you must bypass your identity provider (IdP) domains in the PAC file. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#pac-file-template-with-identity-provider-bypass
- [definition] Performance optimization — Browsers evaluate PAC files for every request. Optimizing PAC file performance is critical to avoid delays and issues in web browsing for your users. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#performance-optimization
- [definition] Cache DNS results in variables — When performing DNS resolution with `dnsResolve()`, store the result in a variable to reuse it across multiple checks. This avoids redundant DNS lookups: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#cache-dns-results-in-variables
- [definition] Check for plain hostnames first — NetBIOS names (hostnames without periods) are typically internal and should bypass the proxy. Check for these first: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#check-for-plain-hostnames-first
- [definition] Case sensitivity handling — JavaScript is case-sensitive. Convert hostnames to lowercase for consistent matching: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#case-sensitivity-handling
- [definition] Common bypass rules — When using PAC files for public Internet browsing (not just internal services), you may need to bypass the proxy for certain domains to prevent website functionality issues. The following are common scenarios where your proxy may interfere with traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#common-bypass-rules
- [definition] Font and static asset providers — Font APIs and static asset providers should typically bypass the proxy to prevent rendering issues: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#font-and-static-asset-providers
- [definition] Streaming and media services — Video streaming and large media downloads may perform better with direct connections: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#streaming-and-media-services
- [definition] Apps with certificate pinning — When HTTPS inspection is enabled, applications and services that use certificate pinning reject the Cloudflare-injected certificate and fail to load when routed through the proxy. Bypass these domains in your PAC file: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#apps-with-certificate-pinning
- [definition] Test with expected websites — Before deploying your PAC file to all users in your organization, test it with the websites and applications your users commonly access. This helps ensure: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#test-with-expected-websites
- [definition] Validate syntax — PAC files use JavaScript syntax. A single syntax error (such as a missing closing parenthesis `)` or bracket `]`) will cause the entire PAC file to fail. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#validate-syntax
- [definition] Debug PAC file routing decisions — If you have an issue with proxy routing, most browsers provide debugging tools to verify PAC file behavior: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#debug-pac-file-routing-decisions
- [definition] Browsing on a device using a PAC file is slow — Excessive DNS lookups in the PAC file can cause delays. Review your PAC file and minimize the use of `dnsResolve()`, `isInNet()`, and `isResolvable()` functions. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#browsing-on-a-device-using-a-pac-file-is-slow
- [definition] Browser caches PAC files incorrectly — When you update a PAC file, browsers may continue to use a cached version, causing unexpected behavior. Clear your browser cache and restart the browser after updating the PAC file to ensure the browser uses the latest version. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/resolvers-and-proxies/proxy-endpoints/best-practices/#browser-caches-pac-files-incorrectly

- [definition] Incompatible DNS record types — To block the resolution of queries for DNS records with types other than `A` or `AAAA`, Gateway will respond with the `REFUSED (RCODE:5)` DNS return code. Gateway will block the request but will not display a block page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/custom-pages/gateway-block-page/#incompatible-dns-record-types
- [definition] Third-party filtering conflict — Gateway will not properly filter traffic sent through third-party VPNs or other Internet filtering software, such as [iCloud Private Relay ↗](https://support.apple.com/102602) or [Google Chrome IP Protection ↗](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/ip-protection#ip-protection). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/custom-pages/gateway-block-page/#third-party-filtering-conflict
- [definition] Data center and IP address matching — If an HTTP request that matches a block policy does not arrive at the same Cloudflare data center as its DNS query, Gateway will display the default block page instead of your custom block page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/custom-pages/gateway-block-page/#data-center-and-ip-address-matching

- [definition] Edit a list — 1. In the **Lists** page, locate the list you want to edit. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/lists/#edit-a-list
- [definition] List size — Your lists can include up to 1,000 entries for Standard plans and 5,000 for Enterprise plans. An uploaded CSV file must be smaller than 2 MB. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/lists/#list-size
- [definition] Wildcard entries — Hostname lists do not support wildcard entries (`*.example.com`). You will need to add domains as exact matches. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/lists/#wildcard-entries
- [definition] Non-Latin characters — Gateway supports non-Latin characters by converting all domains and hostnames to [Punycode ↗](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3492.txt). Once you save a list with non-Latin characters, Gateway will display the entry as Punycode. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/lists/#non-latin-characters
- [definition] Duplicate entries — Lists cannot have duplicate entries. Because domains and hostnames are converted to [Punycode](#non-latin-characters), multiple list entries that convert to the same string will count as duplicates. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/lists/#duplicate-entries
- [definition] URL slashes — Gateway ignores trailing forward slashes (`/`) in URLs. For example, `https://example.com` and `https://example.com/` will count as the same URL and may return a duplicate error. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/lists/#url-slashes
- [definition] Extended email addresses — Extended email addresses (also known as plus addresses) are variants of an existing email address with `+` or `.` modifiers. Many email providers, such as Gmail and Outlook, deliver emails intended for an extended address to its original address. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/lists/#extended-email-addresses
- [definition] API rate limit — You can send 600 requests to the [Gateway Lists](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/zero%5Ftrust/subresources/gateway/subresources/lists/) endpoint per minute. If you exceed the rate limit, Cloudflare will block subsequent requests for 120 seconds. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/reusable-components/lists/#api-rate-limit

- [definition] Android devices — If you are deploying the Cloudflare One Agent on Android/ChromeOS, you must also add `cloudflare-dns.com` to your firewall exception list. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#android-devices
- [definition] Client authentication endpoint — When you [log in to your Cloudflare One organization](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/manual-deployment/), you will have to complete the authentication steps required by your organization in the browser window that opens. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#client-authentication-endpoint
- [definition] WARP ingress IP — The Cloudflare One Client connects to the following IP addresses, depending on which [tunnel protocol](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/configure/settings/#device-tunnel-protocol) is configured for your device (WireGuard or MASQUE). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#warp-ingress-ip
- [definition] Captive portal — The following domains are used as part of our captive portal check: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#captive-portal
- [definition] Connectivity checks — As part of establishing the WARP tunnel, the client runs connectivity checks inside and outside of the tunnel. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#connectivity-checks
- [definition] Outside tunnel — The client connects to the following destinations to verify general Internet connectivity outside of the WARP tunnel. Make sure that these IPs and domains are on your firewall allowlist. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#outside-tunnel
- [definition] Inside tunnel — The Cloudflare One Client connects to the following destinations to verify connectivity inside of the WARP tunnel: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#inside-tunnel
- [definition] NEL reporting (optional) — The Cloudflare One Client reports connectivity issues to the Network Error Logging (NEL) endpoint via `a.nel.cloudflare.com`. This is not technically required to operate but will result in errors in our logs if not excluded properly. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#nel-reporting-optional
- [definition] Latency statistics (optional) — The Cloudflare One Client generates ICMP traffic to the [WARP ingress IPs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#warp-ingress-ip) when running tunnel latency tests. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#latency-statistics-optional
- [definition] Time synchronization (optional) — The Cloudflare One Client attempts to synchronize the exact time by NTP (`UDP 123`) to [Cloudflare's Time Service](https://developers.cloudflare.com/time-services/ntp/usage/) via `time.cloudflare.com`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#time-synchronization-optional
- [definition] Required scopes — If your organization does not currently allow inbound/outbound communication over the IP addresses, ports, and domains described above, you must manually add an exception. The rule at a minimum needs to be scoped to the following process based on your platform: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#required-scopes

- [definition] Desktop platforms — Cloudflare One Client releases for Windows, macOS, and Linux come in two forms: beta and stable. Occasionally, a stable release will be declared a Long-Term Support release (LTS). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#desktop-platforms
- [definition] Mobile platforms — Cloudflare One Client releases for iOS, iPadOS, Android, ChromeOS, and ChromeOS Flex are limited to stable releases released via the iOS App Store or Google Play Store. Therefore, security fixes will be shipped via the latest release. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#mobile-platforms
- [definition] Feature deprecation policy — Major features included in a Cloudflare One Client release will not be removed while that release is still receiving security fixes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#feature-deprecation-policy
- [definition] Release schedule — Cloudflare does not operate on a fixed release schedule; all releases for the Cloudflare One Client are incremental. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#release-schedule
- [definition] Supported operating systems — The Cloudflare One Client is guaranteed to support operating systems for the primary maintenance timespan provided by the vendors or maintainers. This is to ensure that security fixes in the Cloudflare One Client are always supported by security fixes in the underlying operating system. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#supported-operating-systems
- [definition] Windows — The Cloudflare One Client support policy for Windows follows [Microsoft's Lifecycle Policy ↗](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#windows
- [definition] macOS — The Cloudflare One Client supports the current major version of macOS and the two previous major versions. Devices on a previous major version must have the latest minor and patch updates installed (for example, `14.8.3`) to receive support. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#macos
- [definition] Debian — The Cloudflare One Client supports all Debian releases within their [standard EOL window ↗](https://www.debian.org/releases/). Devices must be updated to the latest point release (for example, `12.12`) to receive support. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#debian
- [definition] Ubuntu — The Cloudflare One Client supports all Ubuntu releases within their [Standard Security Maintenance window ↗](https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle). Devices must be updated to the latest point release (for example, `22.04.5`) to receive support. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#ubuntu
- [definition] Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) — Cloudflare One Client support for RHEL is pending. Once testing is complete, our policy will be to support all major versions of RHEL within their [Full Support window ↗](https://access.redhat.com/product-life-cycles). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#red-hat-enterprise-linux-rhel
- [definition] iOS and iPadOS — The Cloudflare One Client supports the current major version of iOS and iPadOS as well as the two previous major versions. Devices must have the latest available update installed (for example, `17.7.2`) to receive support. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#ios-and-ipados
- [definition] Android — The Cloudflare One Client supports the current major Android release and the three previous major releases. Devices must have the latest available [Android Security Patch Level ↗](https://source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/asb-overview) installed to receive support. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#android
- [definition] ChromeOS — The Cloudflare One Client supports only the current ChromeOS release on the Stable, LTS, and LTSC channels. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/support-lifecycle/#chromeos

- [definition] 5\. - [definition] 6\. Log in to your organization's Cloudflare Zero Trust instance from your devices. — Once the Cloudflare One Client is installed on the device, [log in to your Zero Trust organization](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/manual-deployment/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/set-up/#6-log-in-to-your-organizations-cloudflare-zero-trust-instance-from-your-devices
- [definition] DNS only mode — This mode is best suited for organizations that only want to apply DNS filtering to outbound traffic from their company devices. It does not enable advanced HTTP filtering features such as HTTP policies, identity-based policies, device posture checks, or Browser Isolation. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/set-up/#dns-only-mode
- [definition] 1\. - [definition] 4\. - [definition] Cause — The device failed to present a [valid mTLS certificate](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/device-enrollment/#check-for-mtls-certificate) during device enrollment. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#cause

Review the [managed deployment guide](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/mdm-deployment/) for your operating system. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#resolution
- [definition] Cause — The device is not connected to a Wi-Fi network or LAN that has connectivity to the Internet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#cause
- [definition] Resolution — 1. Launch the network settings panel on your device. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#resolution
- [definition] Cause — The device is not authenticated to an [organization](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/setup/#2-create-a-zero-trust-organization) because: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#cause
- [definition] Resolution — 1. Launch the Cloudflare One Client. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#resolution
- [definition] Cause — A third-party application or service is intercepting DNS over HTTPS traffic from the Cloudflare One Client. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#cause
- [definition] Resolution — Configure the third-party application to exempt the [WARP DoH IPs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/#doh-ip). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#resolution
- [definition] Cause — A third-party security product on the device or network is performing TLS decryption on HTTPS traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#cause
- [definition] Resolution — In the third-party security product, disable HTTPS inspection and TLS decryption for the [WARP IP addresses](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/deployment/firewall/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#resolution
- [definition] Cause — The account administrator has disconnected the Cloudflare One Client for all devices registered to the account. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#cause
- [definition] Resolution — The account administrator must turn off both of the following features: - [Disconnect the Cloudflare One Client on all devices](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/configure/settings/#disconnect-the-cloudflare-one-client-on-all-devices)… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/client-errors/#resolution

## Common issues
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and- — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#on-this-page
- [definition] Common issues — Last updated Jun 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#common-issues
- [definition] Stuck on "Disconnected" or frequent flapping — If the Cloudflare One Client is stuck in the `Disconnected` state or frequently changes between `Connected` and `Disconnected`, this indicates that the client cannot establish a connection to Cloudflare's global network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#stuck-on-disconnected-or-frequent-flapping
- [definition] Registration error (Authentication Expired) — When registering the client, you may see `Authentication Expired` or `Registration error. Please try again later`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#registration-error-authentication-expired
- [definition] (Linux) DNS connectivity check failed — This error often means that `systemd-resolved` is not allowing the client to resolve DNS requests. In `daemon.log`, you will see `DNS connectivity check failed to resolve host="warp-svc."`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#linux-dns-connectivity-check-failed
- [definition] (Mac/Linux) Invalid character in resolv.conf — The client cannot parse `resolv.conf` files containing invalid characters like `!@#$%^&*()<>?` in `search` directives. Remove these characters to restore service. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#maclinux-invalid-character-in-resolvconf
- [definition] "Your connection is not private" or untrusted warnings — Advanced security features require the [Cloudflare root certificate](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/user-side-certificates/) to be trusted on the device. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#your-connection-is-not-private-or-untrusted-warnings
- [definition] 2025 Certificate migration — Starting with version 2024.12.554.0, the client can automatically install new certificates as soon as they are **Available** in the dashboard. For older versions, certificates had to be marked **In-Use** first. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#2025-certificate-migration
- [definition] Windows shows "No Internet access" — This is often a cosmetic error with Windows Network Connectivity Status Indicator (NCSI). Apps like Outlook or JumpCloud may refuse to connect because of this status. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#windows-shows-no-internet-access
- [definition] Setup Wizard ends prematurely — This usually indicates a missing dependency, such as .NET Framework `4.7.2` or later. Legacy systems (like Windows 10 Enterprise 1607) may require a manual update of the [.NET Framework Runtime ↗](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet-framework/net472). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#setup-wizard-ends-prematurely
- [definition] WSL2 connectivity — If WSL2 loses connectivity, check your [split tunnel configuration](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/configure/route-traffic/split-tunnels/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#wsl2-connectivity
- [definition] SMTP port 25 blocked — The client blocks outgoing traffic on port `25` to prevent spam and reputational harm to IP adresses used by customers. Use port `587` or `465` for encrypted email. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#smtp-port-25-blocked
- [definition] Admin override codes expired — [Admin override codes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/configure/settings/#allow-admin-override-codes) are time-sensitive and adhere to fixed-hour blocks. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#admin-override-codes-expired

- [definition] Windows Server — The Cloudflare One Client does not run on Windows Server. Refer to the [downloads page](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/) for a list of supported operating systems. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#windows-server
- [definition] Cloudflare One Client disconnected on Windows ARM — On Windows devices with ARM-based processors, the Cloudflare One Client can sometimes get [stuck in a disconnected state](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/common-issues/#unable-to-connect-warp) when you connect (such… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#cloudflare-one-client-disconnected-on-windows-arm
- [definition] Managed network on legacy Windows Server — [Managed network detection](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/configure/managed-networks/) will not work when the TLS certificate is served from IIS 8.5 on Windows Server 2012 R2\. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#managed-network-on-legacy-windows-server
- [definition] nslookup on Windows in DoH mode — On Windows devices in [DNS only mode](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/configure/modes/#dns-only-mode), `nslookup` by default sends DNS requests to the [WARP local DNS… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#nslookup-on-windows-in-doh-mode
- [definition] Comcast DNS servers — Comcast DNS traffic (to the IPs below) cannot be proxied through the Cloudflare One Client. This is because Comcast rejects DNS traffic that is not sent directly from the user's device. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#comcast-dns-servers
- [definition] Cox DNS servers — Similar to the [Comcast DNS servers](#comcast-dns-servers) limitation listed above, Cox DNS servers will not respond to traffic from the WARP egress IPs (or any IP that is not a Cox IP). The workaround is nearly identical, except that Cox DNS servers may be specific to the individual end user. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#cox-dns-servers
- [definition] HP Velocity — The HP Velocity driver has a bug which will cause a blue screen error on devices running the Cloudflare One Client. HP recommends [uninstalling this driver ↗](https://support.hp.com/gb-en/document/c06266198). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#hp-velocity
- [definition] Dell firmware version 1.35.0 — For Dell devices running firmware version `1.35.0` (released 2025-07-07), regardless of operating system, Cloudflare has confirmed a bug that prevents the WARP service from starting. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#dell-firmware-version-1350
- [definition] Cisco Meraki — Cisco Meraki devices have a bug where client traffic can sometimes be identified as [Statistical-P2P ↗](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/ios-xml/ios/qos%5Fnbar/prot%5Flib/config%5Flibrary/pp4600/nbar-prot-pack4600/s.html#wp1488575851) and de-prioritised or dropped entirely. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#cisco-meraki
- [definition] Windows Teredo — The [Windows Teredo ↗](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/teredo/about-teredo) interface conflicts with the Cloudflare One Client. Since Teredo and the Cloudflare One Client will fight for control over IPv6 traffic routing, you must disable Teredo on your Windows device. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#windows-teredo
- [definition] Docker on Linux with bridged networking — [Docker ↗](https://www.docker.com/products/container-runtime/) on Linux does not perform the underlying network tunnel MTU changes required by the Cloudflare One Client. This can cause connectivity issues inside of a Docker container when the Cloudflare One Client is enabled on the host machine. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#docker-on-linux-with-bridged-networking
- [definition] Access Cloudflare One Client DNS from Docker — The Cloudflare One Client runs a local DNS proxy on `127.0.2.2` and `127.0.2.3`. You may need access to these addresses from within Docker containers to resolve internal-only or fallback domains. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#access-cloudflare-one-client-dns-from-docker
- [definition] Linux DNS domains with systemd-resolved versions earlier than 252.3 — On some Linux systems with `systemd-resolved` versions earlier than `252.3`, DNS domains configured on non-WARP interfaces may not resolve as expected while the Cloudflare One Client is connected. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#linux-dns-domains-with-systemd-resolved-versions-earlier-than-2523
- [definition] Windows App connection issue — When the Cloudflare One Client is active on a local machine, users may be unable to connect to a Windows 365 PC using the [Windows App ↗](https://aka.ms/WindowsApp). This issue does not affect browser-based connections to Windows 365. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#windows-app-connection-issue
- [definition] Windows 10 in Microsoft 365 Cloud PC is not supported — Use of the Cloudflare One Client in a Microsoft 365 Windows 10 Cloud PC is not supported. To work around this limitation, use Windows 11. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#windows-10-in-microsoft-365-cloud-pc-is-not-supported
- [definition] IPv6 DNS resolution in Traffic only mode — In [Traffic only mode](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/configure/modes/#traffic-only-mode), devices using IPv6 DNS servers may experience connectivity issues if these servers are not manually excluded from the WARP tunnel. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#ipv6-dns-resolution-in-traffic-only-mode
- [definition] Ivanti Secure Access (formerly Pulse Secure) — The Ivanti Secure Access VPN client can conflict with the Cloudflare One Client by installing Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) rules that block outgoing traffic to the [WARP local DNS… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#ivanti-secure-access-formerly-pulse-secure
- [definition] Always-On VPN with Lockdown Mode in Microsoft Intune — If you are using Microsoft Intune to deploy the Cloudflare One Client on Android with [Always-On VPN and Lockdown mode enabled… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#always-on-vpn-with-lockdown-mode-in-microsoft-intune
- [definition] Repeated reinstalls on macOS with Microsoft Intune — When you deploy the Cloudflare One Client `.pkg` to macOS with Microsoft Intune, Intune may repeatedly reinstall the package. Each reinstall restarts the client and briefly drops the WARP connection, and you may see the client reinstalled several times within a single Intune evaluation cycle. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#repeated-reinstalls-on-macos-with-microsoft-intune
- [definition] Windows 11 24H2 performance issues — For Windows 11 24H2 users, Microsoft has confirmed a regression that may lead to performance issues like mouse lag, audio cracking, or other slowdowns. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#windows-11-24h2-performance-issues
- [definition] False positive malware warning on Windows with KB5055523 — Windows devices with KB5055523 installed may receive a warning about `Win32/ClickFix.ABA` being present in the installer. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/troubleshooting/known-limitations/#false-positive-malware-warning-on-windows-with-kb5055523

- [parameter] [Delete a registration](#delete-a-device-registration): What it does=Permanently removes a single device registration and its configuration.; Virtual IPs released?=Yes; When to use=You want to fully remove a user's enrollment from a device and free up the virtual IP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/device-registration/#manage-device-registrations
- [parameter] [Revoke a registration](#revoke-a-device-registration): What it does=Invalidates the registration's public key, blocking it from connecting. - [parameter] [Delete a device](#delete-a-device): What it does=Removes the physical device record and all its associated registrations.; Virtual IPs released?=Yes; When to use=You want to fully remove a device and all associated registrations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/device-registration/#manage-device-registrations

- [definition] Delete a device registration — Devices can have multiple device registrations. - [definition] Seat management (billing) — Deleting a device or a device registration does not affect [seat usage](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/users/seat-management/). Seats are tied to the user identity, not to individual devices. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/device-registration/#seat-management-billing

## WAN transformation
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-trans — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#on-this-page
- [parameter] **Performance**: Traditional WAN (MPLS)=Predictable but limited to circuit capacity. High latency for cloud-bound traffic due to backhauling.; SD-WAN=Improved path selection across multiple links. Still relies on branch appliances for processing.; Cloudflare One=Traffic routed to the nearest Cloudflare data center. Cloud-bound traffic egresses locally without backhauling. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#compare-wan-approaches
- [parameter] **Cost model**: Traditional WAN (MPLS)=High fixed costs. Multi-year contracts for private circuits. Per-site hardware investment.; SD-WAN=Lower circuit costs (uses Internet links). Per-site appliance licensing and hardware costs remain.; Cloudflare One=Internet circuit costs only. No per-site hardware required (optional). Pay-as-you-grow model. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#compare-wan-approaches
- [parameter] **Agility**: Traditional WAN (MPLS)=Weeks to months to provision new circuits. Rigid topology changes.; SD-WAN=Faster site deployment over Internet circuits. Still requires appliance staging and configuration.; Cloudflare One=Connect a new site in minutes. Tunnels auto-establish from any Internet connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#compare-wan-approaches
- [parameter] **Security**: Traditional WAN (MPLS)=Security applied at central data center or per-site firewalls.; SD-WAN=Varies by vendor. Some offer integrated security, others require separate appliances.; Cloudflare One=Integrated security at every data center — firewall, secure web gateway, and Zero Trust policies applied inline. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#compare-wan-approaches
- [parameter] **Management**: Traditional WAN (MPLS)=Separate management for WAN circuits, routers, and security appliances.; SD-WAN=Single console for WAN, but security often managed separately.; Cloudflare One=Single dashboard for network connectivity, routing, firewall rules, and security policies. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#compare-wan-approaches
- [definition] WAN transformation — Last updated Aug 24, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#wan-transformation
- [definition] Reduce cost and rigidity — MPLS circuits require multi-year contracts and take weeks or months to provision. Adding a new site means ordering a new circuit. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#reduce-cost-and-rigidity
- [definition] Eliminate Internet breakout tradeoffs — With traditional WANs, you have two options for Internet-bound traffic: backhaul it to a central data center for security inspection (adding latency), or break out directly at the branch (bypassing security controls). Cloudflare One eliminates this tradeoff. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#eliminate-internet-breakout-tradeoffs
- [definition] Avoid vendor lock-in — Proprietary SD-WAN appliances create dependency on a single vendor's hardware and software ecosystem. Cloudflare One uses open standards — IPsec, GRE, and BGP — and works with your existing third-party routers and firewalls. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#avoid-vendor-lock-in
- [definition] Simplify operations — On-premises network and security appliances require manual firmware updates, patching, and capacity planning at every location. With Cloudflare One, networking and security services run in the cloud. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#simplify-operations
- [definition] Plan your migration — WAN transformation is not an all-or-nothing change. Most organizations follow an incremental approach, adding capabilities over time while decommissioning legacy infrastructure as each phase proves out. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#plan-your-migration
- [definition] 1\. Secure user access — Start by replacing VPN concentrators with Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA). Deploy the Cloudflare One Client on user devices and use Cloudflare Access to enforce identity-based policies for application access. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#1-secure-user-access
- [definition] 2\. Connect your networks — Set up site-to-site connectivity by establishing IPsec or GRE tunnels from your existing routers, deploying the Cloudflare One Appliance at branch locations, or using Cloudflare Network Interconnect for private connectivity. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#2-connect-your-networks
- [definition] 3\. Secure Internet egress — Enable Cloudflare Gateway to apply secure web gateway (SWG) policies to Internet-bound traffic from your sites. Add Cloudflare Network Firewall rules to enforce packet-level filtering. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#3-secure-internet-egress
- [definition] 4\. Reduce infrastructure — As Cloudflare handles routing and security in the cloud, you can begin decommissioning branch firewalls, VPN concentrators, and MPLS circuits. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/wan-transformation/#4-reduce-infrastructure

- [definition] HTTPS filtering — To inspect HTTPS traffic, you need to install a Cloudflare root certificate on each client device. - [definition] DNS filtering — You can configure the DNS resolver for your Cloudflare WAN networks to the shared IP addresses for the Gateway DNS resolver. - [definition] Outbound Internet traffic — By default, the following traffic routed through IPsec/GRE tunnels and destined to public IP addresses is proxied/filtered through Cloudflare Gateway: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-gateway/#outbound-internet-traffic
- [definition] Private traffic — By default, TCP, UDP, and ICMP traffic routed through IPsec/GRE tunnels and destined to routes behind [Cloudflare Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/) will be proxied/filtered through Cloudflare Gateway. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-gateway/#private-traffic
- [definition] Default filtering criteria — When enabled, TCP/UDP traffic meeting **all** the following criteria will be proxied and filtered by Cloudflare Gateway: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-gateway/#default-filtering-criteria
- [definition] Custom filtering criteria — You can specify more specific matches to override the default criteria: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-gateway/#custom-filtering-criteria
- [definition] Test Gateway integration — To check if Gateway is working properly with your Cloudflare WAN connection, open a browser from a host behind your customer premise equipment, and browse to `https://ifconfig.me`. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-gateway/#test-gateway-integration

- [definition] Route evaluation and precedence — Cloudflare evaluates private network routes using longest-prefix-match. A prefix combines a base IP address with a prefix length that indicates how many bits define the network portion (for example, `192.168.0.0/24`). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-tunnel/#route-evaluation-and-precedence
- [definition] Route uniqueness — Within a [virtual network](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/private-net/cloudflared/tunnel-virtual-networks/), each prefix can only appear once in the Zero Trust routing table. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-tunnel/#route-uniqueness
- [definition] Reserved IP ranges — Cloudflare reserves the following IP ranges for Zero Trust services: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-tunnel/#reserved-ip-ranges
- [definition] Interaction with WAN routes — If your account also uses WAN connections (IPsec, GRE, and CNI), route selection behavior depends on your routing mode. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-tunnel/#interaction-with-wan-routes
- [definition] Interaction with other route selection mechanisms — Longest-prefix-match routing is the default route selection method. Other mechanisms can bypass or augment route evaluation. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-tunnel/#interaction-with-other-route-selection-mechanisms
- [definition] Automatic Return Routing (ARR) — [Automatic Return Routing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/traffic-steering/#automatic-return-routing-beta) bypasses route lookup for return traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-tunnel/#automatic-return-routing-arr
- [definition] Hostname Routes (Initial resolved IPs) — [Hostname-based routing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/egress-policies/host-selectors/) uses Gateway DNS to resolve hostnames to Initial resolved IPs, which then map to specific next hops. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/cloudflare-tunnel/#hostname-routes-initial-resolved-ips

- [parameter] **Deployment model**: Cloudflare Mesh=Software on Linux host (can run alongside other workloads); Cloudflare One Appliance=Dedicated hardware appliance or virtual machine — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/connectivity-options/#cloudflare-mesh-and-cloudflare-one-appliance-comparison
- [parameter] **Best for**: Cloudflare Mesh=Cloud VPCs, development environments, smaller deployments with an available Linux host; Cloudflare One Appliance=Enterprise branch offices, data centers, sites requiring high throughput (1 Gbps+) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/connectivity-options/#cloudflare-mesh-and-cloudflare-one-appliance-comparison
- [parameter] **Platform support**: Cloudflare Mesh=Linux only (x86\_64, ARM64). - [parameter] **High availability**: Cloudflare Mesh=[Active-passive replicas](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-mesh/high-availability/) for nodes with routes; Cloudflare One Appliance=Supported through multiple connectors per site — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/zero-trust/connectivity-options/#cloudflare-mesh-and-cloudflare-one-appliance-comparison

## Glossary
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/ — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#on-this-page
- [parameter] anycast: Anycast is a network addressing and routing method in which incoming requests can be routed to a variety of different locations. Anycast typically routes incoming traffic to the nearest data center with the capacity to process the request efficiently. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] data packet: A data packet is a unit of data consisting of user and control information. Information in a network is broken down into packets, that might follow different paths to their final destination. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] equal-cost multi-path routing: A technique that uses hashes calculated from packet data to determine the route chosen. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] GRE tunnel: Stands for generic routing encapsulation. It is a protocol wrapping one data packet within another type of data packet. This is useful for enabling protocols that are not normally supported by a network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] ICMP: Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) is used by network devices to send error messages and other operational information. ICMP is useful for diagnostic purposes, for example. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] Internet key exchange (IKE): The protocol Cloudflare uses to create the IPsec tunnel between Cloudflare WAN and the customer's device. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] IPsec tunnel: Stands for Internet Protocol secure. It is a group of protocols for securing connections between devices, by encrypting IP packets. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] maximum segment size (MSS): MSS limits the size of packets, or small chunks of data, that travel across a network, such as the Internet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] on-ramp: Refers to a way of connecting a business network to Cloudflare. Examples of on-ramps, or ways to connect to Cloudflare, are Anycast GRE tunnels, Anycast IPsec tunnels, Cloudflare Network Interconnect (CNI), Cloudflare Tunnel, and WARP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] static route: A fixed configuration to route traffic through Anycast tunnels from Cloudflare global network to the customer's locations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] subnet: Also known as subnetwork. It refers to a network that is part of another network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] traffic steering: Cloudflare evaluates your route's health and steers traffic according to priorities defined by you and / or tunnel health. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] tunnel health-check: A probe sent by Cloudflare to check for tunnel health. If a tunnel is not considered healthy, Cloudflare reroutes traffic to one that is considered healthy. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [parameter] WAN: Stands for Wide Area Network. It refers to a computer network that connects groups of computers over large distances. WANs are often used by businesses to connect their office networks. The objective is to make each of the local area networks (LANs) be remotely connected and accessible. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
- [definition] Glossary — Last updated Apr 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/glossary/#glossary
