## Configure hardware Appliance
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/>

- [snippet] Create a WAN: curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/magic/sites/{site_id}/wans \ — `curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/magic/sites/{site_id}/wans \` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#create-a-wan
- [snippet] Create a LAN: curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/magic/sites/{site_id}/lans \ — `curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/magic/sites/{site_id}/lans \` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#create-a-lan
- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configura — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#on-this-page
- [parameter] UDP/53: Destination IP/URL=DNS destination IP 1.1.1.1; Purpose=Needed to allow DNS traffic to Cloudflare DNS servers. Cloudflare uses this port for DNS lookups of control plane API. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#firewall-settings-required
- [parameter] TCP/443: Destination IP/URL=\-; Purpose=Cloudflare One Appliance will open outbound HTTPS connections over this port for control plane operations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#firewall-settings-required
- [parameter] UDP/4500: Destination IP/URL=Destination IP 162.159.64.1; Purpose=Needed for Cloudflare One Appliance initialization and discovery through outbound connections. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#firewall-settings-required
- [parameter] UDP/4500: Destination IP/URL=Destination IP - Cloudflare anycast IPs; Purpose=Needed for the Cloudflare anycast IPs assigned to your account for tunnel outbound connections. This traffic is tunnel traffic. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#firewall-settings-required
- [parameter] TCP/7844, UDP/7844: Destination IP/URL=Outbound connections; Purpose=Used to support debugging features in Cloudflare One Appliance. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#firewall-settings-required
- [parameter] UDP/123: Destination IP/URL=http://time.cloudflare.com/; Purpose=Needed for Cloudflare One Appliance to periodically contact Cloudflare's Time Services. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#firewall-settings-required
- [definition] Configure hardware Appliance — Last updated Aug 24, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#configure-hardware-appliance
- [definition] Prerequisites — You need to purchase [Cloudflare WAN ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/magic-wan/) before you can purchase and use Cloudflare One Appliance. Cloudflare One Appliance can function as your primary edge device for your network, or be deployed in-line with existing network gear. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#prerequisites
- [definition] Before you begin — There are a couple of decisions you need to make when installing your Cloudflare One Appliance. Review the following topics for more information. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#before-you-begin
- [definition] Determine the need for a high availability configuration — You can install up to two instances of Cloudflare One Appliance for redundancy at each of your sites. If one of your devices fails, traffic will fail over to the other, ensuring that you never lose connectivity to that site. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#determine-the-need-for-a-high-availability-configuration
- [definition] Decide on DHCP vs static IP connections — You can use Cloudflare One Appliance in both DHCP networks and networks that require a static IP configuration. At first boot, however, Cloudflare One Appliance needs to reach out to Cloudflare to download your settings and go through the activation process. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#decide-on-dhcp-vs-static-ip-connections
- [definition] Port speeds — The hardware version of the Cloudflare One Appliance includes two [SFP+ ports ↗](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small%5FForm-factor%5FPluggable) that support 10G throughput, as well as six RJ45 ports that support 1G throughput. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#port-speeds
- [definition] Register your Appliance — To set up and use the hardware version of Cloudflare One Appliance (formerly Magic WAN Connector), you first need to register it with your account. This is not applicable to Virtual Cloudflare One Appliance. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#register-your-appliance
- [definition] Create a new profile — You need to create a profile for your appliance before connecting it to the Internet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#create-a-new-profile
- [definition] Create a WAN — When you have more than one anycast IP configured in your account (set up during your Cloudflare WAN (formerly Magic WAN) onboarding), Cloudflare One Appliance will automatically create at most two tunnels per WAN port. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#create-a-wan
- [definition] Create a LAN — 1. In **LAN configuration**, select **Create**. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#create-a-lan
- [definition] Add your Cloudflare One Appliance to a site — After finishing your Cloudflare One Appliance configuration, you need to add it to a site. Sites represent the local network of a data center, office, or other physical location, and combine all on-ramps available there. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#add-your-cloudflare-one-appliance-to-a-site
- [definition] Device installation — There are several deployment options for Cloudflare One Appliance. Cloudflare One Appliance can act like a DHCP server for your local network, or integrate with your local setup and have static IP addresses assigned to it. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#device-installation
- [definition] Activate appliance — The Cloudflare One Appliance is shipped to you deactivated, and will only establish a connection to the Cloudflare network when it is activated. Cloudflare recommends leaving it deactivated until you finish [setting it up in the dashboard](#set-up-cloudflare-dashboard). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#activate-appliance
- [definition] WAN with a static IP address — After activating your device, you can use it in a network configuration with the WAN interface set to a static IP address — that is, an Internet configuration that is not automatically set by DHCP. To use your Cloudflare One Appliance on a network configuration with a static IP, follow these steps: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#wan-with-a-static-ip-address
- [definition] Bootstrap via Serial Console — Advanced users can locally configure their Cloudflare One Appliance to work in a static IP configuration. This local method does not require having access to a DHCP Internet connection. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#bootstrap-via-serial-console
- [definition] Equipment required — To access the serial port on Cloudflare One Appliance you will need the following equipment: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#equipment-required
- [definition] 1\. Access the device's serial port — 1. Using the Phillips screwdriver, loosen the screw covering the serial console panel on the back of the Cloudflare One Appliance and turn the panel out of the way. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#1-access-the-devices-serial-port
- [definition] 2\. Install a serial terminal client — To access the Cloudflare One Appliance device environment you need a serial terminal client. Follow these instructions to install one, based on your operating system. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#2-install-a-serial-terminal-client
- [definition] 3\. Configure a static IP — The `reset device` option in your Cloudflare One Appliance clears most of the configuration that is locally cached, resets the password to the default, and reboots. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#3-configure-a-static-ip
- [definition] About high availability configurations — You need to deploy two Appliances in your premises before you can set up a site in high availability. When you set up a site in high availability, the WANs and LANs in your Cloudflare One Appliance have the same configuration but are replicated on two nodes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#about-high-availability-configurations
- [definition] Create a high availability configuration — You cannot enable high availability for an existing site. To add high availability to an existing site in the Cloudflare dashboard, you need to delete the site and start again. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#create-a-high-availability-configuration
- [definition] IPsec tunnels and static routes — Cloudflare One Appliance automatically creates [IPsec tunnels](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/gre-ipsec-tunnels/#ipsec-tunnels) and [static routes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/traffic-steering/) for you. You cannot configure these manually. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#ipsec-tunnels-and-static-routes

- [definition] SFP+ port information — Last updated Apr 17, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/sfp-port-information/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/sfp-port-information/#sfp-port-information
- [definition] Port configuration — SFP+ ports are next to the regular LAN ports. They are represented as follows in the dashboard: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/sfp-port-information/#port-configuration
- [definition] SFP+ module compatibility — Cloudflare One Appliance only supports 10Gbps SFP+ modules, including RJ45, DAC, and fiber, among others. Many 1 Gbps modules are incompatible with the Intel driver used internally, and thus are not supported. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/sfp-port-information/#sfp-module-compatibility
- [definition] Recover from unsupported SFP+ inputs — SFP+ modules should be installed and tested prior to deploying Cloudflare One Appliance into production usage. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/sfp-port-information/#recover-from-unsupported-sfp-inputs

## Reference

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configura — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#on-this-page

- [definition] ICMP traffic — ICMP traffic is routed through the Internet and bypasses [Cloudflare Gateway](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/). This enables you to ping resources on the Internet from the Cloudflare One Appliance directly, which can be useful for debugging. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#icmp-traffic
- [definition] VLAN ID — This feature allows you to have multiple [virtual LANs ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/network-layer/what-is-a-lan/) (VLANs) configured over the same physical port on your Cloudflare One Appliance. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#vlan-id
- [definition] High availability — A site set up in high availability (HA) mode has two Cloudflare One Appliances with the same configuration but replicated in two nodes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#high-availability
- [definition] Active/Standby Election — During the LAN configuration, one of the LAN links is configured as a HA link, which is used to exchange heartbeats, resulting in the active / standby election of nodes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#activestandby-election
- [definition] Configuration — The two Cloudflare One Appliances of a high availability (HA) pair are part of a single site. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#configuration
- [definition] Failure detection and failover — The Cloudflare One Appliance's health can be in one of three states: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#failure-detection-and-failover
- [definition] WAN settings — This is where you add and configure your WAN connections. Each configured WAN will create one IPsec tunnel, unless you have more than one anycast IP configured in your account. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#wan-settings
- [definition] High-capacity use cases — For high-capacity use cases, multiple tunnels can be established with equal priority. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#high-capacity-use-cases
- [definition] Configure multiple tunnels in the same WAN profile — If you do not have more than one anycast IP configured in your account, and you need to configure multiple tunnels for the same WAN profile, [set up multiple WAN connections](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/configure-hardware-appliance/#create-a-wan). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#configure-multiple-tunnels-in-the-same-wan-profile
- [definition] Restrict traffic to your premises — Depending on your use case, you can define policies in your Cloudflare One Appliance to either allow traffic to flow between your LANs without it leaving your local premises or to forward it via the Cloudflare network where you can add additional security features. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/appliance/reference/#restrict-traffic-to-your-premises

- [definition] Cloudflare One Client — Some Linux distributions default to a very strict setting for [reverse path filtering ↗](https://sysctl-explorer.net/net/ipv4/rp%5Ffilter/). This strict setting attempts to drop fake traffic as a security measure. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/configuration/how-to/traceroute/#cloudflare-one-client

## Anti-replay protection
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#on-this-page
- [definition] Anti-replay protection — Last updated Aug 24, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#anti-replay-protection
- [definition] Replay attacks — Replay attacks occur when a malicious actor intercepts and records a [packet ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/network-layer/what-is-a-packet/), and later sends the recorded packet to the target network again with an intent that benefits the attacker. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#replay-attacks
- [definition] Example — Consider a poorly designed Internet of Things (IoT) garage door opener. The device has a simple protocol for operation: A User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packet contains the garage door password and either `open` or `shut` in its data segment. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#example
- [definition] IPsec anti-replay protection — IPsec anti-replay protection works similarly to the prevention example in the scenario above. The sender assigns each IPsec packet a sequence number. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#ipsec-anti-replay-protection
- [definition] Cloudflare WAN and anti-replay protection — Standard IPsec anti-replay protection assumes a single sender and a single receiver. The sender stores a sequence number in memory and increments it for every packet. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#cloudflare-wan-and-anti-replay-protection
- [definition] Additional considerations — IPsec anti-replay protection is extremely important for transport mode - host-to-host or even app-to-app IPsec. In transport mode, an attacker has a relatively easy time identifying the encrypted protocol and identifying which packets to replay if the protocol is even subject to replay attacks. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#additional-considerations
- [definition] Troubleshooting — If you're experiencing tunnel instability or packet drops related to anti-replay protection, refer to [Troubleshoot tunnel health](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/troubleshooting/tunnel-health/#ipsec-tunnel-instability-or-packet-drops). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/anti-replay-protection/#troubleshooting

## Bandwidth measurement
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/bandwidth-measurement/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/bandwidth-measurement/#on-this-page
- [definition] Bandwidth measurement — Last updated Aug 24, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/bandwidth-measurement/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/bandwidth-measurement/#bandwidth-measurement
- [definition] How bandwidth is measured — Cloudflare WAN bandwidth includes the sum of traffic routed to and from the Cloudflare WAN network namespace across all your connections. This measurement includes traffic from the following tunnel types: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/bandwidth-measurement/#how-bandwidth-is-measured
- [definition] 95th percentile calculation — The 95th percentile method is an industry-standard approach to bandwidth measurement that accounts for short traffic spikes. By discarding the highest 5% of samples, the measurement reflects your sustained bandwidth usage rather than momentary peaks. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/bandwidth-measurement/#95th-percentile-calculation

## How Cloudflare calculates tunnel health alerts
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/>

- [snippet] Error budget: number of events x (1 - SLO) = 1,000,000 x (1-0.999) = 1,000 — `number of events x (1 - SLO) = 1,000,000 x (1-0.999) = 1,000` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#error-budget
- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/clou` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#on-this-page
- [definition] How Cloudflare calculates tunnel health alerts — Last updated Aug 24, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts
- [definition] Service-level indicator (SLI) — SLI is the ratio of positive events to total events. An SLI of 0% means the feature is not working at all, and an SLI of 100% means the feature is fully working as expected. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#service-level-indicator-sli
- [definition] Service-level objectives (SLOs) — SLOs are the threshold for the SLI and set a target level of reliability for IPsec/GRE tunnels. For example, an SLO could be 99.9% of tunnel states being healthy over the past 30 days. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#service-level-objectives-slos
- [definition] Error budget — The error budget is the amount of unsuccessful events that can happen over the course of the SLO time window while maintaining the service at the level of availability the SLO defines. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#error-budget
- [definition] Burn rate — The burn rate measures how fast you expend the error budget over a given time window relative to the SLO window. In the example, an SLO of 99.9% means you can observe 1,000 tunnel health check failures over the course of 30 days. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#burn-rate
- [definition] When Cloudflare alerts you — To determine when to send Tunnel health alerts, Cloudflare relies on a multi-window, multi-burn rate approach. Every five minutes, Cloudflare analyzes the last hour and the last five minutes of data. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/how-cloudflare-calculates-tunnel-health-alerts/#when-cloudflare-alerts-you

- [definition] MTU and MSS — The [maximum transmission unit (MTU) ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/network-layer/what-is-mtu/) is a measurement representing the largest data packet that a network-connected device will accept. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#mtu-and-mss
- [definition] Encapsulation — Since Cloudflare WAN uses encapsulation to deliver its services, it is also important to understand why MTU and MSS matter in this case. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#encapsulation
- [definition] Fragmentation — If the data packet is larger than what the network interface can accept, the network must either drop or fragment it into smaller packets. - [definition] Fragmentation in Cloudflare WAN — Consider a UDP datagram of size 3,000 bytes (8 bytes for the UDP header + 2,992 bytes for the UDP data). The main takeaways are: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#how-cloudflare-handles-fragments
- [definition] MSS clamping — Maximum segment size (MSS) is a TCP setting that limits the size of TCP segments. The SYN packets set this option during the three-way handshake. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#mss-clamping
- [definition] GRE tunnels as off-ramp — The MSS value depends on how your network is set up. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#gre-tunnels-as-off-ramp
- [definition] IPsec tunnels — For IPsec tunnels, the value you need to specify depends on how your network is set up. The MSS clamping value is lower than for GRE tunnels because the physical interface sees IPsec-encrypted packets, not TCP packets, and MSS clamping does not apply to those. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/mtu-mss/#ipsec-tunnels

If you are using the Cloudflare WAN Connector, you can also steer traffic based on well-known applications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/traffic-steering/#application-aware-policies

- [parameter] Destination Address: Type=Request Style; Unidirectional health checks=Origin Tunnel Endpoint (Publicly Routable); Bidirectional health checks=Origin Interface Address (Privately Routable) / Custom Target — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#summary-table-with-tunnel-health-check-probe-types

- [definition] Tunnel health checks — Last updated Aug 24, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#tunnel-health-checks
- [definition] Types of health checks — Cloudflare WAN uses two types of health checks: — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#types-of-health-checks
- [definition] Tunnel health checks — Tunnel health checks monitor the status of the tunnels that route traffic from Cloudflare to your origin network. Cloudflare WAN relies on these checks to steer traffic to the best available routes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#tunnel-health-checks
- [definition] Endpoint health checks — Endpoint health checks evaluate connectivity from Cloudflare distributed data centers to your origin network. Unlike tunnel health checks, endpoint probes are designed to provide a broad picture of Internet health between Cloudflare and your network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#endpoint-health-checks
- [definition] Tunnel health check attributes — A tunnel health check probe has the following attributes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#tunnel-health-check-attributes
- [definition] Target — A tunnel health check probe tests whether Cloudflare can successfully connect to a specific address or endpoint through the tunnel. The target is the address you want to verify is reachable. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#target
- [definition] Direction — A tunnel health check probe can have two possible directions — unidirectional and bidirectional. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#direction
- [definition] Type — A tunnel health check probe can have two possible types: request and reply. For each type, the source and destination address depends on the direction. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#type
- [definition] Health state and prioritization — There are three tunnel health states: healthy, degraded, and down. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#health-state-and-prioritization
- [definition] Cloudflare data centers and tunnels — In the event a Cloudflare data center is down, Cloudflare's global network does not advertise your prefixes, and Cloudflare routes your packets to the next closest data center. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#cloudflare-data-centers-and-tunnels
- [definition] Recovery — Once a tunnel is in the down state, global network servers continue to emit probes according to the cadence described earlier. When a probe returns healthy, the global network server that received the healthy packet immediately sends two more probes. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#recovery
- [definition] Example — Consider two tunnels and their associated routing priorities. Remember that lower route values have priority. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#example
- [definition] Failure response — If the link between Tunnel 1 and Cloudflare becomes unusable, Cloudflare global network servers discover the failure on their next health check probe, and immediately issue two more probes (assuming the tunnel was initially healthy). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#failure-response
- [definition] Recovery response — Suppose the connectivity issue that set Tunnel 1 health to down becomes resolved. At the next health check interval, the issuing global network server receives a successful probe and immediately sends two more probes to validate tunnel health. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#recovery-response
- [definition] Troubleshooting — For help resolving tunnel health issues, refer to [Troubleshoot tunnel health](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/troubleshooting/tunnel-health/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-wan/reference/tunnel-health-checks/#troubleshooting

- [definition] Customize key storage — By default, your private keys are encrypted and securely distributed to each Cloudflare data center, where they are used for local TLS termination (the process of decrypting incoming HTTPS traffic). Geo Key Manager allows you to choose where you want to store your private keys. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/geo-key-manager/#customize-key-storage
- [definition] Cloudflare data center flow example — The following diagram shows what happens when an end user connects to a Cloudflare data center that does not hold your private key. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/geo-key-manager/#cloudflare-data-center-flow-example

## Customer Metadata Boundary
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metada — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/data` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/#on-this-page
- [definition] Customer Metadata Boundary — Last updated Jul 23, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/#customer-metadata-boundary
- [definition] Customer traffic metadata flow — The following diagram shows how metadata about your traffic is generated at a Cloudflare edge data center and forwarded exclusively to the core data center in the configured region (EU in this example). Authorized users access logs and analytics from that core data center. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/#customer-traffic-metadata-flow
- [definition] Dashboard analytics visibility — When Customer Metadata Boundary is configured, dashboard analytics and Logs views are only accessible to users whose sessions are routed to the configured region's core data center. This is determined by geo-steering, not by your physical location. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/#dashboard-analytics-visibility
- [definition] Log management — Additionally, you can configure [Logpush](https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/) (Cloudflare's log export service) to push Customer Logs to your own storage services, SIEMs (Security Information and Event Management systems), and log management providers. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/#log-management
- [definition] Product specific-behavior — For detailed information about product-specific behavior regarding Metadata Boundary, refer to the [Cloudflare product compatibility](https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/compatibility/) page. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/#product-specific-behavior

## FAQs
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/faq/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metada — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/data` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/faq/#on-this-page
- [definition] FAQs — Last updated May 5, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/faq/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/faq/#faqs
- [definition] What data is covered by the Customer Metadata Boundary? — Nearly all end user metadata is covered by the Customer Metadata Boundary. This includes all of the end user data for which Cloudflare is a processor, as defined in the [Cloudflare Privacy Policy ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/faq/#what-data-is-covered-by-the-customer-metadata-boundary
- [definition] What data is not covered by the Customer Metadata Boundary? — Some of the data for which Cloudflare is a controller, as defined in the [Cloudflare Privacy Policy ↗](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/faq/#what-data-is-not-covered-by-the-customer-metadata-boundary
- [definition] Who can use the Customer Metadata Boundary? — Currently, this is available for Enterprise customers as part of the Data Localization Suite. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/faq/#who-can-use-the-customer-metadata-boundary
- [definition] What are the analytics products available for Metadata Boundary? — HTTP and Firewall analytics are available. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/faq/#what-are-the-analytics-products-available-for-metadata-boundary

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/data` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#on-this-page

- [definition] Gateway — Regional Services can be used with Gateway in all [supported regions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/region-support/). Be aware that Regional Services only apply when using the Cloudflare One Client in Traffic and DNS mode. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#gateway
- [definition] Egress policies — Enterprise customers can purchase a [dedicated egress IP](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/egress-policies/dedicated-egress-ips/) (IPv4 and IPv6) or range of IPs geolocated to one or more Cloudflare network locations. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#egress-policies
- [definition] HTTP policies — As part of Regional Services, Cloudflare Gateway will only perform [TLS decryption](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/traffic-policies/http-policies/tls-decryption/) when using the [Cloudflare One… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#http-policies
- [definition] DNS policies — Regional Services controls where Cloudflare decrypts traffic. Because most DNS traffic is not encrypted, Gateway DNS (domain name filtering) cannot be regionalized using Regional Services. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#dns-policies
- [definition] Custom certificates — You can [bring your own certificate](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/user-side-certificates/custom-certificate/) to Gateway but these cannot yet be restricted to a specific region. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#custom-certificates
- [definition] Logs and Analytics — By default, Cloudflare will store and deliver logs from data centers across our global network. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#logs-and-analytics
- [definition] Access — To ensure that all reverse proxy requests for applications protected by Cloudflare Access will only occur in FedRAMP-compliant data centers, you should use [Regional Services](https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/regional-services/regional-hostnames/) with the region set to FedRAMP. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#access
- [definition] Cloudflare Tunnel — The [\--region parameter](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/run-parameters/#region) in `cloudflared` controls where the tunnel connector establishes its connection to Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#cloudflare-tunnel
- [definition] Local Domain Fallback — You can use the WARP setting [Local Domain Fallback](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/configure/route-traffic/local-domains/) in order to use a private DNS resolver, which you can manage yourself. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#local-domain-fallback
- [definition] Split Tunnels — [Split Tunnels](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/configure/route-traffic/split-tunnels/) allow you to decide which IP addresses/ranges and/or domains are routed through or excluded from Cloudflare. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/zero-trust/#split-tunnels

## Limitations
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/limitations/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/limita — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/data` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/limitations/#on-this-page

- [definition] Key Management — When using Geo Key Manager or Keyless SSL (a service where your private key stays on your own infrastructure), some caveats may apply. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/limitations/#key-management
- [definition] Regional Services — When using Regional Services, some caveats and limitations may apply. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/limitations/#regional-services
- [definition] Regional hostnames and Spectrum applications — Regional hostnames configured through the dashboard or the Regional Hostnames API only apply to hostnames [proxied](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/proxy-status/) through Cloudflare. They do not regionalize [Spectrum](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/) applications. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/limitations/#regional-hostnames-and-spectrum-applications
- [definition] Customer Metadata Boundary — There are certain limitations and caveats when using Customer Metadata Boundary. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/limitations/#customer-metadata-boundary
- [definition] Data unavailability — If you encounter a message on the dashboard indicating that your data is unavailable due to your account's Metadata Boundary configuration, this is because you are trying to access data that is not stored in your region (that is, you are in the US and trying to access data that is only stored in… — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/limitations/#data-unavailability
- [definition] Dashboard UI Analytics — In some cases, when using Customer Metadata Boundary set to the EU, some Dashboard UI Analytics might show up empty. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/limitations/#dashboard-ui-analytics

## FAQs
<https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/>

- [snippet] On this page: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#p — `{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"TechArticle","@id":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/data` — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#on-this-page
- [definition] FAQs — Last updated Jul 1, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/) — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#faqs
- [definition] Are DLP and DLS the same? — No, they are not. DLP stands for [Data Loss Prevention](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/data-loss-prevention/), and it is part of Cloudflare's Zero Trust offering (requiring Gateway, Cloudflare's secure web gateway for filtering outbound internet traffic). — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#are-dlp-and-dls-the-same
- [definition] Are Cloudflare's services GDPR compliant? — Yes, even without DLS, Cloudflare services are designed to satisfy the requirements of the GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation). Cloudflare services are also verified compliant with the EU Cloud Code of Conduct (EU Cloud CoC), Verification-ID: 2023LVL02SCOPE4316\. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#are-cloudflares-services-gdpr-compliant
- [definition] How can I use DLS? — Once you have purchased DLS, your account team will enable DLS on your account, and you will be able to configure all features via the dashboard or API. You can find more specific information under the [Configuration guides](https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/how-to/) section. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#how-can-i-use-dls
- [definition] Does Regional Services work with HTTP/3 / QUIC? — Not yet. HTTP/3 uses the QUIC transport protocol, which is not currently compatible with Regional Services. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#does-regional-services-work-with-http3-quic
- [definition] Can I apply Regional Services to only part of my traffic? — Yes. [Regional Services](https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/regional-services/) is not all-or-nothing. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#can-i-apply-regional-services-to-only-part-of-my-traffic
- [definition] How is traffic from users outside the configured region handled? — Regional Services accepts connections at any Cloudflare data center worldwide. When a request arrives outside the configured region, Cloudflare forwards it — still encrypted — to a data center inside the region, where TLS termination (decryption) and all Layer 7 processing take place. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#how-is-traffic-from-users-outside-the-configured-region-handled
- [definition] What is the difference between managed and custom regions? — In short, **managed regions** are predefined regions that Cloudflare maintains and are available to all accounts, while **custom regions** are tailored to your account when the managed regions do not meet your compliance requirements. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#what-is-the-difference-between-managed-and-custom-regions
- [definition] I have configured [Customer Metadata Boundary](https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/metadata-boundary/) for EU region, I am accessing the Cloudflare Dashboard from Europe, why am I getting an error `Data not available due to your account's Customer Metadata Boundary configuration`? — This is typically caused by dynamic network routing. Based on Internet conditions that vary over time, your connection may be routed to a data center that is physically outside your configured region. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/data-localization/faq/#i-have-configured-customer-metadata-boundaryhttpsdeveloperscloudflarecomdata-localizationmetadata-boundary-for-eu-region-i-am-accessing-the-cloudflare-dashboard-from-europe-why-am-i-getting-an-error-data-not-available-due-to-your-accounts-customer-metadata-boundary-configuration

- [parameter] RA: If true, it means the Recursion Available bit was set. This is always set to true for Cloudflare DNS over HTTPS. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/1.1.1.1/encryption/dns-over-https/make-api-requests/dns-json/#successful-response
- [parameter] AD: If true, it means that every record in the answer was verified with DNSSEC. — https://developers.cloudflare.com/1.1.1.1/encryption/dns-over-https/make-api-requests/dns-json/#successful-response
- [parameter] CD: If true, the client asked to disable DNSSEC validation.
